News.title: Two dead and one seriously injured after ‘hunters gunned down’ by ‘unknown assailant’ in forest in Norway
News.content:
'GUN ATTACK' Two dead and one seriously injured after ‘hunters gunned down’ by ‘unknown assailant’ in forest in Norway







Next

TWO people have been killed and a third is seriously injured after a horror shooting in Norway.

An unknown assailant reportedly opened fire on a group of at least 10 hunters, police said.

Police raced to the forest east of Halden at around 8am this morning after reports of a shooting.



Two people were confirmed dead at the scene, while one person was found seriously injured and rushed to hospital by air ambulance.



A frantic manhunt was launched to track down the shooter with drones deployed to scour the area.

Just an hour and a half later police called off the search and confirmed a suspect had been arrested.

The alleged shooter did not belong to the hunting team, police said.

“We are conducting technical investigations at the scene and will question several people”, a police statement read.

A resident near the scene told local media outlet VG that he heard several shots ring out in the forest.

He said: “I heard two shots. But I was sleeping and woke up from the shots, so there were probably more.”

The man said he initially assumed the gunshots came from a moose hunt.



Two police helicopters, an ambulance helicopter and a rescue helicopter remain at the scene.

A crisis team has been set up as authorities work to get an overview of the situation, Local Mayor Fredrik Holm told the outlet.

More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: Girl, 6, trapped in body of old woman reveals how bullies call her ‘grandma’ as desperate parents raise surgery funds
News.content:
CRUEL TAUNTS Girl, 6, trapped in body of old woman reveals how bullies call her ‘grandma’ as desperate parents raise surgery funds







Next

A SCHOOLGIRL trapped in an old woman’s body has spent years battling savage bullies who constantly call her a “grandma” for her mature looks.

Aizza Akhil, six, has a rare, genetic condition which means she has loose, sagging and wrinkled skin which makes her look old beyond her years.



The diminutive Aizza, from Wayanad in India, suffers from Cutis Laxa, an extremely rare skin condition that affects 1 in 4 million people.

Less than 500 people globally have the same incurable issue making Aizza a remarkable young girl.



Despite her condition, Aizza is just like any ordinary six-year-old girl as she loves to dance, draw and play with her friends.

Her bravery in trying to be a normal child in light of her rare condition has come at a cost, her family has said.



Relentless bullies have led to Aizza suffering at school as they tease and quiz her over why she looks so different to them.

In July, a group of older students laughed at her and called her “grandma”. Aizza remembers running away in floods of tears.



Speaking at home with her parents, Aizza told The Sun: “They call me grandma at school. They tease me saying that my skin looks like an old woman.”

Her parents are now desperately trying to raise enough cash to afford plastic surgery which could help to remove Aizza’s redundant skin.

Housewife Anjali, 27, and security guard father Akhil KC, 32, have been desperately saving up to arrange the necessary surgeries for their only child.

It was not until Aizza was six months old that her skin showed signs of Cutis Laxa.

A shocked Anjali said she looked at her daughter’s face one day and saw it had become loose and wrinkly almost overnight.



As her appearance continued to change, her parents took the baby to over a dozen doctors across the state of Kerala.

Her official diagnosis came when she was nine months old.

Anjali said: “I had a normal pregnancy. I underwent the required treatment, all the scans and ultrasounds and medicines.



“The delivery was a C-section. She was born a healthy child with regular features.

“But by the time she was six months old, we noticed her skin had changed. We could not understand the reason.

“We were told that she has a rare condition, I couldn’t even spell it properly. I had neither heard about it nor could understand what the cause was.”

The doctors warned the parents that her condition will only get worse as she ages.

Her skin would continue to lose its elasticity but also start to impact her internal organs as it would weaken her tissues and immunity.



This could lead to dangerous conditions such as pulmonary emphysema – a chronic lung disease where air sacs are damaged and destroyed, making it hard to breathe.

Aizza already struggles with a weak respiratory system and suffers from dry and itchy skin.

She takes daily medication to help with her breathing and needs regular medical care and products to keep her skin moisturised.



Her treatment costs the family up to 20,000 rupees, around £160, a month, according to her mother.

Akhil only makes the equivalent of £120-a-month, sparking serious financial concerns for the family.

The cash woes were compounded earlier this year when Aizza needed an expensive surgery.

Her first, of hopefully several, plastic surgeries was undertaken to help when the skin around her left eyebrow began to droop and cover her eye.

It cost Akhil and Anjali almost £800.



Anjali continued: “The doctors have told us to be prepared for more plastic surgeries as she grows. We need money for that.”

“We want her to have a safe and healthy life. God has given us a daughter and we want to take care of her.

“We want to provide her with everything and let her live a normal and happy life.”

As the medical challenges ramp up, Aizza has been slowly feeling more confident as her classmates get used to her looks.

Her uncle Arjun George said: “We went to the school and met her teachers.



“After that an assembly was organised and all students were informed about her condition.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Students have become softer towards her now.”

The family is hoping for donations to pursue her future treatment in order to give Aizza the best and longest life possible.

News.title: Tory boss Kemi Badenoch reveals chilling death threat from ‘ex-IRA’ thug who targeted her family
News.content:
'BULLET IN YOUR HEAD' Tory boss Kemi Badenoch reveals chilling death threat from ‘ex-IRA’ thug who targeted her family







Next

KEMI Badenoch has revealed a man claiming to be a former IRA member threatened to kill her and even targeted members of her family.

The Tory leader said the man recently pleaded guilty after sending a string of menacing messages.



She told the BBC: “He was sending messages not just to me but also to my family members.

“And I just think that whether it’s Nigel Farage or even Keir Starmer, who had his home firebombed, that there is a threat to politicians that is increasing, and we just need to crack down on this.”



Kieran Kyle admitted sending threatening emails to Mrs Badenoch after a row over a Tory social media video which mistakenly used footage of Bloody Sunday.

He claimed to be ex-IRA and warned she could be left “face down in a ditch with a bullet in her head”, while also sending racist messages to her husband Hamish.

Kyle pleaded guilty to two counts of sending indecent or offensive communications and was warned that jail was “a real option”.

He will be sentenced this month.

Mrs Badenoch said politicians could not allow threats and abuse to scare them out of public life.

She added: “Let’s build the prison spaces so that we can put people who are making these threats in and threatening politicians.



“But what I want the public to know is that my priority really is their safety.

“MPs have often been threatened in this way, but we must not let that stop us from doing our jobs.

“And we are elected to make sure that we protect national security, to look after public security, and that is my priority.”

Asked how she copes with that as a “mother” as well as a “leading politician”, she said: “It’s really tough… you just have to get on with it. You know, every person who sends an abusive message, you know, they think that they’re just getting something off their chest.

“But the cumulative impact puts a lot of people off politics. But I’m not going to be put off.”



Her warning comes just days after the man accused of murdering former Tory minister Ann Widdecombe was charged with preparing acts of terrorism, including against Reform leader Nigel Farage.

Joshua Kerry, 28, is accused of terror-related activity between May 2024 and July this year and is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.

He is also accused of murdering Ms Widdecombe, who died after being struck over the head with a hammer 21 times at her Devon home, a court has previously heard.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Reform deputy leader Richard Tice yesterday said Mr Farage had repeatedly raised fears about his security but had sometimes “not been believed” or listened to.

News.title: ‘Hijacker who stabbed pilot’ called for women to be ‘stomped on’ as online rants revealed & Al Qaeda issues warning
News.content:
Next

THE pilot accused of stabbing his captain in a suspected bid to hijack an Israel-bound plane called for violence against women while studying at a UK university.

Hamam al Hammami, 29, who was held after the alleged jihadist hijacking attempt on the FlyDubai passenger plane, said women should be “stomped on” in thousands of sick online rants.



All of the posts were published while he was studying aviation management at Buckinghamshire New University in Wycombe, Buckinghamshire.

The Omani national studied the course remotely from Muscat, Oman, according to The Telegraph.



An X account strongly linked to Al Hammami advocated for severe punishments against women justified by reference to Islamic law, homophobic abuse and sexual humiliation.

The posts were made under the name “Pilot Hamam al-Hammami” and handle @PilotHamam.



In one he replied to a woman: “I’d stomp on your head, wipe the floor with you, make you an example to others, and then divorce you :).”

In another post he called a man a “coward and a scoundrel” for failing to violently assault his wife after catching her speaking to another man.

He said: “Anyone else would have stomped on her head and made her an example to others.”

Al Hammami also detailed his mother’s struggle to find him a wife – a subject which appeared to infuriate him.



He wanted any future partner to wear a niqab, a face covering, and stop working after marriage.

“They all refused,” he complained on social media in a February 2022 post seen by CNN.

“Then my mother told them ‘My son is a pilot’ and they all suddenly agreed.”



The posts also railed against mixed-gender workplaces, saying they had a corrupting effect on women.

“How many respectable, religious girls have been ruined in mixed-gender work environments and manipulated?” a post from January 2022 said.

Al Hammami tweeted more than 2,000 vile messages between November 2021 and August 2022 – while at the UK university, The Telegraph reports.

A spokesperson for Buckinghamshire New University told The Sun: “Our thoughts are with the injured pilot, crew and passengers involved in this incident.

“Hamam al Hammami previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management. He did not undertake any pilot training at the University.”



Al Hammami was arrested on Wednesday after allegedly attacking his captain with the cockpit’s crash axe and trying to take control of a plane with 182 people aboard.

Israeli officials claim the co-pilot was trying to cause a 9/11-style tragedy after steering the Flydubai jet into a terrifying 700mph nosedive.

A Gulf diplomat said investigations are working to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or has any connection with any extremist groups”.



On Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the suspect was believed to have undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination.”

Al Qaeda has since called for copycat attacks on US and Israeli airliners.

Pro-Al Qaeda publication, al-Bayan, wrote on Friday: “The war isn’t over yet — planes carrying Zionists, Americans and all the other infidels fighting against Islam are still hovering in the skies and can be targeted, as happened on September 11th and 30th.”

The article included an image of a plane crashing into the Twin Towers on September 11, 2001, alongside an image referencing Wednesday’s attack on the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight.

Al Hammami had previously been banned from flying by Oman over fears he had adopted extremist views.



A LinkedIn profile bearing the name Hamam al-Hammami said he worked at Oman Air for seven years, leaving in February 2025, before joining Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and departing in January 2026.

Two posts were made to the profile, both published in quick succession on Wednesday – nine hours after the incident.

It is unclear who published the posts or whether they were scheduled in advance.

One included a video featuring a photo of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after the death of Osama Bin Laden.

This was followed with an image of Humam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawi, who killed nine people, including seven American CIA officers, in a 2009 suicide bombing.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The second post featured an AI-generated image depicting Islam’s three holiest sites – in Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem.

Flydubai has grounded all flights to and from Israel as investigations continue.

News.title: Map shows Britain’s ‘least safe’ university cities as freshers arrive – where does yours rank?
News.content:
FRESH HELL Map shows Britain’s ‘least safe’ university cities as freshers arrive – where does yours rank?







Next

BRITAIN’S “least safe” university towns can be revealed as students head back for freshers term, according to a study.

Leicester ranked bottom in a data, which analysed crime stats from last year’s opening weeks of term – with The Sun’s below interactive map showing the 10 lowest ranking across the UK as wild boozy nights out begin.

The data, compiled by ID Card Centre, used stats from September and October last year – they used overall crime, violent crime and antisocial behaviour from the city centre assessed relative to the number of students enrolled, which was then used to give each city a “safety score”.



The study said that the data does not show a student’s likelihood of being a victim of crime – and is merely tally of cities from least safe to most safe according to their metric.



The East Midlands city got an overall score of 9.3 – which compares to 94 for St Andrews, deemed the safest in a scale from 0-100 where 100 is the most safe.

Leicester saw 3,114 crimes recorded across the two-month period, including 915 for violence and 445 for antisocial behaviour – with 1,868 crimes per 10,000 students.

The top 10 lowest scoring also include Bradford (9.4), London (10.7), Brighton (11.1), Bristol (14.1), Wrexham (17.2), Belfast (20.3), Plymouth (21.1), Derby (21.8) and Newcastle (22).

It was London that saw the most crimes overall, with 11,186 offences during the period.

Against University College London’s enrolment, that’s 2,389 crimes per 10,000 students, almost six times Oxford’s rate and more than 23 times St Andrews’.



Conversely, the 10 safest university towns, according to the stats, as well as St Andrews (94), also include Dundee (92.1), Stirling (89.1), Derry/Londonderry (85.5), Edinburgh (83.1), Oxford (82.7), Durham (81.9), Bangor (79.6), Aberdeen (75.7) and Aberystwyth (75.5).

As a result, The Sun paid a visit to Leicester last month as freshers prepare for their first term at both the University of Leicester and De Montford University.

We heard a number of horror stories, including a carjacking and the discovery of a dead body – with female students refusing to walk home alone, and the one area many fear to go at night was revealed.



In February, Khaleed Oladip, 20, a third-year cyber security student at De Montfort University, was stabbed to death, after a dispute over money.

The offender, Harper Dennis, 19, who was in his first year at the University of Leicester, was convicted last month of manslaughter and jailed for 10 years.

Study Results in Full The "safety score" results as provided in full: St Andrews — Safety score: 94.0 Dundee — Safety score: 92.1 Stirling — Safety score: 89.1 Derry/Londonderry — Safety score: 85.5 Edinburgh — Safety score: 83.1 Oxford — Safety score: 82.7 Durham — Safety score: 81.9 Bangor — Safety score: 79.6 Aberdeen — Safety score: 75.7 Aberystwyth — Safety score: 75.5 Loughborough — Safety score: 73.7 Cambridge — Safety score: 71.6 Exeter — Safety score: 71.1 Coventry — Safety score: 68.2 Swansea — Safety score: 65.9 Lancaster — Safety score: 63.3 Chester — Safety score: 60.4 Colchester — Safety score: 59.5 Bath — Safety score: 59.5 Glasgow — Safety score: 59.3 Preston — Safety score: 55.8 Canterbury — Safety score: 51.7 Bournemouth — Safety score: 49.1 York — Safety score: 49.0 Cardiff — Safety score: 47.9 Southampton — Safety score: 44.9 Lincoln — Safety score: 43.5 Sunderland — Safety score: 43.0 Reading — Safety score: 41.8 Hull — Safety score: 40.3 Birmingham — Safety score: 40.0 Portsmouth — Safety score: 38.4 Nottingham — Safety score: 36.5 Leeds — Safety score: 34.4 Sheffield — Safety score: 33.6 Norwich — Safety score: 28.7 Liverpool — Safety score: 22.8 Newcastle — Safety score: 22.0 Derby — Safety score: 21.8 Plymouth — Safety score: 21.1 Belfast — Safety score: 20.3 Wrexham — Safety score: 17.2 Bristol — Safety score: 14.1 Brighton — Safety score: 11.1 London — Safety score: 10.7 Bradford — Safety score: 9.4 Leicester — Safety score: 9.3

It comes as Aberystwyth – King Charles’ former university town – has banned street drinking over “wild west” anti-social boozing.

Drunken young men in the university town were accused of “dominating” the centre of Aberystwyth where the King spent a term studying ahead of his investiture as Prince of Wales.

Town leaders say boozy young people are creating an “intimidating” atmosphere for visitors in parts of the seaside town which has a population 14,600 – but with more than 30 pubs in the historic town centre.



A street-drinking ban was brought into the town in West Wales for a trial – and now will be in force for the next three years.

Police have the powers to seize alcohol from people seen drinking in the open air.

Ceredigion Council brought in Public Space Protection Orders, meaning police and dedicated officers can seize booze from anyone who refuses to comply.

Ben O’Brien, Managing Director at ID Card Centre who conducted the research, said: “What this shows more than anything is how different the Freshers experience can be depending on where you go to university.



“The places at the top are mostly smaller student cities, while quite a few of the big nightlife destinations sit much further down.

“That probably isn’t a coincidence.”



A Leicestershire Police spokesperson said: “There are dedicated university officers – a beat officer and a dedicated halls of residents officer – who work closely with the universities and students across the city.

“Officers attend freshers’ events, aiming to ensure they are given appropriate safety and security advice.

“We have more officers on patrol in the city centre offering reassurance and crime in the Central Leicester NPA has fallen overall over the last two years.”

A spokesman for the Met Police said: “London is safe and getting safer each year. Neighbourhood policing is the foundation of what we do – and neighbourhood crime is down 14 per cent across the capital.

“This reduction is a reflection of a wider policing approach and the dedication and hard work of local officers, working with specialist colleagues across the Met, using cutting-edge technology, to bring more criminals to justice.



“When neighbourhood policing works, its impact reaches far beyond local crime. Strong relationships with communities help us prevent and reduce wider forms of violence.”

And a spokesman for Sussex Police said: “Each September and October, Brighton and Hove welcomes almost 40,000 new and returning students to its two universities.

“Throughout Freshers’ Week and the academic year, we work closely with our partners to keep students safe and minimise disruption to local communities.

“Our neighbourhood policing teams work closely with both universities, supported by a University Engagement Officer to address any issues proactively and provide support and advice where needed.

“Alongside this, we carry out regular patrols across the city centre and key student areas, working with partners within the nighttime economy to ensure our city remains a safe place for everyone to enjoy a night out.”



The Sun contacted Avon and Somerset Police and West Yorkshire Police for comment.

News.title: Girl, 12, shot dead & three adults injured in horror shooting over parking spot during youth football game
News.content:
DEADLY PARKING ROW Girl, 12, shot dead & three adults injured in horror shooting over parking spot during youth football game







Next

A GIRL has been shot dead following a row between two “cowards” over a parking spot at a kids’ football game.

The 12-year-old child was rushed to hospital following the horror shooting but tragically succumbed to her injuries hours later.



The horror unfolded at Leon Day Park in Maryland when a disruption erupted over a parking space, cops say.

It is understood the four victims were caught in the crossfire of the two rowing men last night.



Baltimore Police Department (BPD) Commissioner Richard Worley said: “What we know is that there was some type of argument between two cowards.

“And of course they both opened fire on each other.



“And in the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl who was probably down there watching football was shot and killed.”

Officers arrived to find the young girl and a 25-year-old woman suffering from gunshot wounds around 6:15 p.m.

The woman is reportedly in a stable condition, according to CBS.

An additional two men aged 23 and 28 were also struck and taken to the hospital and are expected to survive.



Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott also addressed the tragedy and said on X: “What happened tonight is disgusting, heartbreaking, and unacceptable.

“My thoughts and prayers are with the victims, their families, and everyone impacted by this tragedy.

“We will do everything in our power to hold those responsible accountable.”

At a news conference he added that the shooting was “one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen in my life.”

“Because that baby is just out here, at homecoming, for this youth football league, which is out here every single day, trying to keep people safe, trying to keep young men and young women on the right path, and this is their homecoming,” he said.



Charm City Buccaneers youth football league coach Mark Brown said the shooting broke out mid-game.

It comes hours after another tragedy at a sports match as an 18-year-old ploughed his gold BMW into a crowd of rugby fans in Australia.

Saturday’s early morning tragedy left a five-year-old girl in a coma and a 67-year-old man in a critical condition.

Around 1,000 Newcastle Knights rugby league team fans had gathered in Newcastle, about 200 miles north of Sydney, as the team’s coach set off.

At around 9.30am a car rammed into the mass of supporters lining the streets, hitting at least 10 people.



Emergency crews treated the injured, including a two-year-old girl, at the site before transporting 10 people to hospital.

A five-year-old girl is in an induced coma and her mother is seriously injured following a car crash.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A GoFundMe in support of the pair said: “Both mum and child now have a long road ahead of them, with ongoing surgeries, hospital stays, rehabilitation and recovery.

“Sadly, because of the severity of their injuries, mum not will be able to work for some time.”

News.title: Women’s stripped bodies piling up in Brit honeymoon hotspot gripped by serial killer fears…how ripper could strike again
News.content:
NIGHTMARE IN PARADISE Women’s stripped bodies piling up in Brit honeymoon hotspot gripped by serial killer fears…how ripper could strike again







Next

A KEEN runner, Elizabeth Moselakgomo set out for a solo jog after work – but never made it home to her eight-year-old daughter waiting for her.

When Elizabeth’s half-naked body was found days later on September 12, stunned cops revealed that they had discovered five women’s bodies in the same area this summer alone.



They would go on to find another six in just the last few weeks – as a region loved by Brit honeymooners is gripped by fears of a serial killer on the loose.

A total of 12 women’s bodies have been discovered in Ekurhuleni, the municipality next to Johannesburg, South Africa, since mid July.



Many of the victims had been stripped naked or partially naked and battered before being dumped on the side of the road, hidden in fields, or chucked in a nearby river.

Overwhelmed cops have been fumbling the investigation, increasing the likelihood that the murderer could get away with their twisted crimes – or strike again, The Sun has been told.

The bodies have been piling up around the nearby O.R. Tambo International Airport – where more than 100 direct British Airways flights land from London every year.

More than 400,000 Brit holidaymakers visited South Africa last year, with many newlyweds choosing to visit the country for a safari honeymoon.

Paul O’Sullivan is an ex-murder cop who caught the infamous Wemmer Pan Killer, a serial murderer who massacred 27 people in the southern suburbs of Johannesburg in the 90s.

O’Sullivan now investigates corrupt police officers and fraud.



He told The Sun that police have made a key mistake in their hunt for whoever is behind the 12 women’s brutal deaths – they have not released details of how the murders were carried out.

Cops have not yet confirmed a serial killer is behind the murders, but said “the similarities are sufficiently concerning” to give a public warning.

Police are probing if the cases are “linked to a serial killer”, Gauteng provincial commissioner Fred Kekana said.



Mr O’Sullivan told The Sun: “Obviously, the police have identified that there is a serial killer.

“One of the quickest ways to catch a serial killer is to publish their modus operandi.”

Police warned women not to go out alone, angering many who were already on high alert, but have not revealed details of how the suspected serial killer operated.

Mr O’Sullivan said that publishing the modus operandi, a term detectives use to describe the distinct, repeated way a criminal commits a crime, would do two key things for the case.

He explained: “It lets the killer know that you’re onto him and it also warns the public as to the sort of things that they should look out for. It’s a shocking state of affairs when you have the police warning women not to go out alone.”



Elizabeth’s body was discovered just hours after another woman’s half-naked body was found around 15 miles away.

At her funeral, which was broadcast by South Africa’s national TV news channels, her grieving daughter said: “Dearest mother, how heartbreaking that you left me.

“The day feels quiet without your voice. But your love is still here, surrounding me with love…Your beautiful daughter loves you so much.



“She misses you every day. But I know that I have gained a beautiful angel in you. Love your beautiful princess, Khumo.”

Another six women have been found in similar states since.

They include Dineo Motapane, 38, who also leaves behind a young child.

She was discovered on September 15, her battered and partly burned body found on the side of the road.

Mum Itumeleng Kekana, 32, vanished in July before her body was found bruised and partially clothed on a bridge.



Many of the other victims are yet to be identified.



Mr O’Sullivan is confident one killer is behind at least several of the deaths.

He argued: “You can’t say they’re copycat killers, because nobody knows what the modus operandi of the alleged serial killer is.”

South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world.

Between 70 and 80 people are killed in the country every day, completely overwhelming detectives.

And women are five times more likely to be killed in South Africa than the global average.



Police are overworked, with many murders left unsolved.

As few as one in every 100 murders results in a conviction, according to O’Sullivan.

Mr O’Sullivan, a former homicide detective himself, said: “Most homicide cops work alone. There’s far too many murders to have two people working on each one.



“You end up with a homicide cop carrying more than 100 or 150 murder dockets. You’re not going to be spending many minutes a week on each docket.

“So it gets closed as undetected and now you only have 149 cases, so you’re given another one. They just keep coming.”

He warned that with the bodies being found in the open, there’s more of a risk that a crime scene is disrupted.



“There are shortages of police officials in South Africa that understand proper crime scene management,” he said.

“When I went to a homicide scene, I cordoned it off. I got junior cops and I posted them at the door.”

A disturbed scene makes it much harder for cops to gather the evidence they need to nail a killer.

Tegan Snyman, from Amnesty International South Africa, told The Sun: “There’s very high distrust in the police. A lot of violence and sexual violence cases fail because of a lack of collection of evidence, procedural errors, not taking the right statements.”

“There’s distrust in South Africa in general about the competency of the police.”



But she hopes media attention will force police to chase down the killer.

Snyman said: “Because it’s now a big case, hopefully attention will be given and attention to detail and it’ll be properly done. But what about all the people that get killed all the time and it doesn’t make it to the news?”

“I hope the families get justice. But with femicide, successful prosecution is one thing, but obviously that the women are still dead.”

Juanita du Preez, CEO of the Action Society, warned that huge backlogs in forensics processing mean that even after a suspect is identified in a murder case, it can take years for the evidence to confirm their guilt.

She told The Sun: “We spend about three and a half years on average for a case until there is a conclusion. And then the criminals go to prison and they get out on parole easily.



“Then the recidivism rate is very, very high, above 90 percent so it becomes an evil, evil, evil loop.”

A huge part of the problem is a massive backlog in forensics testing.

O’ Sullivan explained: “There’s a three-and-a-half year backlog.

“What do you think that does to the criminal justice system?

“Because that person can be running around for three and a half years before any shadow is cast on him, or any evidence is revealed.”



Preez warned that these 12 alleged murders are “just the tip of the iceberg”, adding: “We will find bodies now that the light is shining on it. It’s not just recently, it’s just showing up because now they are looking for it.

“There are many more bodies that will come out because this is what we see every single day.”

With women in the affected neighbourhood terrified to leave their homes, catching the killer is a huge priority.

South African President ordered a crackdown on gender-based violence, which he said could not “be accepted as a normal part of life”.

But campaigners say he has repeated the same words before without action, making a similar speech seven years ago.



Mara Glennie, CEO of the Tears Foundation, who work with survivors of GBV, rape and sexual abuse in South Africa, told The Sun: “Similarities may warrant investigation, but we should not present the possibility of a serial killer as a confirmed fact.

“What is clear is that these murders require an urgent, thorough and coordinated response. Whether one person or several people are responsible, women have lost their lives and communities are afraid.

“We do not need confirmation of a serial killer to recognise the seriousness of this crisis.”

She added: “These deaths raise urgent questions about women’s safety in Ekurhuleni and the wider violence women face in South Africa.

“The horror should not begin only when a body is found. Threats, stalking, coercion and earlier violence must receive a serious response while there is still an opportunity to protect a life.”



“Women deserve to move through their communities safely. Their safety cannot be left entirely to the precautions they take.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Glennie added: “The measure of success cannot be how many plans we announce after people die.

“It must be how many people never become statistics in the first place.”

News.title: How ruthless cartels are building self-detonating narco subs to blast enemies & flood Europe with cocaine
News.content:
NARCO TORPEDOES How ruthless cartels are building self-detonating narco subs to blast enemies & flood Europe with cocaine







Next

DEEP in the South American jungle, cartels are building self-detonating narco subs to flood European markets with cocaine.

The world’s most vicious gangs are evolving with new tactics and technology to expand their bloodthirsty empire across the world.



And their latest project is advancing at a terrifying pace – with experts warning that the lethal unmanned vessels could be roaming European waters in just two years.

Last week, a Colombian navy report estimated cartel Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV) could cross the Atlantic and the Pacific by 2035.



But undersea defence expert Verineia Codrean told The Sun these deadly vessels will be ready for deployment much sooner – in as little as two years.

Verineia said: “We already know criminal groups have built crewless vessels using commercially available autopilots and satellite communications.

“The next steps are greater range, more reliable navigation and progressively less dependence on instructions from an operator.”

In July 2025, the Colombian navy announced it had seized the world’s first documented “autonomous semisubmersible”.



The ship, with a 1.5-tonne cargo capacity, operated with two Starlink antennas and an autopilot feature.

Two surveillance cameras were also installed: one on the bow, providing a real-time view of the craft’s trajectory and obstacles, and another inside to monitor the engine and transmission.

There were no drugs on board this time, but most notably, there was no crew.

Officials believe the uncrewed sub seized last year was on a trial run to the US or Europe.

It is understood to have been operated by Colombia‘s largest and most notorious drug trafficking group, the Gulf clan.



This was “not a warning of a future risk, but rather confirmation of a process”, the navy report said.

Given the challenges of detecting these vessels, it is possible drug-laden AUVs are already in regular operation.

Mexican cartels operating in Colombia have been quietly hiring specialised tech experts and engineers to help develop these ghost subs as far back as 2017.



Verineia is the chief strategy and partnerships officer at defence tech company Euroatlas – the makers of the world’s longest-endurance autonomous underwater vehicle, Greyshark.

She said: “A sophisticated vessel does not need every component to be designed for military use.

“The first crewless narco sub intercepted by the Colombian Navy used civilian technology.

“Marine engines, batteries, navigation systems, communications equipment and composite materials are all available on the civilian market.”

AI has drastically lowered the cost of systems that, a decade ago, were exclusive to the military.



Verineia said: “Criminal groups are not trying to build a military submarine capable of performing multiple missions over decades of service.

“They need a vessel that can transport a high-value cargo from A to B with a sufficiently low probability of detection.

“Portugal is particularly relevant. The Colombian navy has estimated the first AUV-1G Atlantic crossing will deliver its cargo near the Portuguese coast.”



It comes as Colombia – the world’s leading cocaine producer – faces record-high production of the drug, fuelled by surging global demand.

The country’s estimated coca leaf cultivation increased from 204,000 to 253,000 hectares – 504,000 to 625,000 acres – in 2023, according to the United Nations.

The Colombian navy said that in the first half of 2025, 10 narco subs were detected in different regions of the continent.

All had been adapted to make them difficult to track by radar – and even mobilise with partial autonomy.

The navy has warned that autonomous technologies are “an emerging threat that is transforming the transnational criminal landscape”.



By eliminating the crew, AUVs free up more space for cargo and remove the risk of human capture, extradition, and informing.

They scale cheaply, and challenge detection systems built for a world where someone was always on board.

Verineia said: “The fundamental problem is persistence. These vessels are deliberately designed to minimise their visual, radar and electromagnetic signatures, while operating across enormous maritime areas.



“Detecting something once is difficult, maintaining sufficient surveillance to find, classify and then track a low-signature vessel over a long route is much harder.”

At the same time, interception also becomes more dangerous.

The Colombian navy said submarines could be fitted with explosive cargo and remotely activated self-destruction systems.

To combat the risk, security forces have suggested using unmanned assets themselves during initial contact with an unknown AUV.

“That keeps sailors and coastguard personnel away from the vessel until the threat is better understood,” Verineia said.



While most cocaine is still smuggled on container ships, narco subs are playing a growing role especially for long-haul routes.

The Colombian navy predicts cartels could programme these vessels with a destination and mission, using AI to analyse patrol patterns, detect threats, and choose the safest route without human input.

An estimated 25 million people use cocaine worldwide, according to the United Nations, and around 22 per cent of them are in Europe.

Cocaine production has reached an all-time high to meet the growing demand.

Since 2024 the drug has overtaken oil as Colombia’s single biggest export making the country responsible for about 70 per cent of what’s sold across the globe.



It is also the main hub of illicit naval engineering for long-range ocean missions, the Navy said.

And a history of bloody civil war has spawned armed militias which are now keen to facilitate a drugs trade worth some $15billion.

Colombia is well positioned to profit from cocaine – sharing land borders with five countries, and with maritime access to the Pacific, Atlantic and Caribbean.

And its cartels have begun to form alliances with neighbouring drug lords to smuggle it across the Atlantic.

The Colombian cartels supply the drugs and naval construction while the Mexicans provide financing and delivery logistics into Europe.



A report published by Europol earlier this year confirmed that cocaine trafficking into Europe continues to expand and diversify.

Governments around the world are now recalibrating their playbooks to meet this shifting threat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In October 2025, the Pentagon announced an expanded Caribbean counter-narcotics task force.

The team included AI-enhanced ISR feeds, drones, and naval assets to anticipate unmanned maritime traffic patterns.

News.title: Burnham scraps controversial plans to curb jury trials
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has scrapped controversial plans to curb some jury trials.

Sir Keir Starmer's government had introduced proposals to allow judges to make the sole decision on cases that would lead to a sentence of less than three years.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said only complex fraud and financial offences would be judge-alone - and it proposes that thousands of medium-level crimes should stay with volunteer magistrates, who sit without a jury.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris said he had changed course after hearing the "strength of feeling" about the original proposals.

Criminal lawyers have welcomed the decision and the Conservatives say it is a "major victory" for those who fought to defend trial by jury.

Former Justice Secretary David Lammy first announced the plans in December following a recommendation in a major review of the court system in England and Wales.

The series of radical reforms, including scaling back jury trials, were presented as the best way of turning around record backlogs which, in turn, were exacerbating the prison population crisis.

The backlog - which has led to record delays for defendants and victims - currently stands at nearly 81,000 cases - having rocketed largely thanks to cuts before the pandemic and court closures during the national lockdowns. Official projections have estimated it could reach 100,000 before the next general election and, in a worst case scenario, climb to double that number by 2035.

There are, however, indications the backlog is now stabilising after the government committed unlimited funding to pay for more judges to sit in courts that were otherwise being unused.

Under the original plans, Lammy had wanted to reserve jury trials for the most serious "indictable" offences - meaning cases that are always sent to Crown Court, including murder and rape.

Less serious offences, where the sentence would be no more than three years, would be decided without a jury in the Crown Court by a judge alone. Even less serious offences would stay in magistrates' courts, abolishing defendants' right to ask for a trial by jury when they feel that is their best chance of being cleared.

The proposals triggered an outcry across many parts of the criminal justice world, with many opponents saying that eroding the 800-year-old right to trial by jury would not solve the backlogs.

News.title: Bellingham unlocks new level and potential to be 'one of the greatest'
News.content:
Just a year ago, Jude Bellingham's place in the England squad was up in the air. Now he is being talked about as having the potential to be one of football's "greatest of all time".

The Real Madrid man was left out of Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions squad in October 2025 and his place at the World Cup was called into question, with the German head coach saying Bellingham wouldn't get star treatment.

But Bellingham did of course make the squad for the World Cup and was arguably his team's standout performer, finishing as England's top scorer with seven goals as they reached the semi-finals and finished third.

He has already shown that he is world class with starring performances for club and country, but the way he helped England to dismantle Croatia 7-0 in the Nations League on Saturday looked like someone perhaps reaching a new level.

The 23-year-old was instrumental in Rijeka, scoring as well as registering a hat-trick of assists. He even ended the match wearing the captain's armband as England inflicted the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history.

"Bellingham can go on to be one of the greatest players of all time," former Manchester United and Republic of Ireland midfielder Roy Keane said on ITV after the game.

"At this moment in time, he is an amazing footballer. The package â his running power, his delivery, his goal threat. The way he is progressing as a player, I still think there is a lot more to come from him."

Bellingham, recently voted England's player of the year for the second year in a row, is now "nailed on as the 10" for the future, former England defender Matt Upson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Keane added: "He has been fantastic in possession, but what he does out of possession lifts all these other players.

"If you have a player that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and he's playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball... that will just inspire other players. He is a huge leader for them."

News.title: The Celebrity Traitors connections that might surprise you
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the first two episodes of The Celebrity Traitors

"I know Rob very, very well. I mean, I've sat next to him as he's had a colonic."

That was Romesh Ranganathan, reminding us - in case we were in any doubt - of his close friendship with Rob Beckett in the opening episode of The Celebrity Traitors.

His words sum up the key difference between this series and the regular civilian version. In Celebrity Traitors, the players aren't just on-screen competitors - many actually know each other outside the show.

Lots have worked together, and some are even friends. And those previous connections can have a huge impact on the show's dynamics.

It's also partly why it is quite so delightful to watch - as friendships unravel, and former co-stars turn on each other.

We've been unpicking the six degrees of separation. Here are some of the connections we've found - if you spot any more, we'd love to know. Get in touch with your thoughts in the comments section below.

News.title: Gentle parenting, helicopter or snowplough – is there really a best way to be a parent?
News.content:
Before Rosie Whitfield became a mum, she imagined herself parenting very calm children.

"Then I had two wild boys," she says with a laugh.

Following the birth of her kids, Rosie spent hours online looking for the best advice and was drawn to one particular approach to parenting: Gentle parenting, which focuses on empathy and mutual respect with little emphasis on punishment, albeit with boundaries.

But she constantly worried her choices, from sleep schedules to handling toddler tantrums, were "ruining their lives forever".

Rosie does not blame the gentle parenting philosophy itself but instead says the overall amount of parenting advice online was "overwhelming" and "made mundane parenting choices feel like the absolute end of the world."

"I felt like if I was choosing to put the TV on for 20 minutes while I did the dishes or had a coffee, I was choosing to destroy my children's brains," says Rosie, who is originally from Birmingham and now lives in Dubai.

Rosie believes her confidence and intuition were stripped away as she questioned every parenting decision. And she is not alone.

Government research suggests that around two-thirds of parents with young children feel overwhelmed by the amount of parenting information available and struggle with conflicting advice, with many turning to social media for support.

News.title: Why Canada is preparing for a (long shot) US invasion
News.content:
Even if a US invasion is extremely unlikely, Matthew Schmidt, an associate professor of national security at the University of New Haven in Connecticut, said the fact that Canadians were preparing was a sign of just how drastically the global order has shifted.

He added Canadian leaders do have hard questions to ask about how closely they want to continue working with the American military - a partnership that gives them valuable information should they want to harm Canada in any way.

"It's really doing harm to relationships with the United States, and there's a certain amount of legitimate fear," he said.

Americans might not take Trump's comments about making Canada the 51st state seriously, he said, but Canadians clearly do - and are prepared to defend themselves if needed.

So what would it be like if it happened?

The first phase of a war could be quite short.

According to the model used by the Canadian military, as reported on by the Globe and Mail newspaper earlier this year, a US attack would see Canada's strategic positions overwhelmed within a week

Its military would quickly be outnumbered, forcing Canadian forces to resort to guerilla-type warfare to try to suppress their enemy.

Allied nations like France and Britain would be called on to provide support and defence for Canada, the newspaper reported in January, citing senior government officials.

The theoretical model is believed to be the first time in a century that Canada planned for an American assault.

The modelling is on the lighter end of military combat planning, Coates said.

He said that Canada, unlike its Nato allies, was lagging behind when it came to having a response plan in place in the event of any ground invasion, and that it was now playing catch-up in this era of unpredictable geopolitics.

Part of that, he said, was made evident by a recent call by Canada's defence chief to drastically increase the size of its military, including the addition of as many as 300,000 lightly trained citizen soldiers.

An invasion of Canada might not be straightforward from the US point of view either.

Even with its outsized military, the US would have a difficult time getting buy-in for a fight with Canada, said Schmidt.

"I think you would have a large number of American officers who would resign if given the order to invade Canada," he said.

"They would see it as an illegal and immoral order."

Schmidt said Canadian soldiers and American soldiers routinely train together, and share a mutual respect.

But in the unlikely scenario that relations would deteriorate to the point of combat, Schmidt said the US would likely focus on acquiring valuable Canadian resources like oil and minerals, and political decapitation.

"You would see a a kind of operation that would mirror perhaps what you saw in Venezuela," he said, referring to US military action earlier this year to capture former Venezuelan President Maduro.

Although he acknowledged the US has greater military capacity, he said that "pound for pound" Canadian soldiers would be able to put up a fight.

News.title: The Papers: 'Another tax bombshell?' and 'Terror plot targets'
News.content:
The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a flight travelling to Israel had previously advocated for violence against women while studying remotely at a UK university, according to the Sunday Telegraph., external, During his time with Buckinghamshire New University, Hamam al-Hammami allegedly said women should be "stomped on" and slapped. The university had its licence to sponsor international students suspended on the day of the attack. Both the Home Office and the institution said the incidents were unrelated.

The Sunday Mirror leads on the court appearance, external of two Iranian men charged with plotting terror attacks on the Jewish community in Manchester. Its front page features pictures of the alleged targets, which include a synagogue and museum.

The Sunday Times says a leaked document, external suggests Russia has introduced strict rules on fighting-aged men, to get them to 

The Mail on Sunday focuses on Home Office figures showing taxpayers have funded more than 1,000 free hijabs, external this year for migrants arriving in the UK illegally. A Home Office spokesman told the paper it had a legal duty to provide basic clothing, including cultural and religious items.

The Sun on Sunday leads on comments by the footballer Andy Carroll, external, who says he was sexually assaulted by a former cast member of the BBC show, Fame Academy. The dance coach, Kevin Adams, was convicted in 2023 and jailed for 20 months. The paper's front page features images of the two men.

A report in the Sunday Telegraph says a church in Hampshire is appealing for the public's help in decoding a recently-discovered labyrinth, external. The single, winding path designed for walking meditation and prayer was hidden by an altar table at St Mary's Church in Itchen Stoke. A member of the Churches Conservation Trust is quoted as saying it feels like being in the Da Vinci Code.

And turkey is off the menu, external for Christmas lunch at the King's Highgrove Estate, according to the Sunday Express. It says the traditional bird will be replaced by chicken for the festive lunches, with all proceeds going to charity. Brussels sprouts also no longer feature, in an attempt to cut costs.

News.title: Tories pledge to remove £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge'
News.content:
The Conservatives have promised to scrap the "absurd cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than Â£100,000 a year.

Under the current system, only families where no parent earns more than this threshold are eligible for government-funded or tax-free childcare.

"What we want to see is that people who work harder don't get punished for doing so," Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme.

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.

The party said the move would be a "first step" in broader efforts to address issues in the tax system which damage incentives to work or invest.

This will be a theme of shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith's conference speech on Monday.

Since September 2025, working parents in England have been entitled to 30 hours of free childcare, external for children aged between nine months and four years old.

However, to qualify both parents must earn less than Â£100,000 a year, although all three and four-year-olds are eligible for 15 hours of free childcare, regardless of parental income.

The same Â£100,000 threshold, which was set by the Conservative government, applies to the government's tax-free childcare scheme, external.

For every Â£8 paid into an online childcare account, the government adds Â£2, up to Â£2,000 per child per year, which parents can then use to pay for childcare.

The Tories said that if they return to power they would remove the Â£100,000 threshold entirely so parents no longer lose childcare support when their income exceeds this level.

The threshold has been criticised by economists, who point out it can leave parents worse off overall even after a pay rise of tens of thousands of pounds.

Badenoch told the BBC the party didn't want "people to stop working because of that".

Speaking before the party's conference, she added: "What we want to see is more people in work and not taking the wrong decisions or the wrong choices, and it doesn't matter whether they're earning Â£10,000 or Â£100,000 - what matters is that people are out there working".

Asked if this could result in someone who earns Â£1 million a year get free childcare under a Conservative government, Badenoch responded: "It doesn't matter what you earn - we don't want you to be punished for working hard. What we're trying to do is grow our economy."

News.title: Autumn chill to arrive this week as temperatures set to drop
News.content:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK during the week ahead, bringing an end to a run of warmer-than-average autumn weather.

By Wednesday, afternoon highs are expected to range from 11C (52F) in northern Scotland to 17C (63C) in southern England.

It will mark a significant change from the summer-like warmth that has brought temperatures of up to 28C over the last week.

If the thermometer fails to reach 20C anywhere in the UK, it will be the first time that has happened since 11 June.

News.title: Debris in engine very likely caused Spitfire crash
News.content:
Debris which had been present in the carburettor of a Spitfire for decades was "very likely" the cause of a crash in which a pilot died, according to a report.

Sqn Ldr Mark Long was killed when the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) plane he was flying crashed in a field in Lincolnshire on 25 May 2024.

A report published by the Ministry of Defence says the debris was responsible for causing fuel starvation, "leading to a loss of thrust required to maintain powered flight".

Just 56 seconds after taking off from RAF Coningsby, witnesses saw the plane turn and plunge to the ground.

Long was flying a Spitfire Mk IX, built in 1944, operated by the RAF's BBMF for commemorative flypasts and displays.

The opening of an inquest heard the provisional cause of his death was head and neck injuries.

The Service Inquiry report, external said chemical analysis revealed evidence that indicated the debris in the carburettor "had been present for decades".

It said: "The presence of multiple, contradictory publications created ambiguity over the correct procedures for carburettor maintenance.

"The panel assessed that this inconsistency likely led to varying interpretations of how extensively the carburettor should have been dismantled, inspected and cleaned, which was very likely to have reduced the reliability of detecting any debris build-up."

The design of the cockpit and restraint were identified as aggravating factors, but the report acknowledged any structural design change would likely require "significant moderations".

"This would not only affect the historic authenticity of the aircraft but would possibly affect overall airworthiness due to a change in aircraft mass and balance," the report said.

Twenty-six safety recommendations were included in the report, including improved maintenance records, reviews of cockpit protection and better training for emergencies.

The report described the recommendations as "robust" and said they "should minimise the likelihood of a recurrence or similar tragedy".

News.title: University asks staff to review some partnerships with China after MI5 warning
News.content:
Queen's University of Belfast (QUB) has asked staff to review some partnerships with China after a warning from MI5.

In a highly unusual move, the UK's internal security service had warned universities they may have unintentionally assisted China's espionage.

MI5 said the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) was a front company working for China's intelligence and security service.

However, a spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in London said the accusation was "imaginary and purely fabricated".

Staff at Queen's have now been "strongly advised to review any existing or proposed collaborations involving CGTRI".

"Work is ongoing within Queen's to do this," an email to staff said.

"However, this may not be obvious through our existing systems and so researchers are also advised to undertake appropriate due diligence to identify the ultimate source of funding for collaborations with Chinese institutions."

MI5 issued the alert for UK universities about CGTRI which it said had "very strong ties" to the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS).

Universities in the UK often collaborate and partner with universities elsewhere in the world to share research and expertise.

But MI5 said it had identified more than 100 UK-linked academics who had contributed to projects funded by Ministry of State Security via CGTRI.

It said that in some cases the researchers would not be aware of the front company's role in their project.

UK academics have contributed to CGTRI-funded projects on topics including AI, cyber-security, covert communications systems and steganography, which means hiding a secret message or file inside an ordinary message or object.

MI5 added that academics who failed to cut ties with CGTRI could ultimately face criminal charges for aiding a foreign state.

As a result, UK universities were advised to immediately review the funding of any research collaboration with China.

A QUB spokesperson told BBC News NI that the university takes "responsibilities around research and national security extremely seriously".

"Queen's University has commenced a review around any existing or proposed collaborations involving CGTRI," they said.

"We have also contacted staff requesting they review any existing or proposed collaborations with them and report any concerns to the relevant Faculty Dean of Research.

"We will keep this situation under review while continuing to support our collaboration, research and innovation projects locally, nationally and internationally."

According to its website, QUB has invested over $10m (Â£7.56m) in China-related research in areas like sustainable energy, information technology, food security and cancer research over the past decade.

Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Ulster University said they had no research links with the organisation referenced by MI5.

News.title: Man rescued after car crashes into house
News.content:
A man had to be rescued by firefighters from a house that partially collapsed after a car crashed into it.

Police officers, paramedics and firefighters were called to the property on Ninefields, in Waltham Abbey, Essex shortly before 23:00 BST on Friday.

Upon arrival, they found a silver Skoda, which had smoke coming out of it, that had smashed into the corner of a house, leaving it badly damaged.

Essex Police said a man was arrested on suspicion of being unfit through drink or drugs and taken to hospital for treatment.

Another man was safely removed from the rear of the property by fire crew using a ladder, while a woman was also taken to hospital for a "precautionary assessment."

News.title: Bees create a buzz at Liverpool shopping centre
News.content:
A Liverpool shopping centre's lesser known tenants are creating a buzz.

St Johns Shopping Centre has thousands of bees in hidden hives on the roof and some of the staff have even had beekeeper training.

Two hives were installed in 2021 and a third was set up last year. During summer peaks the hives become home to about 180,000 of the striped insects.

They produced a bumper amount of honey this year - enough for 150 jars of the sweet nectar - and local school children are helping design the labels.

The project was developed by St Johns and NG Bailey, who provide maintenance support to the site, after they wanted to do something for the environment.

Two hives were initially installed and staff were recruited to train as beekeepers. A third hive was added last year, with five members of staff now trained to look after them.

Kieron Jones, maintenance supervisor, told BBC Radio Merseyside: "I never thought it would be part of my maintenance routine to look after beehives.

"When it was suggested, it piqued our interest and we thought this is another skill set we can get, and it lets us give something back, so it was really good."

The hives are positioned on the roof of the shopping centre, in the shadow of the famous St Johns Beacon.

News.title: Train station returning to village after more than 100 years
News.content:
Work is beginning on bringing a train station back to the heart of a Greater Manchester village more than a century after its original station closed.

Cheadle in Stockport had a station just off the high street up until 1917.

Funding for a new hub, which would be built next to Alexandra Hospital, was given the green light in 2022, with planning permission granted in 2023 but concerns about its effect on the timetabling of trains elsewhere on the network led to delays.

Stockport Council said the issue had now been resolved and council leader Mark Roberts said it was "a hugely significant moment for Cheadle and for Stockport".

"For years we've fought for this station because we know the difference it will make to residents, businesses and the future prosperity of the area," he added.

Roberts said he was delighted that the initial highways work could now start on site thanks to the persistence and partnership of all involved.

Services are expected to run from Cheadle into Stockport town, Manchester Piccadilly and Chester, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

The project had been held up by an unresolved timetabling issue over concerns the new station could impact trains elsewhere on the network, with a previous proposal made to remove services at Ashley and Plumley.

Stockport Council said the latest assessment by Network Rail and Northern Trains concluded that Cheadle Station could be introduced without removing a significant barrier that had put the project at risk and these plans have now been dropped.

News.title: Youth charged after shopping centre attack leaves teenager in hospital
News.content:
A teenager has been charged after an attack involving a groups of youths inside a Glasgow shopping centre left another teenager needing hospital treatment.

Video posted on social media shows a young man, who was using a crutch and wearing a medical boot, being knocked to the ground, then repeatedly punched and kicked inside the St Enoch Centre on Friday afternoon.

A second person was also pushed to the ground during the disturbance but security staff intervened.

Police Scotland said a 19-year-old was taken to hospital and a 17-year-old boy was later arrested and charged following investigations.

The attackers had run off by the time officers arrived and the injured man, who was bleeding from a head wound, was initially helped by shoppers and security staff.

News.title: Man shot dead as families gather for memorial
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people â including children â gathered for a memorial service in west London.

The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.

No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.

Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence.

"We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated.

"We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."

He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw".

He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?

"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media.

"However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."

News.title: Huge crowds turn out in support of residents over Drumcree parade dispute
News.content:
Rallies were held on both sides of the Drumcree parade dispute on Saturday as the stand-off between Garvaghy Road residents and the Portadown District Orange Lodge continues.

Addressing thousands of people at an event on the Garvaghy Road, First Minister and Sinn FÃ©in vice president Michelle O'Neill said she heard the Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant "talk about being between a rock and a hard place", adding she has "never heard such nonsense, this is between right and wrong".

The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) said anyone blocking the Garvaghy Road will be "treated as participating in an unnotified and therefore illegal protest and that anyone "found to have broken the law will face criminal justice consequences".

Speaking at Drumcree church, Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) MP Carla Lockhart repeated calls for PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher and his officers to "do their job" and facilitate the parade, describing the current impasse as "mob rule".

For most of the afternoon stewards in high visibility jackets kept people off the Garvaghy Road and those attending were told it was important to allow traffic to flow freely.

However, by 15:00 BST the crowd was so large that they were standing on the road as police closed it to traffic.

The fallout over the proposed Portadown District Orange Lodge march - which is opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since Sunday morning after the Parades Commission's decision that the parade could go ahead with restrictions.

News.title: Alison Hammond shares update from hospital bed after being rushed from This Morning mid-show with heart issues
News.content:

Alison Hammond has shared an update from her hospital bed after being taken ill during a live broadcast of This Morning.

The presenter, 51, rushed to seek medical attention on Friday, 2 October after experiencing alarming heart palpitations while on camera.

Addressing the scare she told fans on social media: "I know you're all worried about me. Honestly, I am fine, first of all.

“I'm getting me old ticker checked out. I had a little bit of a palpitation, and now I'm getting it all checked out, but I think I'm okay.

“I'm hoping it was just a little panic attack or something like that.”

Co-host Dermot O'Leary, 53, announced Hammond had to leave the broadcast when the show came back from an advert break.

“Welcome back to This Morning. Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she’s just had to duck out,” he announced.

open image in gallery Hammond was forced to leave the programme after troubling heart palpitations ( ITV )

The programme had begun with Hammond and O'Leary at the helm, and her departure came after a segment about pets.

The star was last seen clutching her chest in the edge of a frame, before she was helped away from the sofa by O’Leary.

Hammond apologised to viewers for leaving mid-broadcast, saying that she would normally never leave a TV show, before joking: “Look how good I look! Still got my make-up on from This Morning. Lush.”

open image in gallery Dermot O'Leary announced that Hammond had left the show and wouldn’t be returning ( This Morning/ITV )

Five years ago, Hammond shared she was embarking on a health kick after discovering she was pre-diabetic.

Since then, the TV personality has taken up Reformer Pilates and boxing. She has also shared that she cut out sweets and fatty foods.

Hammond, 51, rose to fame in 2002 when she appeared as a contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother.

She has since appeared on programmes including I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! and Strictly Come Dancing.

The star first appeared on This Morning in 2003 and became a co-host in 2021.

She is known for memorable TV moments and celebrity interviews such as playing Connect 4 with pop star Beyonce.

Hammond also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off with comedian Noel Fielding, which recently started airing its latest season with new judge Nigella Lawson.

( Reuters )

Formula 1 returns to a fan-favourite circuit this weekend as the Sepang circuit in Malaysia hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix in a one-off event.

George Russell got his season back on track with a first victory in three months at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix last time out, pipping Max Verstappen to the line to narrow the deficit on championship leader and Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli to 66 points.

Antonelli, who crashed out of qualifying, recovered from the back of the grid to finish fifth while Isack Hadjar joined Verstappen on the podium on a positive day for Red Bull. However, it was a tricky day for McLaren and Ferrari, who both struggled for form and pace.

As for this weekend, Bahrain’s original grand prix date in April was cancelled due to the war in the Middle East. The Gulf country have, however, opted to pay the hosting fees to have their name attached to Sepang’s return to the calendar for the first time in nine years this weekend.

Follow live updates for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with The Independent

Temperatures across the UK are set to drop in the coming week with cooler air and outbreaks of rain, after one of the warmest Septembers on record.

Temperatures hit a maximum of 28C on 29 September, while the average temperature for the month was 14.6C, making it the joint-fourth warmest since records began in 1884, according to provisional figures by the Met Office.

The warmer start to Autumn also followed the hottest British summer on record. But that is now set to change as milder weather comes in this week.

Sunday will see cloudy weather across much of Scotland and Northern Ireland with outbreaks of rain turning “heavy and persistent” across western Scotland, according to the Met Office’s forecast.

open image in gallery Wednesday’s forecast, with rain expected to move across the UK this week as colder weather comes in ( Met Office )

Heavy rain in western Scotland is expected to be accompanied by gusts of wind of up to 40mph far in northwestern areas of the country.

The rest of the UK will be dry and warm with sunshine across southern England once lingering fog clears between mid-to late morning on Sunday.

Early mist and fog will affect south Wales, the Midlands and East Anglia where it is expected to persist for longer.

As the day progresses the rain and brisk winds seen across Scotland and Northern Ireland will sink southwards reaching the north of England and Wales.

Clouds will develop in northern regions of Wales and England, with a chance of rain in some areas.

open image in gallery Temperatures on Sunday will start to drop with several areas experiencing cooler weather throughout the week ( Met Office )

open image in gallery Temperatures across the country on Wednesday are expected to be much cooler than September ( Met Office )

There are expected to be clear spells elsewhere with more fog forming by dawn on Sunday.

Temperatures are still expected to be higher than usual for the season, possibly reaching 23C in southern England. But if temperatures don’t reach 20C across the UK, it will be the first time since 11 June.

A weather front is then expected to move “erratically” southwards between Monday and Wednesday, according to the BBC, bringing outbreaks of rain and the possibility of thunder and lightning in southern England on Tuesday and Wednesday night. Chilly nights and some frost could be experienced in the most affected locations.

open image in gallery Cloud cover across the UK on Monday morning ( Met Office )

There will be more sunny spells and dry weather in the south and east once the ongoing foggy weather clears on Monday.

Elsewhere, it is expected to be cloudy with patchy rain, which is heaviest and most persistent on the northwestern upslopes.

The rain will move southeastwards between Tuesday and Wednesday with potentially heavy downpours in the southeast.

On Thursday, the weather is expected to be dry and bright for most areas, with it feeling initially warm and then turning colder for all areas.

Forecast for the next five days

Today

Cloudy weather and outbreaks of rain across much of Scotland and Northern Island, turning “heavy and persistent” across western Scotland, according to the Met Office.

Elsewhere, the weather will be dry with sunshine and warmth across the south once fog clears between mid to late morning.

Tonight

Brisk winds, outbreaks of rain and cloud affecting Scotland and Northern Ireland will sink southwards into northern England and Wales. Clear spells will be seen elsewhere with fog forming by dawn.

Monday

Areas of the south and east will see dry weather with sunny spells once fog clears, while elsewhere there will be cloudy weather and patchy rain. Rain will be heaviest and most persistent on northwestern upslopes.

Outlook for Tuesday to Thursday

The southeast of England will face potentially heavy rain through Tuesday and Wednesday as rain moves in that direction. Most areas will be dry and bright on Thursday with it feeling warmer initially before dropping to cooler temperatures.

Celebrity Traitors alum Celia Imrie has revealed that she warned 2026 contestant Richard E Grant that it would be hard to keep his “brain working” at all hours while filming the deceptive game show.

Grant, 69, stumbled at the first hurdle and threw the celebrity edition of the much-loved BBC show into disarray during it’s first episode by revealing his secret identity as a traitor to his fellow contestants.

Imrie, who placed seventh in the inaugural A-list version of the series told the Saltburn star ahead of his time in the show’s Scottish castle that the game is “very strict” and “it’s hard always being on”. A fact he soon forgot.

“[He] rang me up and asked what it was like. I said I didn’t quite know what I was letting myself in for,” Imrie told The Times.

“But it was good fun, although it’s very strict and there is an element of cruelty about the game,” she added of the show’s foundation in betrayal.

open image in gallery Imrie placed seventh in the inaugral A-list version of the BBC series and warned Grant the programme was “very strict” ( Getty )

It comes after Grant’s fellow contestant, former BBC presenter Amol Rajan, shared that the lauded actor told him he “just went mad”.

Rajan, who was the first celebrity to be killed off by Grant and his fellow traitor Maya Jama, wrote in his newsletter that he asked the actor why he chose to eliminate him from the show.

“To protect myself,” Grant was quoted as having replied. “And that’s a compliment!”

Rajan replied: “But if you really wanted protection, you should have recruited me. That would have been a compliment!”

“Ah yes, that makes sense,” Grant said. “But I think I just went mad.”

open image in gallery Grant threw the BBC show into disarray after revealing his secret identity as a traitor to his fellow contestants ( BBC )

Meanwhile, the show’s host Claudia Winkleman attributed Grant’s blunder to sheer “giddiness” over the fact he’d been selected as a traitor.

“He was just so happy. He just couldn’t believe it,” the host said.

“The genius of the game is everybody plays it completely differently, and he took that to the next level.”

Grant, Jama, and their newly recruited traitor, comedian James Acaster, must now work to kill off the remaining 17 faithfuls without detection.

Celebrity Traitors will return on Thursday at 8pm on BBC One.
