Nearly 1,500 Myanmar nationals who were sent back from Malaysia arrived in the country’s largest city on Sunday, despite warnings from the United Nations refugee agency and rights groups that conditions for return remain unsafe.

Myanmar has been in turmoil since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi on Feb. 1, 2021, triggering widespread opposition and plunging large parts of the country into conflict.

The returnees, including 86 women, have been convicted of staying illegally and other immigration violations in Malaysia, according to reports from Myanmar state media. They were transported from Malaysia aboard two navy warships and a hospital ship last Tuesday. They arrived in southern Yangon early Sunday, Nay Lin Tun, a regional government minister, said.

The returnees are among 5,000 Myanmar nationals who will be repatriated in stages from Malaysia, where 10,388 others were being held at immigration detention centers, according to Malaysia’s Home Ministry.

The U.N. high commissioner for refugees and rights groups have criticized the repatriation, saying the security and humanitarian situation in parts of Myanmar remains volatile and returnees could face persecution and forced military conscription in an active war zone.

“Under international law, the Government of Malaysia is obligated to uphold the principle of non-refoulement and prevent the return of individuals to situations where they face a real risk of persecution, torture, or other serious human rights violations,” Kelley E. Currie, the U.N. special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Myanmar, said in a statement on Thursday. “In my assessment, the risk of refoulement in the present circumstances is substantial.”

It was unclear if any of the returnees included minority Muslim Rohingya, who are facing persecution in Myanmar and have been denied citizenship.

Myanmar Foreign Ministry official Han Win Aung told The Associated Press that the repatriation involved “genuine citizens.”

Malaysia is home to about 215,600 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UNHCR, including about 126,000 Rohingya who make up one of Southeast Asia’s largest refugee communities. Despite hosting them, Malaysia is not a party to the U.N. Refugee Convention and treats refugees as undocumented migrants.

Min Aung Hlaing, the leader of Myanmar’s military-backed government who was sworn in as president in April, is expected to visit Malaysia this month to discuss the refugee and migrant issues.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has arrived in Kyiv on Sunday to demonstrate support as Russia steps up strikes on Ukrainian cities.

Aerial warfare has intensified further, with Moscow targeting cities across Ukraine using difficult-to-intercept ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, while Kyiv has launched strikes against Russian commercial interests and oil infrastructure.

Merz said his trip to Kyiv, his second as chancellor, was intended to underscore Germany’s ongoing commitment to Ukraine.

"If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," he said in a statement on Sunday, adding that he told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, "You can continue to count on our help."

Merz described the partnership between the nations as "not a one-way street," highlighting joint efforts by German and Ukrainian firms to build mutually beneficial technologies. "This makes us safer and stronger," he stated.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said discussions would concentrate on "strengthening Ukraine, our defense and resilience, and our shared European security."

Zelensky and Merz embrace before a commemorative ceremony at the memorial of fallen Ukrainian soldiers at Independence Square in Kyiv ( AP )

Russia’s Foreign Ministry announced on Saturday that it would persist with "mass retaliatory strikes" against Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, urging foreign citizens and diplomats to leave the country—reiterating a similar warning previously issued in May.

A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River once more on Sunday morning. Footage on social media showed the drone striking the bridge and exploding near crossing traffic. No casualties were immediately reported.

This latest attack followed earlier strikes this week that forced full or partial closures across three of Kyiv’s six Dnipro River road bridges, gridlocking traffic in Moscow’s ongoing effort to disrupt daily life in the capital. Russia has previously targeted apartment buildings, supermarket warehouses, petrol stations, and data facilities, among other sites.

More than 4-and-a-half years after Russia invaded its neighbour, there remain no clear indications that a peace settlement might be possible. Clashes along the roughly 1,250-kilometre (780-mile) front line winding across northern, eastern, and southern Ukraine have remained largely stagnant in recent months.

Global food prices could climb by more than nine per cent this year as a deadly escalation between Russia and Ukraine around the Black Sea threatens vital grain exports, analysts have warned.

Ukrainian exports fell an astonishing 75 per cent year-on-year in the first two weeks of August as Russia stepped up its attacks, striking ports more than 70 times in July and early August and hitting vessels on 62 occasions, according to port authorities.

Kyiv says the attacks threaten $40bn in crucial export revenue, worth 1.5 per cent of GDP, while hundreds of millions of people reliant on Ukrainian grain around the world stand to go without.

Pablo Meijer, assistant industry economist at advisory firm Oxford Economics, told The Independent that they now expect the World Bank food price index to rise by around 9.3 per cent in 2026, easing to around 4.4 per cent in 2027.

“Ukraine's exports have fallen sharply with Odesa shut, and world wheat trade is running around 7 per cent lower,” he said, noting Russia’s grain export volumes also contracted by 71 per cent in August, down 83 per cent year on year for the first 10 days of September.

open image in gallery Ukraine’s ports are struggling to export agricultural staples as Russian attacks ramp up around the Black Sea ( Getty/iStock )

How important is grain to Ukraine and the world?

Russia is the largest exporter of grain in the world while Ukraine is the fifth. Between them, they supply nearly a third of the world’s wheat demand.

A flare up in hostilities has seen Russia’s Black Sea grain exports fall to their lowest level in 15 years, down 65 per cent year on year in July, according to Lloyd’s List. Ukraine has seen an even larger fall of three quarters, according to government data.

Evghenia Sleptsova, senior economist at Oxford Economics, warned that Ukraine’s position has further deteriorated since August as ports remain shut and farmers are advised to plan for them to stay closed into the new year.

Grain exports totalled just 774,000 tonnes last month, down 79 per cent from the 2023-25 average for August, and around 1.4m tonnes in September, she said.

“On current rates, 2026/27 grain exports look closer to 20m tonnes, roughly half the pre-blockade forecast – and only if alternative routes reach capacity,” she said.

open image in gallery A destroyed apartment following a Russian drone attack in the port city of Odesa on 20 June, 2025 ( AFP/Getty )

Agriculture is worth around 60 per cent of Ukraine’s export revenues and the current de facto blockade is estimated to be costing Ukraine as much as $70m per day, according to Economichna Pravda.

In recent seasons, Ukraine has provided around 6 per cent of global wheat exports and 11 per cent of corn. The disruptions, if prolonged, could start to eat away at global markets.

The United Nations’ World Food Programme (WFP) is among those reliant on Ukrainian agricultural exports due to their cost and location, meaning a drop in output threatens people in some of the most vulnerable parts of the world.

Before the war, Ukrainian food exports - largely wheat, vegetable oil and peas - fed around 400 million people each year, according to the WFP.

Jean-Martin Bauer, director of the WFP's food security and nutrition analysis service, said that the organisation sourced more than 880,000 metric tons of food from Ukraine in 2021.

But since 2022, they have transported more than 1 million metric tons from Ukraine to countries in need.

“The initial closure of Black Sea ports in 2022 contributed to a sharp surge in global food prices, pushing food prices to levels not seen in a decade and making it harder for vulnerable families to access basic foods,” he said.

“While markets have adapted since then, more recent attacks on ports, vessels and export infrastructure remain a concern because they increase transport and insurance costs, reduce the predictability of grain exports, and risk putting additional pressure on food prices - particularly when combined with current disruptions in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz.”

Is there a way out of the crisis?

Since the full-scale invasion, the European Union has tried to facilitate alternative transport routes for goods to move into and out of Ukraine.

These ‘Solidarity Lanes’, transporting goods by rail, road and rivers, were still carrying 95 per cent of Ukraine’s non-agricultural exports in July, but only 20 per cent of Ukraine’s grain, oilseeds and related products.

Sea remains the most efficient way of moving big shipments over long distances, and the remaining 80 per cent of goods were still passing through the Black Sea shipping corridor - albeit in depressed quantities.

Oxford Economics warned that alternative routes could only hope to replace around 17m tonnes of missing grain, even if they build in more capacity. And even these are not currently safe from Russian strikes.

Dr Sleptova said the slide in exports from last year reflects the perception of risk rather than a lack of capacity.

“Ukraine's self-controlled corridor worked through 2025 and volumes ran at 2.5m to 3.5m tonnes a month. From late July, Russia began striking civilian vessels and port infrastructure directly, underwriters withdrew cover, and shipowners stopped calling.

“That is why volumes collapsed even though the ports were never formally closed, and it is also why they could recover quickly if the attacks stopped,” she said.

Mr Meijer noted they had reduced their earlier estimate of how much the World Bank food price index would rise - previously 11.8 per cent this year - as the disruption “has proved to be a problem of movement rather than availability”.

Global wheat supply is essentially unchanged from last year, he said, even if the war continues to create obstacles to shipping it.

open image in gallery Ukrainian seaborne grain exports have fallen an astonishing 75 per cent year-on-year from last August after months of targeted strikes. Kyiv says the trend threatens $40bn in export revenue, or 1.5 per cent of GDP. (Kyiv harvest in 2024 pictured) ( AFP/Getty )

In a renewed bid to reopen shipping in the Black Sea, Turkey, India, Egypt and other Middle Eastern nations took part in talks at the end of last week, according to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky.

Turkey and the UN helped to mediate the so-called Black Sea Grain Initiative in July 2022 to allow for the safe export of Ukrainian grain amid the war, but Russia withdrew from the agreement the following year, complaining that its own food and fertiliser exports faced serious obstacles.

Natia Seskuria, senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), said the chances of a durable reopening of the Black Sea corridor are still low, but a limited arrangement is a possibility.

“The Kremlin has little reason to make concessions, because its strikes on Ukrainian ports and energy infrastructure are a source of political leverage in any wider negotiation,” she explained. “The blockade also hits Ukraine where it is most exposed, since agriculture brought in more than half of the country's export revenue last year.”

“For Russia it is an effective way to pressure Kyiv, so the most realistic outcome is therefore a limited, time-constrained arrangement rather than a lasting corridor.

It’s a day for wagging tails, happy faces and a special annual blessing at the Malate Church in Manila.

Every Oct. 4, Catholics mark the feast day of St. Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of animals and ecology, remembered for his humility, compassion and deep love for all living things. Many parishes choose the first Sunday of October to hold community animal blessings or St. Francis service events for convenience.

At Malate Church, parishioners marked the feast Sunday by bringing their beloved pets for a special blessing — mostly dogs but also cats and even a pet snail.

“We are blessing the animals and plants and this is so much in relation to the feast of Saint Francis of Assisi ... so the Malate parish has been advocating this one,” said Father Leonito Distor, parish priest of Malate Church.

Parishioners formed a line as they walked up the aisle with their pets, waiting patiently for a priest to sprinkle their companions with holy water.

For pet owners, it was a simple expression of gratitude for the unconditional love, joy and companionship these animal friends bring into their lives every day while honoring St. Francis' call to respect and care for all of God’s creation.

“They are part of our family ... Not exactly like us in the sense that they can’t speak, but they do have emotions," said 32-year-old nurse Gaudine Supnet, who owns four Shih Tzu dogs. “I want them to feel, in some way, that we are grateful for their presence in our lives; that’s why we have them blessed.”

The church also organized free pet vaccinations for dogs and cats in the church parking lot.

___

Associated Press writer Eileen Ng in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, contributed to this report.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
News.content:
We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Eight tips to improve your laptop’s performance (and save your sanity)
News.content:
MacBooks and Windows laptops both have modes intended to maximise battery life. Low Power Mode (Mac) and Power Saver (Windows) should be avoided if you want peak performance.

On a Mac, you’ll find the Low Power Mode switch in Settings > Battery. For the best experience, set this to Never, but remember to change it back if you need your MacBook to last longer.

On a Windows laptop, there are two controls you need to consider. Both are found in Settings > System > Power & Battery.

Energy Saver mode uses multiple tactics to reduce battery consumption, including lowering maximum power. Switch this off, and you have access to Power Mode controls.

Your options are Best Power Efficiency, Balanced and Best Performance. While Balanced is the default, I was able to unlock up to 33 per cent more power by playing around with these settings using my own laptop.

To make matters more complicated, some laptops have their own performance modes. Many Asus laptops have MyAsus or Armory Crate, for example. Lenovo has the Vantage app, Dell has MyDell, and MSI laptops have MSI Center.

3. Stop applications from opening on start-up

If your laptop is slow when it first starts up, it may be because a whole bunch of apps have been given the green light to wake up with it.

Some applications such as antivirus software are critical, but most can be toggled off. As an example, I make sure apps such as Spotify, Steam and WhatsApp don’t open on startup; I only launch them when I need them.

On a MacBook, you can see which apps have this permission in Settings > General, under Open at Login. Select an app entry and click the “minus” button to remove it.

On a Windows laptop, you’ll find the list of start-up apps in Settings > Apps > Startup. Each entry has a little on/off slider.

4. Free up storage space

Kane will equal Peter Shilton’s record caps haul of 125 if he plays against Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday.

The Three Lions skipper, who came off with 20 minutes to go, said: “I’m ready to start. It would be nice. That is why he takes me off, to save me for the next one!”

Crestfallen Croatia boss Slaven Bilic added: “Of course we’re all very disappointed. I’m sad and sorry for the kids. England were just superior in every detail.”

Sports.title: Man City get Premier League expulsion update as 'two punishments proposed'
Sports.content:
Man City get Premier League expulsion update as 'two punishments proposed'

Premier League expulsion is possible for Manchester City after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the league's financial rules

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca's Manchester City could be expelled from the Premier League (Image: Getty Images)

Premier League clubs are reportedly split on expelling Manchester City from the top-flight after they were found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them. Some believe City's rule-breaking should see them kicked out and start again in non-League, while others are said to fear that removing them could lead to the resurrection of a European Super League.

‌



‌



City were the first club to formally commence withdrawal procedures from the ESL back in April 2021, following immense backlash from fans before other teams across the Premier League and Europe followed suit. The Super League project, however, did not fully die out until UEFA announced it had reached “an agreement of principles for the well-being of European club football” with Real Madrid and the European Football Clubs group back in February.

‌



It is not the only concern of some Premier League clubs concerning City's potential removal. It was reported earlier this week that unnamed executives from two top clubs have admitted that they would be 'staggered' if 15 clubs voted to expel City, describing it as 'commercial suicide'.

‌



The Telegraph claim that there are also arguments from some clubs that the Premier League is better with City in it, while its reputation will be damaged globally without them.

However, the same report also claims that there is a desire, among leading figures at some clubs, to see City thrown out and not even admitted to the EFL, as well as discussions about a potential 200-point deduction applied over several seasons.

Expulsion from the Premier League is one possible punishment that the independent commission could consider, though it would need 15 clubs to vote in favour of it. Transfer embargoes, points deductions and fines are also possibilities.

‌



View 3 Images Premier League chief executive Richard Masters faces an unprecedented situation with Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

City were found guilty of all financial-related charges and stand accused of artificially inflating revenue by more than £900million through 'sham' sponsorship deals. However, the club have appealed the decision and will now have their challenge heard by a new independent panel of three, appointed by the Premier League’s judicial panel, to determine once and for all whether any wrongdoing was committed.

The former champions claim they have 'irrefutable evidence' proving the 'sham' deals were legitimate and paid for by the Abu Dhabi government, not by the club's owners in the Abu Dhabi United Group. The Premier League allow state-owned bodies to sponsor clubs, which could help clear the club of any wrongdoing and prove that AGUD did not manufacture illegitimate deals.

‌



However, that claim has already been undermined by past statements from title sponsors Etihad during a 2015 investigation. The state-owned airline of the United Arab Emirates told the United States Department of Commerce, Transportation, and State that reports of the government paying for sponsorships were "false" during an investigation into state-owned airlines.

View 3 Images Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak is the only executive to speak publicly since the decision (Image: Elsa - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

A statement at the time read: "We are government-owned and have been since our founding. We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans.

‌



"Our shareholder's equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model."

On Friday, City confirmed their appeal and said in a statement: "The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

Sports.title: Spanish media united in 'Anthony Gordon show' verdict as they fawn over England star
Sports.content:
Spanish media united in 'Anthony Gordon show' verdict as they fawn over England star

Anthony Gordon was outstanding yet again as England crushed Croatia 7-0 in the Nations League

View 3 Images Anthony Gordon brings the ball down before setting up England's second goal (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Spanish media have lavished more praise on Anthony Gordon following his superlative display in England's demolition of Croatia. The Three Lions turned in one of their most commanding performances in recent memory, tearing apart Slavan Bilic's side in a 7-0 triumph.

‌



‌



Their firepower was on full display in the Nations League clash in Rijeka, with Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Gordon and Bukayo Saka running riot. Kane and Saka both netted twice and chipped in with an assist apiece, Bellingham struck once and set up three more, while Gordon grabbed a goal and laid on another with a stunning assist.

‌



Morgan Rogers, who came off the bench, rounded off the scoring as Thomas Tuchel's men sealed a remarkable win. Spanish publications were inevitably drawn towards the showings of Barcelona's former Newcastle man Gordon and Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham.

‌



The duo linked up brilliantly for England's second goal, with Gordon producing a breathtaking piece of control to bring down Bukayo Saka's cross before teeing up Bellingham. SPORT said: "Gordon, nicknamed 'Antoni Gros' in Barcelona, pulled off a moment of magic. With a turn, he positioned himself and delivered a precise left-footed ball to Bellingham."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Mundo Deportivo gushed: "Gordon made a control that seemed impossible, turned around and laid it back to Bellingham, who only had to push it into an almost empty net."

‌



There was widespread acclaim for Gordon's overall display, with AS labelling him "one of the standout players" alongside Bellingham. SPORT added: "Speedy as ever, he tirelessly patrolled the left flank, leaving everyone in his wake.

"He dribbled, linked up intelligently and found the net again. After missing a one-on-one chance, he made it 3-0 with a diving header."

View 3 Images Gordon starred in England's thrashing of Croatia (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Noting that Gordon had contributed to eight goals in his previous seven England appearances, SPORT suggested Gordon should head back to Barcelona in excellent shape, stating: "Gordon is still searching for his first goal as a Barca player.

"But that's what this long break is for: to sharpen his nose for goal. He has scored in his last three games and had the pleasure of assisting Bellingham for the second goal."

Mundo Deportivo dubbed it a "Gordon show" as it reported: "The Barcelona player, who scored against Spain and the Czech Republic, couldn't miss his chance against Croatia. This time it wasn't with a run into space, his speciality, but with a diving header at the far post. A Gordon show."

‌



View 3 Images Gordon celebrates scoring England's third goal (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Gordon has gone from strength to strength since England's last encounter with Croatia at the World Cup. Back then, there was widespread conjecture over whether he or Marcus Rashford ought to feature on the left wing.

There were even claims in the Spanish press that Barcelona had recruited the wrong Englishman after opting against making Rashford's loan deal permanent.

Article continues below

Yet within a few months, Gordon has established himself as one of Europe's most dangerous attacking talents. Following England's home clash with Czechia on Tuesday, he will return to Barcelona full of confidence.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham 'best in the world’ verdict from Spanish press after England blitz Croatia
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham 'best in the world’ verdict from Spanish press after England blitz Croatia

Jude Bellingham once more delivered an imperious midfield performance for England as the Three Lions dealt Croatia their biggest ever defeat

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham has been given high praise by the Spanish press (Image: Getty )

Jude Bellingham’s incredible performance during England’s 7-0 rout of Croatia saw him hailed in the Spanish media as arguably the best player in the world. Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after Three Lions skipper Harry Kane was brought off in the second half of the drubbing in Rijeka.

‌



‌



But the Real Madrid midfielder led by example throughout, playing an instrumental role as Thomas Tuchel’s side made a mockery of their formerly fearsome opponents. The 23-year-old notched a hat-trick of assists to inflict Croatia’s worst ever defeat, as well as getting on the scoresheet himself.

‌



Bellingham returned to the starting line-up on Saturday, having been rested for Tuesday’s game against Czechia before coming on in the 70th minute. He quickly showed Tuchel had made the right call by assisting Harry Kane’s early opener with a through ball.

‌



He scored one himself in the 21st minute, before a sublime bit of play in the box set up Bukayo Saka for a tap-in on the stroke of half-time. The Los Blancos star grabbed his third assist in the 87th minute, playing a through ball from deep to Morgan Rogers, who rounded the keeper.

FOLLOW OUR REAL MADRID FB PAGE! Latest news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Unsurprisingly, his display caused a stir in Spain, where he has played his club football since 2023. But even a player who played a pivotal role in a treble in his first campaign is still capable of surprises.

‌



Madrid-based publication Marca spoke glowingly of Bellingham after the Croatia match, claiming that, since his standout performances at the World Cup, Bellingham "hasn't been far from being the best player in the world."

AS described him as "a standout player" during the game, and ran with the headline: "Bellingham causes an embarrassment." Mundo Deportivo echoed that feeling by writing: "Bellingham was another standout, along with Kane and Saka."

View 2 Images Bellingham dominated in all phases of play (Image: Getty )

‌



SPORT, meanwhile, wrote: "England were in their element, playing brilliant football and thrashing Croatia. Bellingham provided the magic."

Goal’s Spanish site gave the all-action midfielder a 9/10 match rating. They heaped praise on Bellingham by writing: "A virtuoso performance from the Real Madrid star. His ability to break lines with his dribbling was the driving force behind England’s success."

La Razon summed up a stellar performance by penning: "Bellingham assisted, orchestrated and scored. He made the difference, especially in the first half when the game was still up in the air."

Article continues below

Bellingham had played a starring role in England’s summer World Cup campaign, scoring seven goals as Tuchel’s men finished in third place. He has not let up that remarkable form, managing three goals and three assists for his club so far this season, along with five goal involvements in the Nations League.

Sports.title: 'I stood between Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola - their behaviour said it all'
Sports.content:
'I stood between Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola - their behaviour said it all'

Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola were responsible for iconic Premier League battles between Liverpool and Manchester CIty

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola had an iconic rivalry (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has given an insight into the dynamic between Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp. The iconic managers oversaw a rivalry between Manchester City and Liverpool as both sides battled for the league title.

‌



‌



Their duels increasingly came to the fore as Klopp established the Reds as challengers, first taking the title race to the wire in the 2018/19 season. Guardiola’s City side narrowly finished first by a solitary point. Liverpool responded by storming to the Premier League trophy the following year.

‌



The two world-class managers added another chapter to their storied rivalry in the 2021/22 season, with City once again clinching top spot by just one point. Guardiola’s side celebrated a fourth consecutive league triumph as Klopp stepped down from his Liverpool post in 2024 but their title battles provided fans with lasting memories.

‌



The footballing world was recently rocked by City being found guilty of all financial charges brought by the Premier League, spanning from 2009 to 2018, though the club have appealed the verdict. While Guardiola has offered a supportive message to City fans, Liverpool icon Klopp refused to celebrate the outcome. Klopp’s response may not have surprised former Premier League official Scott, who sensed the pair’s mutual respect while working as a fourth official.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I actually found that when, I mean, the real elite managers, obviously Klopp and Pep absolutely were, that there was so much respect there,” Scott said on the Undr the Cosh podcast. “You could feel the respect between them. They were never actually going to go at each other.

‌



“When a big team is at home, somehow, the manager of a lower-placed team, they’re all big clubs, but the lower-placed team can be a little bit cowed and respectful. They’re quieter than they are when they’re at home and they’ve got their own environment. When they’re at home to the big clubs, they tend to be a bit more like that.

“Generally, Pep and Jurgen Klopp would have been so full of respect for each other that they wouldn’t have got into a proper bun fight.”

View 2 Images Graham Scott shared what he observed between Klopp and Guardiola as an official (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Image)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Former Liverpool boss Klopp recently gave his thoughts on the City verdict. The new Germany manager offered a fresh stance, having previously vowed to celebrate if the Reds were retrospectively awarded titles.

He said: “Of course I've heard about that, but I haven't given it much thought. I can only wait and see. I have big respect for Pep Guardiola and City's style of football; they played fantastic football and were a top class opponent for us.”

‌



Despite City securing six Premier League crowns in seven seasons, Klopp holds a slight advantage in his overall head-to-head record with Guardiola. The two legendary coaches faced each other on 30 occasions in all competitions, with the 59-year-old earning 12 victories to his rival’s 11.

“I will sleep better [when Klopp goes]. The games we play before against Liverpool were almost a nightmare,” Guardiola said about Klopp choosing to leave Liverpool in 2024. “Of course he will be missed. It was a shock [to hear the news]. I felt when I heard it that a part of Man City … we will lose something. We cannot define our period here without him … without Liverpool. Impossible.

“They have been our biggest rivals. And personally he [Klopp] has been the best rival I ever had in my life – in Dortmund when I was in Bayern, then here. I think the Premier League are going to miss him – the charisma, the personality and especially the way his teams play.”

Sports.title: 'I was a Man Utd flop after being dubbed Fergie's next gem – but I've no regrets'
Sports.content:
'I was a Man Utd flop after being dubbed Fergie's next gem – but I've no regrets'

Sir Alex Ferguson did not always get it right when it came to signing unknown talents for Manchester United

View 2 Images Manchester United signed unknown striker Manucho in 2008 (Image: 2007 Manchester United)

A Manchester United flop once hailed as another one of Sir Alex Ferguson’s gems insists he has no regrets about how his career panned out. Manucho - full name Mateus Alberto Contreiras Goncalves - was handed a three-week trial at United back in 2008.

‌



‌



Coming from obscurity in Angola, there was plenty of intrigue surrounding the forward after he impressed enough against the likes of Rio Ferdinand and Nemanja Vidic in training to be awarded a contract at England’s biggest club.

‌



Sir Alex’s assistant at the time, Carlos Quieroz, had persuaded the Scot to grant the then-24-year-old a trial period in a move which would be unthinkable today. Ferguson said: "He is a tall, agile, quick forward and through contacts that Carlos has, was brought to our attention around six months ago."

‌



Despite already boasting a wealth of world class attacking options, namely Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and Carlos Tevez, United needed a back-up striker, owing to Louis Saha’s fitness issues. After signing for United, Manucho fired Angola to the quarter-finals of the Africa Cup of Nations with four goals, earning him a place in the tournament’s best XI ahead of Samuel Eto’o.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Premier League winner opens up on ‘unfair’ Sir Alex Ferguson row that involved Gary Neville READ MORE :

Man Utd eye JJ Gabriel legal action if teenager leaves amid Barcelona and Real Madrid interest READ MORE :

Off the back of that, The Manchester Evening News published a story on Manucho, which read: "All the signs suggest Sir Alex Ferguson has unearthed another gem in new signing Manucho. The Angolan striker is fast becoming the story of the African Cup of Nations - setting alight a tournament that features global stars such as Didier Drogba, Samuel Eto'o and Michael Essien."

‌



Ferguson was also impressed, commenting: "It is always difficult to assess, but there is good potential there. He has good assets, so there is something to work on. If we can get the work permit, we can map out a future for him."

The work permit mentioned was one of the key factors in Manucho's time at United not working out. The initial application was rejected by the Home Office, which saw the forward sent on an initial six-month loan to Greek club Panathinaikos. Manucho's work permit was finally approved that summer, but a metatarsal injury denied him the chance to make the first impression he wanted.

View 2 Images Manucho's time at Old Trafford overlapped with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: 2008 Getty Images)

‌



In September 2008, Manucho finally made his debut for United in the Carling Cup against Middlesbrough. He made his Premier League bow during a 5-0 win over Stoke, where he played 16 minutes and set up a goal for Danny Welbeck.

However, following that dream debut, he never played for the Red Devils again in the Premier League. Hull offered him a lifeline in the January window by signing him on a six-month loan as they attempted to maintain their top-flight status, but the Angolan managed just two goals in 17 appearances.

By the time his loan stint ended, Ferguson had made up his mind that the forward didn’t have a future at Old Trafford. Manucho sealed a permanent move to Real Valladolid in 2009 and went on to play over 100 times for the Spanish outfit, before doing the same for Rayo Vallecano after further loans at Bucaspor and Manisaspor.

Article continues below

He called time on his professional career back in 2019 after leaving Cornella, having scored 22 goals across 53 games with Angola. Yet, the former striker was adamant in a 2023 interview looking back on his career that he had no regrets over his United stint, telling others that their dreams can also come true.

Sharing a snap of his time playing at United, Manucho said: "Never stop dreaming. If I could, you can too. Never stop fighting to get your dreams."

Sports.title: 'I've seen Wayne Rooney's true character – he's very different away from football'
Sports.content:
'I've seen Wayne Rooney's true character – he's very different away from football'

One of Wayne Rooney's former teammates has given an insight into the Manchester United and England legend's personality

View 2 Images A former England star has discussed his experience of being Wayne Rooney's teammate (Image: IAN KINGTON/AFP via Getty Images)

Jermain Defoe has revealed that Wayne Rooney often showed a different side of his personality away from the pitch. The Premier League legend was a burst of confidence and aggression when making his Everton breakthrough, aged 16.

‌



‌



Rooney soon became a global superstar and showed no fear against more experienced pros as he continued to take his career to the next level. After starring for England at Euro 2004, the striker joined Manchester United for £25.6million, becoming the world’s most expensive teenager.

‌



Under Sir Alex Ferguson's guidance, Rooney’s winning mentality and competitiveness were often on full display as he claimed five Premier League titles, the Champions League and numerous other major honours. These characteristics, combined with his natural ability, saw him become United and England’s all-time top scorer, though Harry Kane has since taken the latter accolade.

‌



Having been in the spotlight from an early age, the 40-year-old’s on-pitch persona was well-documented. However, his former England teammate Defoe has given an insight into Rooney’s more humble and caring nature after experiencing a different side of his character.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Wayne Rooney was special,” Defoe said on The Warm-Up podcast by William Hill. “I could talk about his footballing ability for hours because he is one of the best players England has ever produced, but away from football he is so humble.

‌



“He has so much love for people; you see it and you feel it. Because of how he is as a person, good things were always going to happen for him.”

The United legend and his family are the subjects of a new Disney+ docuseries, The Real Rooneys. While the England icon had already begun to showcase his personality as a pundit, Defoe, who played alongside Rooney for the Three Lions on 28 occasions, fondly remembers their time working together.

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe spoke glowingly about Wayne Rooney's personality (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“He was so natural, and he enjoyed it. He used to tell me to make runs and he would find me,” Defoe continued. “I got the feeling that he wanted me to score. To be like that, you have to be a special person.

“I played with a lot of centre forwards who, if they’re on the bench and you score, you can see that they’re raging. Rooney was completely different. He would score goals, but it wasn’t about that for him – it was about winning.

Article continues below

“He could do everything. He scored a lot of goals when he was young but then sacrificed that for a few years at Manchester United to become a winger and allow Cristiano Ronaldo and Carlos Tevez to do what they do. He was humble enough to be on the side of that but know that it was helping them to win the Premier League. That’s all he was focused on.”

The 40-year-old ended his 13-year stint at United with a record 253 goals in 559 appearances. On the international stage, Rooney scored 53 goals across his 120 England caps, while Defoe netted 20 times for the Three Lions in 57 games.

Sports.title: 'I'm not proud of what I said to Man Utd boss in blind rage - it was harsh and ruthless'
Sports.content:
'I'm not proud of what I said to Man Utd boss in blind rage - it was harsh and ruthless'

This ex-Manchester United idol opened up on his contentious departure from Old Trafford

View 3 Images Ruud van Nistelrooy and Sir Alex Ferguson had a complex relationship at United (Image: 2005 Manchester United)

Manchester United hero Ruud van Nistelrooy said he harbours regret at how he left the club after he hit out at Sir Alex Ferguson in a "blind rage." The Dutch striker scored 150 goals for United after joining from PSV Eindhoven in 2001.

‌



‌



He departed Old Trafford for Real Madrid in July 2006 under a cloud after falling out with the legendary United boss. Van Nistelrooy has since moved into management, taking charge of United on an interim basis in 2024, and was rumoured to have been considered for the caretaker job again after Ruben Amorim was sacked in January.

‌



He is now the assistant coach of the Netherlands national team, with his nation playing Serbia in the Nations League on Sunday evening. However, before he ventured into the dugout, the forward was known as one of the deadliest marksmen in the Premier League.

‌



Despite being United's primary goalscorer, Sir Alex famously left Van Nistelrooy as an unused substitute for United's 4-0 win over Wigan in the 2006 League Cup final.

The Dutch forward remained a substitute for United's next six Premier League games before returning to the starting XI for wins against West Ham and Bolton. However, after he was informed he would not be involved against Charlton for the final game of the season, he stormed out of Old Trafford three hours before kick-off.

Ferguson then accused Van Nistelrooy of undermining team morale. The Dutchman, speaking in 2019, revealed that he regrets how his time at Old Trafford ended.

‌



"It was very harsh, both ways," he told Eleven Sports. "Especially after five years of having such a strong bond. I learned so much from him, and in all modesty: he from me too. And yet the end was ruthless."

Quizzed on whether he had repaired his relationship with the iconic Scot, Van Nistelrooy revealed that he had made the first contact after his departure.

View 3 Images Rudd Van Nistelrooy had a falling out with Sir Alex Ferguson (Image: 2005 AFP)

‌



He added: "It was me who took the first step to make it okay again. I called him. A few times a year I felt bad about what I had done to him and the names I called him when he kept me on the bench the entire match in the League Cup final in Cardiff. In a blind rage I shouted at him.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I called him something. I called him a number of things in a blind rage. Cocky and stubborn as I was, I couldn't snap out of that for some time after. That's how it all crashed.

‌



"It was just really disrespectful, there were lots of other people there. It wasn't all that outrageous in terms of words but it was completely out of order. Not done. I wasn't proud of it, still am not."

View 3 Images Ruud van Nistelrooy managed United on an Interim basis in 2024 (Image: 2024 Getty Images)

Time healed all wounds, however. After spells with Real, Hamburg and Malaga, he retired in 2012 and turned to management with PSV. He then joined United as assistant manager under former boss Erik ten Hag in 2024.

Article continues below

He became interim head coach when Ten Hag was sacked. He won all four games in charge before being replaced by Amorim. A less-than-stellar time in charge of Leicester City followed before he made his way to the Dutch national side.

"Ruud is and always will be a Manchester United legend," a United statement said after he departed the club as assistant and interim coach. "We are grateful for his contribution and the way in which he approached his role throughout his time with the club. He will always be very welcome at Old Trafford."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Star 'ready for January transfer' as private Mo Salah chats revealed
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Star 'ready for January transfer' as private Mo Salah chats revealed

The latest Liverpool news features Mo Salah and a star who is reportedly ready to quit Anfield

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah had a private chat with a Liverpool star (Image: Getty Images)

There's just one more week to go until Premier League action returns with Liverpool in action against Manchester City at Anfield next Sunday. The game against Enzo Maresca's pace setters could act as a major barometer for Andoni Iraola when it comes to judging the level his side are currently at.

‌



‌



Liverpool are unbeaten so far in all competitions, but only have two wins in the Premier League: against Ipswich Town and Bournemouth. The Basque coach is still getting to grips with his squad, with some fringe players yet to feature.

‌



One of whom is Federico Chiesa and the latest news sees the Italian linked with a move away in January. Rio Ngumoha is one player who has been given game time by Iraola, and the teenager opened up about a private chat he had with Liverpool legend Mohamed Salah. Mirror Football takes a closer look.

‌



Chiesa 'set for exit'

According to Italian outlet Calciomercato, Serie A sides Inter Milan, Lazio and Atalanta are circling a swoop for Chiesa. The publication states the 28-year-old is ready to depart Anfield in January.

Zinedine Zidane gives three-word Jeremy Jacquet verdict that Liverpool fans will love READ MORE :

Thierry Henry launches Bradley Barcola defence after slow start to Liverpool career READ MORE :

The Italian international made just two Premier League starts across two seasons under former boss Arne Slot after signing in the summer of 2024 from Juventus. Despite being linked with a move away this summer, he claimed he wanted to stay at the Reds and fight for a spot in the first XI under Iraola.

"Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool," Chiesa said. "I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.

‌



View 3 Images Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola and Federico Chiesa, who could be on his way out of Liverpool (Image: 2026 Visionhaus)

"I don’t know, it is difficult to say [if this is a fresh start]. It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that."

However, the Italian winger is yet to feature for the Reds this season, having been ruled out with an injury. He was also left out of the club's official 25-man squad for their Champions League campaign, suggesting his future at Anfield is now in a precarious position.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ngumoha's Mo Salah chats

Ngumoha has opened up about the advice he received from Mo Salah before the winger left the Reds this summer. Ngumoha became the youngest scorer in the club's history when he bagged a late winner in a 3-2 victory over Newcastle United in August 2025, aged just 16 years and 361 days.

‌



The 18-year-old has since kicked on by earning his first senior England cap, while he has also made five appearances for the Reds so far this season. No doubt a deadly presence on the flank, Ngumoha has found goals and assists hard to come by, however, with two goals and one assist in 35 senior appearances for the club to date.

The youngster explained how Salah tasked him with improving that area of his game. "The player who I probably learned the most from is Mohamed Salah, when he was at Liverpool," Ngumoha said.

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha was given advice by Salah (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



"He taught me a lot, especially towards the back end when he knew he was leaving. He helped me a lot. Like he always says about looking at his numbers and he was always telling me, 'Rio, you know you're a good player but to reach the top, you have to add the goals and assists.'

"And it will come naturally but he was just going through little things like that [with me]. When he first started [talking to me], it was like, 'Wow! I've been watching you since I was young and you're telling me how to [improve]. Like, you're helping me and you're guiding me.'

"But then over time, I saw him as a very good team-mate and he was helping me a lot, so I can't thank him much more."

Sports.title: Rampant Roosters bash Broncos to claim third NRLW premiership
Sports.content:
Sydney Roosters crushed the Brisbane Broncos 30-6 to complete the perfect season and claim a third NRLW premiership title.

The unstoppable Roosters gave legends Corban Baxter and Millie Elliott the perfect send-off with six tries in a first-half blitz at Accor Stadium.

Sydney won all 11 of their regular-season matches before claiming victory in both finals to complete a perfect season.

Brydie Parker (2), Tarryn Aiken, Isabelle Kelly, Jayme Fressard and Amber Hall all crossed the whitewash as the Roosters produced a dominant first-half display.

Parker completed her Grand Final hat-trick before the hour mark to extend Sydney's lead to 30-0.

Jesse Southwell finally got the Broncos on the board after 63 minutes, but the game was already done and dusted, with the Roosters soon celebrating a crushing victory.

Retiring Roosters forward Millie Elliott said: "Everyone knows what that felt like and we definitely used that as motivation all season, not just in this game, all season," she said.

"And we worked so hard, I take my hat off to [head coach John] Strangey and the coaching staff, they really left no stone unturned this year and we wanted to put in a performance like that."

Winning captain Isabelle Kelly said: "I knew that this year we're creating something special, and I think we're building and made that our best game yet. I love you guys and I'm so glad that we get to do this together."

She added: "To Corban and Millie, you guys have been absolutely incredible for this NRLW competition, but mostly for the Roosters the impact that you guys have had on us, Millie, you being a mum, it's just created such a special bond for us to look forward to for many years. And you'll always be a Rooster."

Sports.title: Sabalenka follows Rybakina out of China Open after shock defeat
Sports.content:
A day after world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out of the China Open, world No 2 Aryna Sabalenka followed suit in Beijing on Sunday.

Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova defeated the four-time Grand Slam champion 6-4 6-3, leaving the tournament without its two top seeds in the opening week.

Rybakina was knocked out on Saturday, and Sabalenka has now joined her in an early exit from the WTA 1000 event in Beijing.

Sabalenka, who was denied a US Open three-peat by Rybakina last month, squandered five break points in the opening set as her struggles in Beijing continued.

The 28-year-old Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarter-finals at the tournament.

Bartunkova, the No 26 seed, will next face Austria's 24-year-old Sinja Kraus, who defeated Dayana Yastremska 6-1 6-4 earlier on Sunday.

Fifth seed Mirra Andreeva eased into the fourth round with a 6-4 6-1 victory over Polina Kudermetova.

The French Open champion fired six aces and converted five of seven break-point opportunities to overwhelm her Uzbek opponent in just 68 minutes.

Alcaraz into Tokyo semi-finals

Image: Carlos Alcaraz has reached back-to-back Tokyo semi-finals

Top seed Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the semi-finals of the Japan Open after Denis Shapovalov was forced to retire with a hip injury, extending the Spaniard's strong return from a four-month wrist injury lay-off.

The defending champion was leading 7-6 (7-4) 2-1 when the Canadian called it a day.

"It was a little bit frustrating with my serve. I couldn't find a good way of serving: I was struggling almost every game on serve," Alcaraz said after dropping serve three times in the opening set.

"But I'm just happy with the way I came back after every break. It was a great first set: Great points, great rallies."

The Spaniard said he was disappointed to progress in such circumstances.

"It's a shame that he had to pull out. Going through to a semi-final like this is not the way I wanted, but sometimes sports are tough. You have to accept it. Hopefully he's going to be able to play in Shanghai healthy."

Alcaraz will face compatriot Jaume Munar in the semi-finals after the qualifier defeated France's Kyrian Jacquet 6-4 6-2.

Sports.title: Daryz seeks historic Arc double
Sports.content:
Daryz seeks to retain his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown in the 2026 renewal of Europe's richest race - live on Sky Sports Racing at 3.05pm.

3.05 ParisLongchamp - Daryz bids for historic Arc double

Daryz will look for an historic back-to-back double in Europe's biggest race, bidding to be the first colt since Alleged in 1978 to achieve this feat.

Francis-Henri Graffard's colt looked as good as ever when he returned in the Prix Ganay, which was then followed up with an equally sparkling performance in the Prix Aga Khan IV. A trip to Royal Ascot in June for the Prince Of Wales' Stakes didn't go to plan as he was third, although it transpired blood issues were found following the race.

After a break, Graffard's star made light work of Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller - who he reopposes today - in the Prix Foy, with the trainer saying he was only 75 per cent fit. Having been drawn in stall five, this short priced favourite will take all the beating with connections very confident.

Kalpana was seventh in this contest last year and connections are keen for redemption as she returns to ParisLongchamp looking to emulate Juddmonte filly Bluestocking, who two-years ago took this famous prize. The King George winner looks good as ever this year and has racked up two Group 1s. Drawn in stall six, conditions look well-suited and with Colin Keane having had another year of riding her, she could go very close.

Image: Kalpana faces Daryz in this afternoon's Arc

Maltese Cross looks to give William Haggas his first Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe as this progressive three-year-old looks to continue progressing in notching up his second Group 1. After finishing second in the Derby, this son of Sea The Stars went on to win the Grand Prix de Paris and backed that up with a win in the Great Voltigeur Stakes. His chances have been dealt a blow though, having being drawn in stall 11.

Aidan O'Brien runs three Classic winners in Europe's premier race, with Ryan Moore opting to ride Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini over Diamond Necklace, who has been allocated the dreaded stall 16. Last year's runner-up Minnie Hauk completes the trio and will be partnered by William Buick in a bid to go one better.

3.50 ParisLongchamp - Star mare Aventure headlines field of nine

Aventure looks to add to her impressive record against her own sex when she headlines this field of nine in the Group 1 Prix de l'Opera Longines.

Christophe Ferland's star mare has contested the Arc in the last two years, finishing second and eleventh respectively. This year she returns to racing against fillies and mares, against whom her record reads eight victories from 12 starts - including two Group 1s.

She bounced back from defeat at the hands of Daryz in the Prix Ganay when downing Sunly in the Prix Corrida. Calandagan proved too good for her in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud but her big day came when she subsequently took out the Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville in the summer, defeating the unbeaten Diamond Necklace.

Three-year-old Pink Panthera appears to be the best of the rest. She has hit the crossbar twice at Group 1 level this season - firstly in the Prix de Diane and then last time out in the Prix Vermeille. Three-year-olds have a fabulous record in this contest, having won eight out of the last 10 renewals.

Irish 1000 and Coronation Stakes winner Precise has been highly tried this year and takes the set up in trip for the first time, with Ryan Moore taking the ride.

4.25 ParisLongchamp - Samangan and Thesecretadversary clash again in the Foret

Samangan and Thesecretadversary meet again, this time in the Group 1 Qatar Prix de la Foret over seven furlongs.

Thesecretadversary got the better of the Francis-Henri Graffard trained Samangan in the Prix Jean Prat, which followed victory in the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. The son of St Mark's Basilica then went up in trip to the Prix Jacques le Marois, which saw him beaten three lengths by Rayif - another Aga Khan colt trained by Francis-Henri Graffard.

Samangan was in fourth that day with (the also re-opposing) True Love in second. He then went down in trip to the Prix Maurice de Gheest and brought up his first Group 1, seeing off the fast-finishing Divison to score.

True Love hasn't won since she became a classic winner in Newmarket's 1000 Guineas in May. She has since ran creditably in defeat, placing three times in Group 1 company. Nighttime looks to bounce back to form for Christopher Head, whilst Marvelman flies the flag for Andrew Balding.

Sports.title: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final in 2023 repeat
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester.

Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2.

A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The final, in which the winner will earn £150,000 and runner-up £80,000, will be first to six sets, with Humphries hoping to fare better than he did in 2024 and 2025, when he lost 6-4 to Mike De Decker and 6-1 to Luke Littler respectively.​​​

Price prevails after being frustrated by Aspinall antics

Price romped into a 3-0 lead over Aspinall, peeling off two 13-darters and then a 15-darter to sweep the opener before he broke The Asp in the deciding leg of set two.

The third set went on throw until the fourth leg, when Aspinall missed six darts to hold, including two at double one, and Price subsequently pinned D10 to move 3-0 up.

Things seemed bleak for Aspinall when Price broke in 14 darts at the start of the fourth set, only for The Asp to win back-to-back legs with well-thrown darts at D16 around failed ones before pulling back a set with a stunning 132 finish featuring two bullseyes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Nathan Aspinall's superb 132 checkout during his defeat to Gerwyn Price as he fired in successive bullseyes before hitting D16

The 2022 runner-up won the fifth set against the throw but Price did likewise in the sixth to move one away from victory and then broke Aspinall twice in a row in the seventh set, after being broken himself, to qualify for a fourth Grand Prix final following 2020, 2021 and 2023.

Speaking afterwards, Price said he had been annoyed by Aspinall complaining about the rowdy crowd, telling Sky Sports: "I was upset with him a little bit. I said, 'they're on your side bud, I'm up against it'.

"As good as the crowd is for me, they were all for him. He's performing a little bit on stage. I'm good friends with Nathan, but sometimes you've got to let your darts go. It did [affect my game]."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price said he had words with Aspinall on stage after becoming annoyed with his opponent's reactions to the crowd

'Controlled' Humphries into another Leicester final

Later, Humphries ended Wade's hopes of a third World Grand Prix crown, and first since 2010.

'Cool Hand' won the sixth set on throw after the first five had been taken 3-1 by the player throwing second.

Wade, who produced the checkout of the game with a 141 in the second set but largely struggled to hit the mandatory leg-opening double, took the next stanza, but Humphries was not to be denied, firing in back-to-back 137s to break 'The Machine' in the eighth set around two holds of throw.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Humphries gave Wade a nod of respect after The Machine pinned a fantastic 141 checkout during their semi-final

Humphries, who had beaten Dave Chisnall, Jermaine Wattimena and Niels Zonneveld prior to knocking out Wade, told Sky Sports: "I did say I was going to play a lot better and I did - I felt a lot more relaxed.

"That was the real me there today and I'm really proud of myself for performing like that. It's been a long time since I've felt that control and not like I was going to flounder a little bit.

"To make four Grand Prix finals on the trot is super special. It's history and I'm proud of that but unless I pick that trophy up, unfortunately that history doesn't mean anything.

"I've got to do it again [on Sunday] because there's so many major finals I've let slip. Gezzy [Price] is playing well but if I play like that again, it's going to be a cracking game."
