Sports.title: Verstappen takes first pole of 2026 ahead of Hamilton and Antonelli in Sepang | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia qualifying
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen dominated qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit to claim his first pole position of the season.

Lewis Hamilton will join him on the front row of the grid for Formula 1’s first race in Malaysia for nine years. The pair will start in the same order they finished the last race at this track.

The threat from Mercedes failed to materialise as Andrea Kimi Antonelli compromised his session with his latest track limits breach and George Russell never figured in the fight for pole position.

Antonelli, who has had multiple penalties for track limits breaches this year, made life difficult for himself when he strayed beyond the exit kerb at turn six on his first lap in Q2. With Pirelli’s soft tyres only good enough for a single flying lap on the highly abrasive Malaysian track, Antonelli had to take a second fresh set to ensure he reached Q3, where unlike most of his fellow front-runners he would not have the benefit of a second set.

Verstappen’s first run in Q3 put him comfortably ahead, while Isack Hadjar backed him up in second place. Antonelli did his sole run in the gap between the others taking to the track and initially slotted into third place.

With his final run, Verstappen cut another tenth of a second off his best time so far, leaving the benchmark at a 1’35.130. His original run would have been quick enough for pole, as only Hamilton could get within three tenths of a second of him.

Hadjar qualified third but his grid penalty will drop him to eighth on the grid. Both Mercedes drivers will be among those to benefit, Antonelli moving up to third, Russell seventh. The two championship leaders will be separated by Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari and the two McLarens.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The two other drivers with grid penalties dropped out in Q2: Franco Colapinto and Arvid Lindblad Racing Bulls used Lindblad to give his team mate a tow down the back straight – some compensation for crashing into his team mate in Baku last week – and Liam Lawson duly took 10th place. However he was eliminated by a superb final lap from Gabriel Bortoleto.

The Audi driver claimed a place in the final 10 having been the only Audi driver to progress through Q1. Like Ferrari, both their drivers used the medium rubber, but a poor final lap by Nico Hulkenberg meant he went no further.

The Aston Martin drivers revelled in their latest car improvements to achieve the team’s first double Q2 appearance of the season. It comes five months after the FIA changed its Additional Development Update Opportunity regulations to help its power unit supplier Honda.

Carlos Sainz Jnr, the only Williams driver to reach Q2, split the two AMR26s. Alexander Albon continued his run of Q1 eliminations this season after locking up and running wide at turn 14.

Both Haas drivers went out in the first round. Oliver Bearman went deep at turn one on his first attempt while Esteban Ocon was one of the first drivers to complete his final run and felt he had left the pits too soon. The Cadillac pair were slowest.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Calls Anthony Joshua A Usyk Warm-Up
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury is already looking past Anthony Joshua toward a trilogy bout with Oleksandr Usyk. He treats their December 11 Cardiff clash like tune-up work for a champion who already beat him twice.

That gives Joshua a golden opportunity to wreck everything. A loss completely ruins any market for another Usyk meeting, especially after Fury spent weeks dismissing Joshua as light work.

“I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk,” Fury told Sky Sports.

Fury wants the Usyk trilogy in New York. He also points to his activity this year, including fights with Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, as evidence that he will enter the Joshua bout ready.

Staying active helps Fury shake off ring rust, but Joshua brings threats none of those recent opponents offered. Joshua carries genuine power. Fury cannot afford to look past him or script future dates while dodging heavy artillery. A single defensive lapse ends all talk of a third Usyk clash instantly.

Joshua hits hard enough to test whether Fury still has elite reflexes over 12 rounds. Usyk is an entirely different animal. He relies on rapid footwork, awkward southpaw angles, non-stop punching. Fury could beat Joshua easily, but that does not solve the tactical problems that cost him against Usyk twice.

Winning in Cardiff gives Fury a huge name to brag about. It proves nothing about how a third fight with Usyk would turn out.

Fury’s trash talk is pure fight promotion. He degrades Joshua to sell the Cardiff gate while teasing an even bigger event down the line. His bravado sells tickets, but talk alone proves nothing about the reality inside his training camp.

If Fury wins, he could try to sell a big victory, but Usyk still holds two decisions over him. The champion would need serious motivation to face a boxer he conquered twice.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez Managers Meet
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez’s manager Keith Connolly has met with Ryan Garcia’s manager Lupe Valencia and teased a “mega fight.” However, making Garcia–Lopez could require Teofimo to give up his WBA welterweight title, with Jack Catterall’s mandatory defense due.

The money fight can happen without two belts. The question is whether Teofimo can take his WBA championship into it while Catterall insists on getting his opportunity.

“Met up with Lupe Valencia today in San Diego for coffee,” Connolly wrote on Instagram, in a screenshot shared by Dan Rafael. “Boxing fans get ready Mega Fight coming.”

Connolly did not identify the matchup or announce an agreement, but meeting with Ryan’s manager and posting that caption gives Garcia–Lopez speculation something more substantial than another exchange of callouts.

It does nothing to settle the Catterall situation.

Teofimo and Catterall have until October 22 to negotiate a deal for their WBA title fight before the organization can move toward a purse bid. Catterall has made clear he won’t step aside, leaving Teofimo’s team with an obligation that a separate agreement with Ryan would not erase.

Unless the WBA grants permission for Garcia–Lopez to go ahead first, Teofimo could have to sacrifice his belt to pursue it. The deadline itself would not automatically strip him, but signing for Ryan would still leave the mandatory unresolved.

From a business perspective, losing the WBA title might be a price Teofimo is willing to pay. Ryan offers a commercially attractive opponent, and his WBC championship would give Teofimo another title to chase if the fight proceeds as a sanctioned defense.

That would change the promotion from a welterweight unification to a challenge for Ryan’s belt, without necessarily reducing the fighters’ interest in making it.

Connolly’s post suggests there is something to watch. Until the Catterall obligation is addressed, though, the two-title billing remains uncertain.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Offered To Stage Bentley–Hernandez In Ghana
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley had an offer from Eddie Hearn to defend his WBO middleweight title against Yoenli Hernandez in Ghana before choosing Zuffa Boxing. Hearn revealed that Bentley requested a meeting with Matchroom, opening discussions about a route that would have included fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bentley instead signed a multi-fight Zuffa agreement and will face Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena. That provides a different opponent and promotional future, although his WBO title situation remains unresolved.

“Denzel Bentley asked for a meeting with us,” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “He was going to fight the mandatory in Ghana on our Ghana show. He chose to accept a little bit more money and … vacate the belt. … You blow the belt for nothing, for an extra 50 grand. I mean, it’s just madness.”

Hearn did not disclose Matchroom’s total offer or the terms beyond staging the Hernandez defense in Ghana. His £50,000 comparison therefore gives only part of the financial picture. A multi-fight agreement also requires Bentley to consider future purses, opponents and opportunities.

Hearn believes Bentley would beat Hernandez. I would favor the Cuban, whose pressure, combination punching and power could make the mandatory a demanding defense. Bentley would need to produce enough offense to discourage Hernandez while avoiding prolonged exchanges that suit the challenger.

That difference in how the fight is viewed helps explain the decision. Hearn sees a title Bentley should retain; Bentley may see a dangerous obligation alongside an alternative that offers greater financial security.

There is also a qualification to Hearn’s claim about vacating. Bentley has reportedly petitioned the WBO to approve Mosley as a voluntary defense, with his title at risk if permission is refused.

The Ghana proposal shows Bentley had another option. Whether it was the better one depends on more than the immediate purse difference Hearn described.

Sports.title: Andy Lee Reveals Ben Whittaker’s COVID Before Wallace Fight
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s trainer, Andy Lee, said the unbeaten light heavyweight had COVID the week before facing Conor Wallace. Whittaker offered a different explanation for his difficult finish in Birmingham on Saturday: the fight had been “too easy,” and he lost concentration.

Dan Rafael reported Lee’s disclosure after Whittaker’s points victory, adding that both sides were discussing a rematch. The illness claim provides context for Whittaker’s performance, although how much it affected him remains unclear.

Whittaker sounded eager to face Wallace again rather than leave the late rounds as the final impression of their IBF eliminator.

“I think we should do it again and I’ll beat him down even better,” Whittaker said afterward. “If I’m honest, it was too easy. I took my eye off the ball a little bit and he come up with a good shot. That’s boxing. But what did I do? I dug it out and I won.”

That explanation reflects how comfortably Whittaker controlled much of the contest, but it understates the danger Wallace created late. Whittaker was hurt and had to survive an opponent who kept pressing after spending the earlier rounds struggling to reach him.

Lee’s account and Whittaker’s explanation can both be true. An interrupted preparation could have left him below his best, while lapses in concentration gave Wallace opportunities. However, the reported illness cannot tell us which mistakes came from his physical condition and which came from his decisions.

Calling the fight easy also gives Whittaker something to prove in a return bout. Winning the early rounds comfortably is only part of the job. Maintaining distance, following instructions and avoiding unnecessary exchanges become more valuable when an opponent starts landing.

A rematch would give Wallace another opportunity after his strong finish and allow Whittaker to show whether he can sustain his early control over 12 rounds.

For a fighter pursuing a world title, that would be useful evidence. Whittaker proved he could survive trouble on Saturday. Facing Wallace again would test whether he can prevent it.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Rejects Dana White’s Fury–Joshua Production Claim
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn claims Sela has denied in writing that Dana White will handle television production for Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua. However, Hearn remains open to negotiating White’s involvement and expects to meet him in Los Angeles next week.

That leaves White’s role unresolved. Hearn is challenging his claim to an existing production role while asking what Joshua and Matchroom would receive in exchange for agreeing to his participation.

“After that video, I spoke to Sela and I said, ‘Have you seen this video?’” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “And they said, ‘Yes, and it is completely untrue.’ And they told me that in writing. … He cannot do that under the contract.”

That is Hearn’s account of Sela’s response and the contractual restrictions. The written communication and relevant contract wording were not presented during his remarks.

Hearn also acknowledged that Turki Alalshikh and Netflix want White involved. Their interest gives the proposed Los Angeles meeting a purpose: finding terms that satisfy Joshua’s side while allowing White a place in the event.

For Hearn, the question is what that participation adds. He asked what would be in it for Joshua and Matchroom, suggesting that permission could depend on a tangible benefit rather than simply accommodating the wishes of the other parties.

He conceded that the public dispute has helped the promotion. That creates an incentive to reach an agreement, particularly if an appearance by White generates more attention. Hearn wants freedom to question him directly if they share a press-conference stage.

The production claim nevertheless concerns a specific responsibility, beyond appearing at promotional events. Hearn’s remarks leave room for White to secure an agreed role later, but challenge the suggestion that television production is already his responsibility.

The proposed meeting could settle that difference. For now, Hearn’s position is that any involvement requires agreement from him and Joshua, with the benefits explained before they give their approval.

Sports.title: Whittaker Holds On To Beat Wallace
Sports.content:
Ben “The Surgeon” Whittaker survived a difficult finish to defeat Conor Wallace by unanimous decision over 12 rounds at Utilita Arena in Birmingham on Saturday. The Matchroom Boxing card, promoted by Eddie Hearn, aired on DAZN.

Whittaker (13-0-1, 9 KOs), the Tokyo Olympic silver medalist from Darlaston, retained his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and secured the IBF mandatory position. Wallace (17-2, 12 KOs), a Northern Irish-born southpaw based in Brisbane, made him work hard to protect the lead he had built.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds before Wallace hurt him with a lead left to the chin in the tenth. Wallace’s success made the closing rounds increasingly difficult, although Whittaker steadied himself in the 11th.

In the 12th, Wallace hurt Whittaker badly and pressed for a stoppage. Whittaker repeatedly held and struggled to stay upright, with referee Kieran McCann separating the fighters as the home boxer tried to reach the bell. Several falls prompted questions about whether knockdowns should have been called, but none were officially recorded.

Whittaker won by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. His early work secured the victory, but Wallace’s late attack exposed defensive weaknesses that will need attention before a world title fight.

Bilal Fawaz stops Eithan James

British and Commonwealth junior middleweight champion Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1, 5 KOs), of London, retained his titles by stopping Northampton’s Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of the eighth round of their scheduled 12-round contest.

Fawaz dropped James with a right hand to the chin, then scored another knockdown before referee Ron Kearney ended the fight. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz collected the £5,000 knockout bonus Hearn had offered before the bout.

Hamza Uddin takes Sean Bruce’s British title

Walsall’s Hamza “The Great” Uddin (8-0, 5 KOs) stopped British flyweight champion Sean Bruce (8-3), of Leicester, at 2:49 of round eight to claim the British and vacant Commonwealth titles.

Uddin scored two knockdowns in the fifth round, with Bruce beating referee Victor Loughlin’s counts and continuing to fight. A third knockdown, from a body shot in the eighth, ended the contest. Loughlin waved it off immediately, bringing Bruce’s first British title defense to a close.

Ibraheem Sulaimaan retains English title

Birmingham southpaw Ibraheem “Spider” Sulaimaan defeated Sonny Hardy (12-1, 5 KOs), of Wickford, by unanimous decision after 10 competitive rounds to retain his English super featherweight title.

There was little between them after six rounds, and referee Chris Dean deducted a point from Sulaimaan in the seventh. The champion finished strongly over the final three rounds to secure scores of 97-93, 97-93 and 96-93.

Hardy’s work in the middle rounds made the contest closer than the cards suggested to some ringside observers, with several scoring it narrowly and others favoring the challenger.

Aaron Bowen wins Midlands Area title

Aaron Bowen (9-1, 6 KOs), of Coventry, took the Midlands Area super middleweight title from Klinton Baptiste (5-1) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds.

Bowen repeatedly landed lead right hands from the third round onward, leaving Baptiste’s left eye badly swollen and nearly closed. Baptiste absorbed sustained punishment but lasted the distance as Bowen pursued a stoppage.

The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92.

Odel Kamara wins professional debut

Liverpool junior middleweight Odel “King” Kamara (1-0, 1 KO), a 2025 World Boxing champion, stopped Greece’s Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) at 2:53 of the third round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Kamara dropped Ritzakis in the opening round, with referee Ryan Churchill administering an eight-count. In the third, Kamara landed a short uppercut in close before Churchill called a halt, with Ritzakis bleeding from the nose.

The stoppage drew criticism from some ringside observers for being premature. Kamara also looked tired early and left openings while loading up on power shots, making this a successful debut with room for improvement.

Harley Burrows stops Matias Ezequiel Herrera

Harley “The Beast” Burrows (3-0, 2 KOs) stopped Argentina’s Matias Ezequiel Herrera (8-9-2, 5 KOs) at 1:24 of round two in a scheduled six-round middleweight contest.

Burrows pressured Herrera and mixed punches to the head and body. With Herrera pinned against the ropes under a sustained attack, referee Ryan Churchill stepped in to end the fight.

Adam Maca overwhelms Rogger Rivera

Adam “The Mac” Maca (7-0, 6 KOs), an Albanian super featherweight based in Brighton, stopped Peru’s Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round bout.

Maca overwhelmed Rivera with power shots until referee Chris Dean intervened. The 19-year-old produced another quick finish, suggesting he is ready for opposition that can offer more resistance.

Paige Murray edges Linzi Buczynskyj

Paige “Perfect” Murray (5-0), of Leicester, defeated Bolton’s Linzi Buczynskyj (6-13) over four two-minute rounds.

Murray controlled the opening round but had a point deducted by referee Chris Dean in the second for repeatedly pulling down Buczynskyj’s head. She won the third and fourth rounds to secure a 38-37 decision.

David Diamante served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Beats Conor Wallace After Late Scare
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a desperate final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, securing the IBF mandatory position at light heavyweight. Whittaker retained his WBC Silver title, but the closing minutes raised questions about his readiness for a world championship fight.

The judges scored it 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. No knockdowns were officially recorded, although Whittaker’s falls during Wallace’s final-round assault became a disputed part of the result.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds, building the lead that ultimately protected his unbeaten record. Wallace could not collect enough rounds early, leaving the Northern Irish-born Australian southpaw needing a dramatic turnaround down the stretch.

He began finding more success in the tenth. With his feet planted, Wallace landed shots that disrupted Whittaker’s rhythm, while the home fighter complained to the referee. Whittaker recovered to take the 11th before Wallace launched his strongest attack in the final round.

Wallace hurt Whittaker and pursued the stoppage, forcing him to grab, stumble and wrestle his way through the remaining time. At one point, Whittaker tackled Wallace as he struggled to stay upright.

Bad Left Hook scored the round 10-8 for Wallace and argued that two or three knockdowns could have been called. Those calls never came, and Whittaker reached the bell with his earlier work enough to secure the decision.

The concern for Whittaker is how little control he had once Wallace hurt him. Holding bought him time, but he struggled to regain his balance or produce enough offense to discourage the pursuit. A stronger finisher could make that escape much harder.

Wallace deserves credit for continuing to press after losing much of the early action. His late surge fell short, but it exposed vulnerabilities that Whittaker and trainer Andy Lee need to address before pursuing the IBF belt held by Dmitry Bivol.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker vs. Conor Wallace Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a punishing final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision, retaining his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and securing the IBF mandatory position for Dmitry Bivol’s belt. The scores were 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113 after 12 rounds in Birmingham.

Whittaker controlled much of the early action, but Wallace hurt him badly in the 12th, leaving him grabbing and struggling to stay upright. No knockdowns were officially scored, although several falls drew criticism over whether Wallace should have received knockdown calls during his late push for a stoppage.

Undercard results

Odel Kamara (1-0) stopped Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) in round three of his professional debut tonight in Birmingham, landing a short uppercut before the referee waved it off. Eddie Hearn rates the 22-year-old junior middleweight highly, but Kamara looked wild swinging for the fences and took unnecessary punches from his overmatched opponent.

The stoppage drew ringside criticism for being premature, and Kamara’s power looked less impressive than the result suggests. At 5’8″, he could be better suited to welterweight, although his stocky build leaves a question over whether he can comfortably make 147 pounds.

Hamza Uddin (8-0) stopped Sean Bruce (8-3) at 2:49 of round eight to capture the British flyweight title and vacant Commonwealth belt at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The 23-year-old from Walsall scored three knockdowns, finishing Bruce with a body shot near the ropes.

Bruce doubled over and went down, prompting referee Victor Loughlin to wave off the contest without starting a count. Uddin picked apart the champion with accurate punching, producing an impressive performance in his first British title fight. Bruce lost his belt in his first defense and could not withstand Uddin’s precision or sustained attack.

Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles by stopping Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of round eight in Birmingham. A heavy right hand sent James to the canvas near the ropes, and another knockdown brought the referee’s intervention.

The 38-year-old Fawaz delivered the finish just as commentary suggested he was beginning to feel the pace. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz earned the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

English super featherweight champion Ibraheem Sulaimaan retained his title with a hard-fought unanimous decision over Sonny Hardy after 10 rounds at Utilita Arena Birmingham. The scores were 97–93, 97–93 and 96–93, moving the Birmingham southpaw to 12–0 and handing Hardy his first defeat at 12–1.

Sulaimaan started quickly, but Hardy pushed him through a difficult stretch in the middle rounds, knocking his gumshield out during one exchange. The champion also had a point deducted before recovering his momentum in the eighth and finishing strongly over the final three rounds. Several ringside observers scored the contest considerably closer than the official judges, with some favoring Hardy.

Aaron Bowen (9-1) captured the Midlands Area super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Klinton Baptiste (5-1) at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92 after 10 rounds.

Bowen controlled the fight, catching Baptiste with clean right hands against the ropes and pressing for a stoppage. Baptiste fought with one eye closed for roughly half the contest but lasted the distance without a reported knockdown.

The punishment prompted ringside criticism that his corner should have intervened, although his durability kept Bowen from securing the finish. Bowen earned a clear victory, while Baptiste’s resistance made the closing rounds harder than the wide scores might suggest. Baptiste looked gone on a couple of occasions, but surprisingly, he stayed in there.

Super featherweight Adam Maca (7-0, 6 KOs) stopped Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round contest. The 19-year-old unloaded with power shots until referee Chris Dean stepped in to end the fight. It was Maca’s sixth stoppage in seven professional outings.

The teenager produced another impressive finish, but he is making this level of opposition look too easy. Rivera offered little opportunity to assess how Maca handles resistance or adjusts when his power alone cannot settle a fight. Maca looks ready for better opposition that can extend him and give him more to solve.

Harley Burrows stopped Matias Ezequiel Herrera at 1:24 of round two in their scheduled six-round middleweight contest on the Ben Whittaker–Conor Wallace undercard in Birmingham. The 20-year-old southpaw pressured Herrera from the opening bell, mixing punches to the head and body.

Burrows trapped the Argentine against the ropes in the second round and punched through his high guard until referee Ryan Churchill intervened. Herrera had not been knocked down before the stoppage, which drew some ringside criticism for being slightly early. Burrows’ attack was wild at times, but his sustained pressure kept Herrera struggling to find room to respond.

The DAZN broadcast starts at 2:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. UK, with a subscription required. That is the card’s start time; Whittaker and Wallace fight later in the evening.

Whittaker has a chance to move within reach of a world title shot, but he must first get through Wallace over the scheduled 12 rounds. British title fights involving Sean Bruce and Bilal Fawaz feature on the undercard.

Ghana News.title: Adom FM Y2K Jam delivers a night of music, fashion and nostalgia
Ghana News.content:
The La Palm Dome at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel came alive on October 2 as music lovers gathered for the Adom FM Y2K Jam, a night of music, fashion and nostalgia.

From the moment patrons arrived at the venue, the atmosphere was filled with excitement as revellers turned up in stylish outfits inspired by the 1990s and early 2000s.



The colourful fashion choices added to the nostalgic feel of the event, with patrons embracing the theme and putting their own spin on the iconic styles of the era.

The venue was packed with music lovers, with many showing up in their best outfits and ready to dance the night away.

The music was at the heart of the celebration, with a selection of popular hits from the 1990s and 2000s keeping patrons on their feet throughout the night.

DJ Andy Dosty took centre stage as the main DJ for the night, serving patrons a rich mix of nostalgic hits that had many singing along and dancing to familiar tunes.

Keeping the energy high was hypeman Mercury Quaye, who constantly engaged the crowd and ensured that the excitement never dropped.

Several other DJs and performers also took turns entertaining patrons, adding variety to the night’s entertainment.

The event also featured energetic dance performances, with dancers showcasing impressive moves to some of the biggest songs from the era.

Their performances drew cheers from the crowd and further heightened the party atmosphere at the La Palm Dome.

As the night progressed, patrons continued to dance, sing along and celebrate the music that shaped an era.

The combination of nostalgic music, themed fashion, DJ performances, dancing and lively crowd interactions created an atmosphere of celebration that lasted into the early hours.

For many patrons, the Adom FM Y2K Jam was more than just a party. It was an opportunity to reconnect with the sounds, fashion and memories of a beloved era.

By the end of the night, one thing was clear — the Adom FM Y2K Jam delivered a full night of music, entertainment and nostalgia, with patrons partying from start to finish.

Ghana News.title: Bel-Aqua intensifies mental well-being campaign ahead of 15th anniversary
Ghana News.content:
Bel-Aqua Mineral Water is intensifying its mental wellbeing campaign as the company prepares to mark its 15th anniversary on October 10.

On Saturday, the company organised a health walk from Ayi Mensah to Peduase, bringing together individuals and corporate teams for exercise and other activities.

Participants later gathered at the Peduase Methodist School for games, health screening and access to psychologists and psychiatrists.

Head of Marketing at Bel-Aqua Mineral Water, Chris Addo Sarkodie, says the company is taking the initiative beyond its annual activities by engaging workers directly in their workplaces.

“So now moving to corporate Ghana, where we are now taking and bearing the cost of psychologists and psychiatrists into companies where they are meeting with their staff and all that.

“And now another leg of it is where we are organising this health walk every year to ensure that people can de-stress and have these conversations because there are psychologists around.”

He says the company wants to make conversations around mental health more common and give people an opportunity to discuss the challenges they face.

“But we want to make sure that we make mental health a discussion. And that’s the reason why we’ve taken it one step further from organising a yearly activity, of having psychologists and psychiatrists and people coming to have that discussion.”

According to Chris Addo Sarkodie, the company is also looking beyond awareness by working towards a helpline that can connect people to professional support.

“So very soon, we’ll be launching our helpline in conjunction with some of the mental health facilities.

“I don’t want to put their name out, but this is something that, from management level, we are very keen on in supporting Ghanaians.”

He says the helpline will be announced once the arrangements with the mental health facilities are finalised.

Bel-Aqua Mineral Water will mark its 15th anniversary on October 10, with the mental wellbeing campaign forming part of its activities around the milestone.

Ghana News.title: From banking to party finances: Alfred Kwadwo Thompson elected NPP Treasurer
Ghana News.content:
Alfred Kwadwo Thompson has been elected National Treasurer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), securing 2,243 votes at the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi.

The election was held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, 2026, as the NPP completed the election of its new national executive team ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Thompson brings extensive experience in banking and finance to the position, having worked with several financial institutions during his career.

Banking career

He began his banking career at the Agricultural Development Bank (ADB), where he worked in the Foreign Operations Department.

Within a year, he was appointed Head of the Trade Finance Unit and the Customer Service Unit before later becoming Manager of Business Development and Marketing Communications in the Corporate and Customer Relations Department.

He subsequently joined Standard Trust Bank, now United Bank for Africa (UBA), as Deputy Head in charge of Foreign Operations.

He also served as Deputy Managing Director of the National Investment Bank (NIB).

Thompson holds a Master’s degree in Marketing from the University of Lincolnshire and Humberside and completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Hull’s School of Business Studies.

Advocate for financial discipline

Thompson has also been active on the NPP’s Communications Team, regularly commenting on governance and economic issues.

He has consistently advocated fiscal discipline and greater accountability in public spending.

In March 2026, he warned that unchecked borrowing and non-transparent spending could threaten the country’s economic stability, while urging the government to prioritise value-for-money projects.

He has also raised concerns about public procurement, including a sole-sourced contract awarded by GoldBod for laptops and office renovation, questioning aspects of the procurement process and alleging a possible conflict of interest.

On illegal mining, Thompson has described galamsey as a national security issue, warning about the consequences of violence associated with the activity.

Youth and civic leadership

His leadership experience extends beyond banking and partisan politics.

Thompson previously served as National President of the Ghana United Nations Students and Youth Association (GUNSA).

He also served as National Coordinator for Life-Link Ghana and the International Students Movement for the United Nations (ISMUN).

His civic involvement includes membership of Rotary International’s Accra Labone Chapter, where he rose through the leadership ranks to become Chapter President.

Thompson hails from Twidan Ebusua in Cape Coast and is a descendant of Tufuhen Moore of Sumpa Fie and the King family of Jerusalem Street, Abowinmu.

He attended St Augustine’s College in Cape Coast and Okuapemman School in Akropong-Akuapem.

As National Treasurer, Thompson joins the NPP’s new national executive team as the party reorganises ahead of the 2028 general elections.

His background in banking and his advocacy for financial accountability are expected to be central to his role as he takes up responsibility for the party’s financial affairs.

Ghana News.title: Ali Suraj elected NPP NASARA Coordinator
Ghana News.content:
Ali Suraj has been elected the National NASARA Coordinator of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

He secured 372 votes to win the contest at the party’s National Delegates Conference held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3.

He defeated Salim Bamba, who polled 311 votes, and Awal Mohamed, who obtained 106 votes.

Ali Suraj’s election comes as the NPP seeks to strengthen its internal structures and broaden its engagement with Muslim communities and other minority groups ahead of the 2028 general elections.

The NASARA Coordinator is responsible for leading the party’s NASARA wing, which focuses on mobilising and coordinating support among minority groups within the NPP.

John Boadu was elected National Chairman after polling 2,888 votes, defeating Boakye Kyerematen Agyarko, who obtained 2,408 votes. Former National Chairman Paul Afoko received 790 votes, while Sammy Crabbe polled 41.

Justin Kodua Frimpong retained the General Secretary position with 4,486 votes.

Daniel Titus Glover was elected National Organiser with 2,964 votes, while Alfred Kwajo Thompson was elected National Treasurer with 2,243 votes.

Three National Vice Chairpersons were also elected from a field of 13 candidates.

Kojo Fosu was elected First Vice Chairman, Henry Nana Boakye was elected Second Vice Chairman, and Nana Akomea was elected Third Vice Chairman.

Boadu emerged 1st Vice Chairman with 3,116 votes, while Henry Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, secured the Second Vice Chairman position with 3,061 votes, and Nana Akomea was elected Third Vice Chairman with 2,981 votes.

Dennis Edward Miracles Aboagye was elected National Communications Director unopposed.

In the special wing positions, Abanga Yakubu Fuseni emerged as National Youth Organiser, while Hawa Koomson was elected National Women’s Organiser.

Mohammed Ali Suraj won the National Nasara Organiser position after securing 372 votes, compared with Salim Mansuru Bamba’s 311 and Awal Mohammed’s 106.

Alfred Kwadwo Thompson was also elected as the party's National Treasurer.

The delegates’ conference brought together 7,163 delegates from across the country to participate in the election of the party’s national officers.

Ghana News.title: Mustapha Hamid misses out on NPP Vice Chairmanship by 31 votes despite early poll lead
Ghana News.content:
Former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive, Dr Mustapha Abdul-Hamid, has missed out on the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Vice Chairmanship, finishing fourth in a closely contested race.

Dr Hamid polled 2,956 votes, falling just 31 votes short of Nana Akomea, who secured the third and final Vice Chairmanship slot with 2,987 votes.

Kojo Fosu Boadu emerged as First Vice Chairman with 3,116 votes, while Henry Nana Boakye was elected Second Vice Chairman with 3,061 votes.

The result marks a significant reversal for Dr Hamid, who had emerged as the leading candidate in an earlier opinion poll.

A Global InfoAnalytics poll released on September 1, 2026, placed Dr Hamid at the top of the Vice Chairmanship race with 18.3% of voter preference.

He was followed by Henry Nana Boakye and Nana Akomea, who both recorded 17.5%.

Kojo Fosu Boadu, who eventually topped the actual election, was fourth in the poll with 5.6%.

The poll surveyed 2,581 respondents across all 16 regions, with a reported margin of error of ±1.9 percentage points.

Dr Hamid has held several senior positions in government and the NPP.

He served as Minister for Information under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo from 2017 before becoming Minister for Inner City and Zongo Development.

In 2021, he was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the NPA, a position he held until the end of the Akufo-Addo administration in January 2025.

An academic by training, Dr Hamid holds a PhD in Religious Studies from the University of Cape Coast and previously lectured at the university’s Department of Religion and Human Values.

His defeat comes as the NPP has elected a new national executive team to lead the party for the next four years.

John Boadu was elected National Chairman, while Justin Frimpong Kodua retained the position of General Secretary.

Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover was elected National Organiser.

The new executives are expected to lead the party as it reorganises ahead of the 2028 general election.

Ghana News.title: Kojo Bamba, Henry Nana Boakye and Nana Akomea elected NPP Vice Chairmen
Ghana News.content:
Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, has been elected First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) after topping the party’s Vice Chairmanship contest with 3,116 votes.

He will be joined in the party’s new leadership by Henry Nana Boakye, who secured the Second Vice Chairmanship with 3,061 votes, and Nana Akomea, who polled 2,987 votes to become Third Vice Chairman.

The three emerged from a field of 13 candidates who contested the three Vice Chairmanship positions at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi.

The results were declared by the Electoral Commission, which supervised the elections.

Mr Boadu’s 3,116 votes placed him ahead of former Health Minister Mustapha Hamid, who obtained 2,956 votes.

Other candidates included Yaa Amponsah Frimpong, who polled 1,503 votes; Richard Ahiagbah, 1,001; Alhaji Masawud Osman, 890; George Kwabena Abankwa Yeboah, 247; Abena Pokuaa Amoah, 194; Richard Oti Aboagye, 152; Samuel Pyne, 206; and Bright Asirifi Kumi, 51.

Mr Boadu campaigned on a message of strengthening the party’s grassroots structures, arguing that constituency executives are central to the NPP’s efforts to regain power in the 2028 general election.

He described constituency executives as the party’s “frontline soldiers” who mobilise supporters and protect polling stations during elections.

“These constituency executives are the ones who work for power to be attained, but they are often sidelined when power is attained. This is why I want to be down there at the grassroots at this critical moment,” he said during his campaign.

The election of the three Vice Chairmen forms part of a broader reshaping of the NPP’s national executive leadership.

John Boadu was elected National Chairman after polling 2,888 votes, defeating Boakye Kyerematen Agyarko, who obtained 2,408 votes.

Former National Chairman Paul Afoko received 790 votes, while Sammy Crabbe polled 41.

Justin Kodua Frimpong retained the General Secretary position with 4,486 votes.

The new Vice Chairmen will work alongside the other national executives as the NPP begins preparations for the 2028 general election.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Bosnia votes in one of world’s most complicated general elections
World.content:
Voters cast their ballots for a dizzying number of officials across multiple tiers of government.

Share Bosnia votes in one of world’s most complicated general elections on social media

Polls have opened in Bosnia and Herzegovina for a general election to choose new leaders at the national and regional levels, in a vote that could affect the country’s European Union membership bid.

On Saturday, about 3.4 million voters are choosing the three members of the country’s multiethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national Parliament and heads of institutions for the country’s two entities: the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH) and Republika Srpska, which is dominated by ethnic Serbs.

Bosnia’s complex web of governing institutions was created by a United States-brokered peace agreement in 1995 in an effort to manage the ethnic divisions between Muslim Bosniaks, Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats that gave rise to the 1992-95 war.

The major parties’ repeated focus on war-era rhetoric and division was frustrating for some voters, activist Adi Selman of the Karton Revolucija protest group told the AFP news agency.

“I don’t think these new elections in Bosnia will change anything,” the 34-year-old said in the northern Bosnian town of Tuzla, ahead of the vote.

“The choice is limited to political parties that have already been around for 30 years and basically pick up votes by harping on about war, tensions, divisions and the past.”

“Bosnia and Herzegovina is dead; it is an impossible country,” Republika Srpska’s former president, Milorad Dodik, told the final rally of his right-wing Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD) in the entity’s capital Banja Luka late on Friday.



EU membership bid

In the FBiH, Bosniak parties are pushing for a stronger central state, with incumbent Bosniak presidency member Denis Becirovic pledging a renewed path to the EU and NATO.

The EU granted Bosnia candidate status in December 2022, but accession negotiations scheduled for 2024 were delayed as Brussels demanded the country pass stronger anticorruption laws and reform its judicial system.

Croat nationalist parties are also pushing for electoral reform, demanding a greater say in choosing the Croat member of the presidency in the entity they share with the more numerous Bosniaks.

Meanwhile, Russia is accused of slowing down the country’s path towards joining the EU, while also holding close ties with the SNSD, which favours secession for Republika Srpska.

This general election is the first in the country in which new electronic tools are being used to scan ballot papers and carry out biometric fingerprint verification in a move to reduce fraud during the election.

Polls close at 7pm (17:00 GMT) and first results are expected later on Sunday.
