World.content:
Share Inside the ‘kill box’: The Yemenis who stayed behind in Houthi-held Mocha on social media

Nabil watched from his balcony as a column of displaced people passed by at dawn on September 10, hours before Houthi forces entered Mocha, a Yemeni city on the Red Sea.

“People were terrified. There was fear everywhere,” he said.

Nabil, a daily wage labourer in his 40s, did not join them. He still lives in Yakhtul, a village north of Mocha, alongside relatives, none of whom has left their homes.

“Displacement is humiliation and homelessness,” he said. “I haven’t done anything wrong, so I have nothing to be afraid of, and I don’t belong to any side.”

Weeks after the Houthis took Mocha from forces loyal to Yemen’s internationally recognised government, thousands of civilians remain in the district. The Houthis – an armed group that has controlled much of northern Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa, since September 2014 – have fought the government for more than a decade in a civil war that has drawn in a Saudi-led military coalition. No one knows how many people remain in Mocha, but according to Yemen’s last census in 2004 the city had 62,500 residents.

The government has declared Mocha a military zone and alleged that the Houthis have forced residents to demonstrate in support of the group or join its ranks.

Residents interviewed by Al Jazeera did not describe forced demonstrations, but one who asked not to be identified because he feared for his safety said three of his neighbours have been recruited and armed by the Houthis. They are now on the front lines fighting against government forces.



“Today my wife heard from a woman who came to our house that a Houthi-armed pick-up truck had kept coming to their home, wanting to recruit her sons, but she refused,” he said. “I know these people. They are our neighbours. One of her sons even spoke to me about it himself.”

The truck left after she refused, he said.

A refuge emptied

Mocha’s port lies about 75km (45 miles) north of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a chokepoint for Red Sea shipping that the Houthis have repeatedly targeted since late 2023.

After government-aligned forces recaptured Mocha in 2017, the city became a refuge for Yemenis fleeing Houthi-controlled territory.

That changed in early September when fighting moved down the coast and families fled towards Aden, Taiz and Lahij. Many had already escaped Houthi rule once before.

On the evening of September 10, the government declared Mocha and its surroundings a “kill box”, a strike zone, warning that any Houthi movement there would be met with available firepower. Attacks began the following day.

Now residents say that leaving Mocha is almost impossible. “After the kill box was declared, the government opened the old al-Barh road so people could leave,” said Fuad, a 27-year-old pharmacist.

“Some got out, some were prevented by the Houthis and some stayed home, fearing the hardship of displacement.”

The Houthis have imposed a nighttime curfew on the city. Prices have soared, and power cuts have grown frequent, Nabil said.

A cooking gas cylinder has more than doubled in price to about 20,000 rials ($13), and a 50kg (110lb) sack of flour has risen by 8,000 rials ($5).

“A day’s work barely covers petrol and lunch,” he said. “Children have stopped going to school.”

Classrooms remain largely empty. “Parents and students are afraid of shelling or of their sons being thrown onto the front lines,” said Mansour, a teacher at a government secondary school who could not afford to flee with his family of seven.

“I am a teacher. I have nothing to do with politics,” he said. “In the end, we only die once.”

For Umm Khaled, a woman in her 60s whose husband is disabled and bedridden, leaving Mocha was never an option. “Where would I flee to? Look at my situation,” she said.

Her son, who had supported the family by fishing, joined the government-aligned National Resistance Forces for a monthly salary of 1,000 Saudi riyals ($267). He fled with them as the Houthis advanced, leaving behind his wife and two children, aged 15 and nine, in her care.



“Now they have fled, and we are lost,” she said. The local grocer has stopped extending credit, and the family survives on a sack of flour distributed by an aid group before the takeover. “Someone brings a fish, someone brings a yogurt and the rest is up to God,” she added.

Hassan, a 40-year-old fisherman who supports nine people, said he could not afford to leave the city. A ride to nearby Taiz costs up to 200,000 rials ($128). “Where would I go when I don’t even have my daily bread?” he asked.

Attacks and collapsed healthcare

Civilians have also been killed in the “kill zone”.

Before dawn on September 22, the bombing of a house in Mocha killed six members of one family, according to Mahmoud al-Otmi, a journalist with Saudi-owned Al-Hadath news channel whose relatives died.

Houthi-run media blamed Saudi air strikes. Saudi Arabia has not commented publicly.

Colonel Abdulbaset al-Bahr, deputy head of moral guidance in the government’s Taiz military command, said the kill box targets Houthi fighters.

“The kill box is for killing the militia, not civilians,” he said. “The statement did not ask civilians to leave the kill box area. Rather it asked them to stay in their homes and keep away from the militia’s barracks, positions and military gatherings.”

Sultan Mahmoud, the government-appointed director of the Mocha district, said no route out of the city was entirely safe as he accused the Houthis of targeting civilians.

Healthcare has nearly collapsed. On the day Houthi forces entered the city, Doctors Without Borders, also known by its French acronym MSF, said nearly all health facilities except Mocha General Hospital had stopped functioning. This was largely because staff had fled although about 30 health workers stayed behind, MSF told The National newspaper.

Residents said conditions in Mocha have since worsened.

“Doctors who were paid by organisations have stopped working because there are no salaries,” Nabil said. Fuad said the Houthis had placed hospitals under a security cordon and some medical equipment had been moved to Sanaa.

Aid has barely reached those who have stayed. Najib al-Saadi, head of the government’s executive unit for displacement camps, said his unit could not reach those in need.

“It is certain that there are families who could not flee because of poverty,” he said, accusing the Houthis of blocking humanitarian work. The International Committee of the Red Cross declined to comment.

In Yakhtul, Nabil said he would not leave, even if the fighting intensifies. “First, money is an obstacle,” he said. “And the house would be looted.”

This story was published in collaboration with Egab.

World.title: Sabalenka, Rybakina handed shock defeats at China Open tennis
World.content:
The Belarusian’s exit follows top seed Rybakina losing to unseeded Charaeva in her first match as world number one.

Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open, leaving the event without its top two seeds as world number one Elena Rybakina was ousted in the second round.

Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes on Sunday.

“I focused on myself, to be calm,” Bartunkova said.

“She’s a legend … so I’m really happy that I won the match,” she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.

Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.

Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.

The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Elena Rybakina – who replaced Sabalenka as the world number one last month – was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round.

Top seed Alexander Zverev was scheduled to play Novak Djokovic later on Sunday in the quarterfinals of the men’s 500-level event also taking place.

The 39-year-old Serbian great enters the match with an extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing, but Zverev — last month’s US Open champion — is in the running for the top men’s ranking.

World.title: Gaza’s Christians mourn mother and daughter killed in Israeli attack
World.content:
Maysa Abu Daoud and her daughter Mary al-Najjar among five Palestinians killed in Gaza City attack.

Funeral held at Gaza church for mother and daughter killed in Israeli strike

The Latin patriarch of Jerusalem, Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, has expressed his “deep sorrow and grief” over the “tragic” killing of two Christian women in an Israeli air attack on Gaza City.

Maysa Abu Daoud and her daughter Mary al-Najjar were among five Palestinians killed in the attack that hit the ground floor of a building in the Remal neighbourhood on Saturday, in the latest Israeli violation of a United States-brokered “ceasefire” agreement with the Palestinian group Hamas.

In a statement, the patriarch extended his “heartfelt condolences” to the loved ones of the two women and to the Christian community in Gaza.

Their funeral took place on Saturday at Saint Porphyrius Church in Gaza City’s Old City.

The two women were Palestinian Christians from Gaza City who devoted their time to helping parishioners and displaced people sheltering at the Holy Family Church, according to Palestine’s Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs.

The committee’s chairman, Ramzi Khoury, described their deaths as a “painful loss” for their families, the church and its parishioners.

Mary’s son, 14-year-old Fouad al-Najjar, told the Anadolu news agency the strike hit the building at about 1:30am (22:30 GMT).

“My grandmother and my mother died. May God have mercy on them,” he said.

Al-Najjar appealed for an end to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, saying Palestinians were losing their loved ones every day.



“We are exhausted by this war and have endured so much,” he said. “For almost three years, we have been living through the same destruction, the same grief and the same war.”

Palestinian Lutheran pastor Munther Isaac, who serves in Ramallah and directs the Bethlehem Institute for Peace and Justice, wrote on X: “The genocide continues in Gaza.”

The Gaza Strip is home to fewer than 1,000 Christians. The community was already small before the war, and many of its members have been killed since then in attacks on their homes and churches throughout the war that began in October 2023.

On October 19, 2023, an attack on the Saint Porphyrius Church compound killed at least 18 people. Two months later, the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem said an Israeli sniper shot dead a woman and her daughter inside the Holy Family parish compound in Gaza.

An Israeli strike on the Holy Family Catholic Church compound on July 17, 2025 also killed three people and wounded others, including parish priest Father Gabriel Romanelli.

According to the Ministry of Health in Gaza, Israeli attacks have killed at least 74,228 people, including at least 1,445 since the start of the “ceasefire” in October 2025.

World.title: Saudi-led coalition dismisses ‘misleading’ Houthi claim of Riyadh attack
World.content:
The Saudi-led coalition spokesman says the Yemeni armed group is ‘attempting to divert attention’ from its losses.

The Houthis’ claims that the Iran-allied armed group has targeted Saudi Arabia’s capital Riyadh are “misleading”, according to the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki’s remarks came on Saturday after the Houthis claimed ballistic missile and drone attacks on an Aramco oil facility near Riyadh.

The group said the assault caused large fires as fighting between the Houthis and government forces intensifies in Yemen.

In remarks carried by Saudi media Asharq Al-Awsat late on Saturday, al-Maliki claimed that the Houthis are “attempting to divert attention from the scale of the losses and the growing public anger against them”.

‘Chaos and devastation’

The development comes after the Yemeni forces “executed 257 precision targeting operations” against Houthi sites, movements, and military capabilities on Saturday, according to the spokesman for Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces, Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili.

He added that initial estimates indicate that the operations killed at least 700 Houthi rebels.

Meanwhile, al-Maliki said the Houthis’ “ties to external agendas” have brought “chaos and devastation to Yemen”, adding that “what the Houthis are facing in Taiz … drive them to seek illusory victories”.

Early on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said its armed forces carried out 97 “precise targeting operations” against Houthi reinforcements on the Tor al-Baha front and the Taiz axis, using warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers.



The fighting between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces has intensified since a fragile 2022 truce collapsed in July, displacing hundreds of thousands of people since then.

In mid-September, the Houthis seized the port city of Mocha and strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a vital route for global oil shipments, before anti-Houthi forces stabilised front lines.

Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, forcing the Yemeni government to retreat to Aden.

World.title: Fury to invite US President Trump to lead ring walk before Joshua fight
World.content:
Tyson Fury is keen for his ‘old pal’ to join his procession to the ring for the fight on December 11 in Cardiff.

Share Fury to invite US President Trump to lead ring walk before Joshua fight on social media

Former boxing heavyweight champion Tyson Fury says he will invite United States President Donald Trump to lead his ring walk before his highly anticipated bout with British rival Anthony Joshua.

“I’ll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we’ll see if he’s available,” Fury was quoted as saying by British media on Saturday.

“Probably unlikely because of the situation he’s in at the moment, being the president of the United States.”

Fury and Joshua are set to fight in Cardiff on December 11 and the self-styled “Gypsy King” is keen for Trump to join the procession to the ring at the 80,000-capacity Principality Stadium.

Fury met Trump at the UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in June and wore a cap emblazoned with the words “Donald Trump for Prime Minister” after having his US travel ban lifted by the 80-year-old.

Fury insists his clash with Joshua is merely preparation for his true priority — a trilogy fight against Oleksandr Usyk, who has beaten him twice already.

“I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this as a warm-up for Usyk,” he said.

“I can guarantee that on the night when I knock him spark out, he won’t know what time it is. And then I want the rabbit [Usyk] in New York City.

“This year will be the most active year for me since 2018. I’ve done 12 rounds with a 6-foot-8-inch [262cm] Arslanbek Makhmudov, and I’ve done seven rounds with another 6ft-7in behemoth in Mariusz Wach.



“Let’s not pull any punches here. I’m firing on all cylinders at the moment. I feel fantastic. I’m 38 years young.”

World.title: Yamal scores stunning goal in Spain’s 3-1 Nations League win over Czechia
World.content:
Lamine Yamal is the first player to score within the first 10 minutes of each of three consecutive men’s football games.

Lamine Yamal has carried on his superb goal-scoring form, helping Spain secure a 3-1 win over Czechia in the UEFA Nations League and consolidating his bid to win the prestigious Ballon d’Or award later this month.

The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3 after Thomas Tuchel’s side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier in Rijeka on Saturday.

Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and captain Rodri Hernandez on target, but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go.

However, Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain’s win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs, as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July.

Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain’s first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth minute before breaking the deadlock. He is the first player to score a goal within the first 10 minutes of three consecutive men’s international matches.

“They are well-drilled; I thought it would be one of the hardest games, and that’s how it was,” Rodri told a Spanish broadcaster after Spain claimed a third win from three group games.

“It was tricky but we got some chances. There are some matches in which you can’t generate that much, but the team was able to manage the match.”

The former Manchester City midfielder scored for the first time for Spain in more than two years.

“It’s always special to score for the national team. I’d not been scoring many goals; let’s see if I’ve found that dynamic – it’s important, we all have to chip in with the goals,” he added.



Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday’s win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez.

It was one of Spain’s star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of.

The 19-year-old winger, a leading candidate for the Ballon d’Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curling into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot.

“We’re doing well; I’m very happy. I was eager to return to the national team after the World Cup, and there’s no better way than this,” said Yamal.

Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal’s superb strike, his 12th in his last nine games for club and country.

“I think he never stops surprising us – I think all of us. He has so much talent, so much quality, that we still haven’t seen the best version of Lamine by a long shot,” said De la Fuente.

“He has a lot more to offer because he’s so classy, so talented, with so much potential.”

The winger’s Barcelona teammate, Rodri, doubled Spain’s lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him.

De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday’s visit to face Croatia, and the pace of the game slowed.

The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in.

Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise.

Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home, but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand.

Czechia’s determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci’s red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez, before Merino rounded off Spain’s win.

World.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
World.content:
A major bridge in Kyiv has been targeted by Russian strikes for the second day in a row, coinciding with a surprise visit from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's to the city.

The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was hit on Sunday morning, a day after it was first struck by drones in an attack that damaged the road surface and led to traffic disruption.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Sunday's strike had also damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.

Major bridges have been targeted in Kyiv over the past four days as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in the capital.

Unverified video footage of Sunday's strike shows cars moving on the bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge.

Klitschko reported the strike on Telegram, writing: "Hitting the roadway on the North Bridge. Emergency services are on their way to the scene."

As emergency services responded to the incident, Germany's Merz reaffirmed his country's support for Ukraine and pledged further assistance to bolster Ukrainian air defences.

He wrote on X: "Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.

"Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well."

World.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
World.content:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.

In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".

The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".

Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.

Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
World.content:
The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday.

Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.

Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said.

Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

Attorneys for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now".

"What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."

Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.

Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.

The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

World.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
World.content:
Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.

In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".

The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.

She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid.

Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.

Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better".

"We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.

He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".

Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history.

"We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said.

On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation.

World.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
World.content:
Tens of thousands of people have protested across Spain calling for greater protections for tenants after the government failed to pass emergency housing legislation.

About 50 marches took place on Saturday in cities including Madrid, Valencia and Barcelona.

"There is a lot of anger in the streets," a spokesperson for the Valencia Tenants' Union said. Clashes have taken place between some protesters and police in the city.

The measures put forward by Pedro SÃ¡nchez's leftist coalition government on Friday followed public outcry over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home last month after she was unable to afford a sharp rent increase.

Her eviction triggered nationwide protests across Spain with protesters demanding lower rents, an end to evictions, and a ban on investment funds - or "vulture funds" as the government has termed them - buying property.

Sanchez's defeat in Congress on Friday heightens speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.

His coalition government, made up of his ruling Socialist party and junior partner the Sumar alliance, does not command a majority in parliament.

World.title: What to know about Brazil's election pitting Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro
World.content:
Lula, the 80-year-old candidate for the left-wing Workers' Party, has been president three times already.

He served two consecutive terms - from January 2003 to December 2010 - and was widely praised for lifting millions out of poverty during this time with the help of a cash-transfer programme called Bolsa FamÃ­lia.

The former metalworker left office with record approval ratings of over 80%, but his party was later rocked by huge corruption scandals.

Lula himself spent more than 18 months in prison between 2018 and 2019 after being convicted of corruption and money laundering, charges he has always denied.

Those convictions were annulled in 2021, leaving Lula free to run for the presidency in the 2022 election, in which he beat Jair Bolsonaro by 1.8 percentage points.

When he started his third term in office, he vowed it would be his last, and yet his party endorsed him as their candidate again this year, even though he will turn 81 later this month.

There is no doubt he remains a towering figure in the left. But while his supporters described him ahead of the 2022 election as the "saviour of the Amazon", praising his commitment to protecting the rainforest, some environmentalists have been critical of some of his recent actions.

His support for exploratory oil drilling in offshore waters near the mouth of the Amazon in particular has drawn criticism.

Lula insists that he remains committed to eventually phasing out fossil fuels and argues that oil revenues are key to financing Brazil's transition to clean energy.

His government has also pointed to the reduction in deforestation in the Amazon - satellite data suggests the area deforested in the first half of 2026 was reduced to its lowest in the past decade - as proof that its policies were working.

During Lula's latest term in office, relations with his US counterpart Donald Trump have been rocky.

Referring to what Trump has dubbed the "Donroe doctrine" - his administration's national security strategy which asserts that US dominance in the Western hemisphere should not be interfered with - Lula has insisted that "Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard".

In another thinly veiled reference to both his rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro and those in the Trump administration who would like to see the right-wing candidate win, the Brazilian leader has also warned that he would not tolerate "foreign and local enemies of democracy" interfering with the polls.

World.title: Debris found from plane that went missing off US coast
World.content:
US authorities have found debris from a medical transport aircraft that went missing with six people on board.

The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday, while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston, Massachusetts.

The search for survivors continues off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, the US Coast Guard said.

Authorities have notified the next of kin of those on the flight, four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals.

"Search crews located a debris field confirmed to be from the aircraft off the coast of Nantucket," the US Coast Guard said in an update on Saturday night. It added that ships, helicopters and planes were involved in searches that would through continue the night.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).

According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.

FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions shows trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?," the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 01:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

The Coast Guard said it would provide an update on Sunday morning local time.

World.title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
World.content:
A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US.

The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to University of Mississippi students.

US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month.

Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom.

The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release.

Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives.

About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives.

Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said.

Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested.

The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin".

Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form.

For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal. But Kratom is not regulated by the US Food and Drug Administration and is legal in some states, including Mississippi.

The Mississippi prosecutors said that kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances in the US and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine.

World.title: Court places restriction on Osun bank accounts
World.content:
The bank accounts of the Osun State Government have again been placed under restriction, some weeks after the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) lifted a freeze on some of the state’s accounts following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention.

Punch reported that the latest restriction followed an application by Gamji Nigeria Company Limited seeking to preserve funds belonging to the state over a $13.9 million arbitration award arising from water infrastructure projects in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

Judge Daniel Osiagor of the Federal High Court in Lagos in a suit marked FHC/L/CS/1233/2026, ordered commercial banks to place a “Post No Debit” restriction on the state government’s accounts.

The order covers funds up to $13.9 million and N157.5 million, pending the hearing and determination of Gamji’s motion on notice.

Affected banks include Guaranty Trust, Access Bank, First HoldCo, Zenith Bank, United Bank for Africa, Ecobank, Fidelity Bank, Stanbic IBTC, Sterling Bank, Union Bank and Wema Bank, among others.

The development comes about months after the EFCC restricted Osun government accounts during the build-up to the 15 August governorship election.

In that earlier case, the anti-graft agency restricted the state’s Federal Allocation Account domiciled with First Bank and two joint allocation accounts with Zenith Bank over an investigation into the alleged handling of about N11 billion in Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and Federation Account Allocation Committee allocations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The EFCC said it acted after detecting what it described as suspicious movements of funds from the accounts, while the Osun government rejected the allegation and described the restriction as politically motivated.

The timing of that restriction became particularly controversial because it occurred 10 days before the governorship election, which Governor Ademola Adeleke contested on the platform of the Accord Party against the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji.

President Tinubu subsequently directed the EFCC to vacate the restriction, saying the timing of the action was capable of creating an impression that a federal agency was being used to interfere with the election. The accounts were eventually unfrozen on 22 August.

The latest restriction, however, is unrelated to the EFCC investigation.

Why the latest accounts were restricted

The latest case arose from two contracts awarded by the Osun State Government then led by former Governor Adegboyega Oyetola (the incumbent minster of marine and blue economy) to Gamji in June 2017 for water infrastructure works in Ilesa West.

One contract involved the construction of transmission mains and booster pump stations, while the second covered the construction of water reservoirs under a water supply and sanitation project.

According to court documents filed by Gamji, the projects were funded through an Islamic Development Bank loan facility facilitated by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

The original value of the first contract was $15.98 million, while the second was valued at $9.70 million.

Gamji said subsequent changes to engineering designs and variations in the scope of the works resulted in delays and increased project costs.

The company said the contract values were subsequently revised to $20.24 million for the first project and $10.95 million for the second.

Gamji further claimed that about 93 per cent of the work had been completed by October 2023 and that the Osun government issued a Substantial Completion Certificate on 14 November 2024.

Disagreements later emerged between the company and the state government over extensions of time, price adjustments and increased costs of materials and labour.

Gamji said its claims were rejected by the state government and that attempts to resolve the dispute through mediation failed.

The company subsequently issued an arbitration notice on 3 April 2025.

The state government accepted the arbitration process and nominated its arbitrator, leading to preliminary proceedings in Lagos on 15 May 2025.

According to Punch’s report, the arbitral panel eventually issued its final award on 24 July 2026, directing the Osun government to pay Gamji $13 million and N157.5 million in reimbursable arbitration fees.

READ ALSO: EFCC unfreezes Osun govt accounts after Tinubus directive

“A preservation order of interim injunction is granted directing the cited financial institutions in Nigeria to immediately place a Post No Debit restriction on the Respondent’s account domiciled with them for the preservation of the funds with them in the sum of $13,924,343.32 and N157,500,000.00 towards the liquidation of the Arbitral Award dated 24th July, 2026 which has become due and enforceable, pending the hearing and determination of the motion on notice,” the order read in part.

The award also provided for 20 per cent annual interest on any outstanding balance after the deadline for compliance.

Gamji told the court that the deadline expired on 24 August without payment of the awarded sums.

It subsequently approached the Federal High Court in Lagos seeking an order to preserve funds in the state government’s accounts pending enforcement of the award.

However, Judge Osiagor granted the interim application and directed the listed banks to place the accounts under “Post No Debit” restriction to preserve funds towards the liquidation of the arbitral award.

The order is interim and does not finally determine the substantive application before the court. The court adjourned the case until 22 October 2026 for hearing of the motion on notice.

The Osun State Government has yet to respond publicly to the court order.

World.title: NPFL Matchday 7: Rangers face derby test as Rivers United close in
World.content:
The Nigeria Premier Football League title race takes another intriguing turn this weekend, as Matchday 7 brings together title contenders, ambitious challengers, and clubs eager to improve their fortunes.

Rangers International have the biggest target on their backs after reclaiming top spot, but the defending champions face a potentially explosive South-East derby against Abia Warriors.

Just one point separates Rangers from unbeaten Rivers United, while Barau FC are also lurking with the same 12-point haul as Rivers.

And behind the leading pack, Enyimba’s emphatic 4-2 victory over Shooting Stars has finally given the Aba giants something to build on, while several clubs at the other end of the table are already feeling the pressure to turn promising performances into points.

With Kano Pillars and Sporting Lagos opening the weekend on Saturday, the rest of Matchday 7 serves up a nine-game Sunday programme that could significantly reshape the standings.

Rangers put top spot and South-East bragging Rights on the Line

Rangers return to action as league leaders, but there will be little room for complacency when they face Abia Warriors in Awka.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Flying Antelopes climbed back to the summit after a crucial 1-0 victory over Warri Wolves in their rescheduled midweek fixture.

It was exactly the response they needed after their previous defeat to Ikorodu City at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena.

Now comes another test, and this one carries the extra spice of a South-East derby, as Abia Warriors arrive with confidence after recording their first home victory of the campaign, a commanding 3-0 triumph over Bendel Insurance.

Imama Amapakabo’s side will believe they can trouble Rangers, particularly after ending their wait for a convincing result.

Recent meetings between the rivals underline how competitive this fixture has become. Rangers have won three of their last six encounters, Abia Warriors have won two, while one ended in a draw.

So while Rangers will be defending first place, Abia Warriors will be chasing much more than three points. This is a derby for momentum, pride and bragging rights.

Meanwhile, another subplot to Rangers’ challenge is that the club continues to play away from its traditional Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium home because of renovation work.

Their home fixtures have already taken them to the MKO Abiola Stadium in Abeokuta and the Dan Anyiam Stadium in Owerri.

This time, the Awka Township Stadium provides the setting. That lack of a permanent home could potentially favour Abia Warriors, who will not have to contend with the intimidating atmosphere Rangers traditionally enjoy at the Cathedral in Enugu.

But Rangers have shown enough resilience to suggest they can overcome the inconvenience; more importantly, they now have the confidence of sitting at the top of the table.

Rivers United: Unbeaten, Second and running out of breathing space

If Rangers are under pressure to stay top, Rivers United are applying it from immediately behind.

The Pride of Rivers remain unbeaten after six matches, with three wins and three draws giving them 12 points, just one behind the leaders. But Sunday’s clash against Ikorodu City presents a different kind of challenge.

Rivers United have been forced into a demanding schedule, with the encounter against Ikorodu City coming after a quick succession of matches against Ranchers Bees and Katsina United.

Their latest outing produced a 1-1 draw against Katsina United at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, as Samson Olasupo put Rivers ahead after the break before former Rivers United midfielder Sani Mubarak’s deflected free-kick restored parity.

Now the Port Harcourt side must find enough energy to maintain their unbeaten start. At this stage of the season, dropping points is not necessarily disastrous.

But when Rangers are only one point ahead, every dropped point gives the leaders a little more breathing space.

With eight points from six matches, the Oga Boys have two wins, two draws and two defeats. A victory against Rivers United would be another major statement and could pull them closer to the leading group.

For Rivers, however, the objective is simple: protect their unbeaten record and keep Rangers within striking distance.

Enyimba finally find their spark

One of the biggest storylines away from the top two comes from Aba, where Enyimba finally got their campaign moving with a thrilling 4-2 victory over Shooting Stars.

For a club of Enyimba’s stature, the opening weeks of the season had been unusually frustrating as the nine-time NPFL champions have struggled badly for goals, points, and consistency. But the emphatic victory in Aba reminded everyone of what they can do when in full flow.

Now they face Plateau United at the Enyimba Stadium. The away side will not arrive merely to admire the surroundings. They come into the contest after beating Inter Lagos 2-0 and will be looking to build on that result.

For Enyimba, however, the challenge is bigger than simply winning another home game. They must prove the Shooting Stars victory was the beginning of a revival rather than an isolated flash of brilliance.

Barau FC looking to keep their unbeaten run alive

Another club demanding attention is Barau FC, as the newcomers have made an impressive start to life in the NPFL and sit among the leading pack after six matches without defeat.

Their next assignment is a trip to Bendel Insurance, who will be desperate for a response after the heavy 3-0 defeat to Abia Warriors.

It sets up an intriguing contest between a Barau side eager to preserve its momentum and an Insurance team determined to restore pride before its supporters.

For Barau, another positive result would further strengthen their credentials as early-season surprise packages.

Kano Pillars held by Sporting Lagos

Matchday 7 began on Saturday with Kano Pillars hosting Sporting Lagos at the Sani Abacha Stadium.

The encounter ended 1-1, with Valentine Ugwu putting Sporting Lagos ahead in first-half stoppage time before Abdullahi Musa equalised three minutes after the restart.

Both sides had chances to claim the points, but neither found a winner. The result extended Sporting Lagos’ unbeaten start and moved them onto eight points.

For Kano Pillars, however, the draw ended an impressive home run, with the Sai Masu Gida having won 10 of their previous 11 home matches before Sporting Lagos arrived.

Sporting Lagos will now turn their attention to Bendel Insurance, while Kano Pillars face another difficult assignment away to Shooting Stars.

The other Sunday battles

The weekend’s remaining fixtures provide their own storylines.

At Pantami Stadium, Doma United will host Warri Wolves, with both sides looking for a result that could change the direction of their campaigns.

In Ibadan, Shooting Stars face Nasarawa United, with the Oluyole Warriors seeking to bounce back from their heavy defeat to Enyimba.

Kwara United will host Ranchers Bees in Ilorin, while Niger Tornadoes welcome Kun Khalifat to Minna. Kun Khalifat arrive with confidence after their 1-0 victory over Kwara United and will look to build on it with another positive result.

In Lagos, Inter Lagos face Katsina United at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, with the hosts seeking to convert home performances into points. And in Aba, Enyimba host Plateau United in a fixture that could tell us whether the People’s Elephant have genuinely turned the corner.

Matchday Seven could change the Picture

The beauty of the NPFL at this stage of the season is that the table remains open enough for one weekend to create major movement.

Rangers have the advantage at the top, but Rivers United are unbeaten and only one point behind. Barau FC are refusing to disappear from the conversation, while Enyimba are suddenly showing signs of life.

Below them, Ikorodu City, Sporting Lagos and several other clubs remain close enough to make a serious push with a run of positive results, making Sunday’s fixtures more than just another round of matches.

For Rangers, it is about protecting the top spot; for Rivers United, maintaining the pressure. While for the people’s Elephant in Aba, it is about proving their revival is real, and for Barau FC, it is about showing their unbeaten start is no fluke.

And for the teams struggling near the wrong end of the table, Matchday 7 is another opportunity to ensure the season does not begin slipping away.

The race is still wide open, and another dramatic chapter is waiting to be written.

World.title: Rev Dachomo in Israel, seeks audience with Netanyahu over killings
World.content:
Ezekiel Dachomo, a Reverend and regional leader of the Church of Christ in Nations (COCIN) in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, has travelled to Israel as part of efforts to draw international attention to killings and insecurity in Plateau and other parts of Nigeria.

Mr Dachomo announced his arrival in Israel on Friday, October 2, on his Facebook account, describing the trip as his first international Christian advocacy tour.

Recent reports also show that he has been using the visit to pray for Nigeria, its leaders and communities affected by violence.

The cleric said he intends to use the visit to highlight attacks affecting communities in Plateau and the wider Middle Belt and seek an audience with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

His stated programme also includes engagements with Christian leaders and prayer groups from different countries, whom he said he hopes to mobilise attention and prayers for Nigeria.

Mr Dachomo has repeatedly spoken publicly about attacks on communities in Plateau and described some of the violence as persecution and “genocide” against Christians.

Those descriptions are his characterisation of the violence and are not presented here as an established finding.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a message announcing his visit, the cleric said he was in Israel to pray for Nigeria, its leaders and its people.

“Today, I am in Israel praying for Nigeria, our leaders, and our people. I believe in miracles, and I believe God can change what looks impossible,” he said.

In a video accompanying his message, Mr Dachomo also said he had prayed for Israel, its people and its leadership, including Mr Netanyahu, his cabinet and the Israel Defence Forces.

He also prayed for President Bola Tinubu, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other African leaders.

The cleric said his advocacy would extend beyond Christian victims of violence, noting that Muslims and other Nigerians affected by insecurity also needed prayers and attention.

“I am coming to stand for Nigeria and to pray for our nation: for Muslims being killed in Zamfara, Kebbi, Sokoto and Katsina; for Christians; for my Biafran brothers,” he said.

Mr Dachomo also referred to attacks in his community and alleged that armed men had invaded his village and killed three people in his jurisdiction.

He said he hoped that, if granted a one-on-one meeting with Mr Netanyahu, he would present what he described as the suffering of Christian communities in Nigeria.

“By God’s grace, if we meet one-on-one in Israel, I will share with him the agony of Christians in Nigeria,” he said.

The Israel trip comes against the backdrop of Mr Dachomo’s sustained advocacy over insecurity in Plateau State.

He has been particularly vocal following attacks on communities in the state, including an attack in July in which he alleged that nine members of his extended family were killed in Riyom Local Government Area.

READ ALSO: Nicki Minaj shares prayer over killings in Plateau

PUNCH reported the allegation and Mr Dachomo’s subsequent public advocacy over the killings.

His latest initiative moves that advocacy beyond Nigeria, with the cleric seeking to engage international Christian groups and draw greater attention to the security challenges confronting communities in Plateau and other parts of the country.

Nigeria’s insecurity has affected communities across religious and ethnic lines, with terrorism, banditry, communal violence, farmer-herder conflicts and criminality among the factors cited in different parts of the country.

Claims concerning the identity of perpetrators, motives and the religious character of individual attacks therefore require independent verification.

For Mr Dachomo, the Israel visit represents an attempt to take his campaign for greater international attention to Plateau’s security crisis beyond Nigeria.

The outcome of his proposed engagements with Israeli officials and international Christian groups will determine the advocacy campaign’s international reach.

World.title: APC vows to mobilise Taraba voters for Tinubu, others in 2027 amid Wike coalition
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Taraba State has vowed to mobilise voters for President Bola Tinubu and other party candidates in the 2027 general elections.

The state APC chairman, Abubakar Bawa, gave the assurance on Saturday in Jalingo during the inauguration of the Taraba chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, a grassroots campaign organisation supporting Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

The declaration comes amid differing approaches among political actors supporting Mr Tinubu, including the Rainbow Coalition promoted by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike.

Mr Wike has said the coalition is primarily aimed at mobilising support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election, while maintaining that the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) remains free to field candidates in governorship, National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections.

Mr Bawa said the APC was confident of its prospects in Taraba and would deploy its structures to secure victory for its candidates at all levels in 2027.

He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would take the party’s message to households and communities across the state.

The campaign group is expected to reach residents through door-to-door engagements as well as mobilisation in churches, mosques and local government areas.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Also speaking at the event, the Director-General of the Tinubu-Shettima campaign organisation in Taraba, Danladi Baido, said the APC would build on its performance in the 2023 presidential election.

Mr Baido expressed confidence that the party would again mobilise substantial support for Mr Tinubu in the state in 2027.

The founder and convener of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, urged Taraba residents to support Mr Tinubu for a second term.

Mr Ekpemupolo said the administration’s reforms needed time to produce lasting results and argued that continuity would help consolidate its policies.

He also linked Mr Tinubu’s re-election to Taraba Governor Agbu Kefas’s development agenda, saying another term for the president would allow the governor to continue implementing his programmes.

Mr Kefas, who backed the mobilisation drive, said residents of Taraba were already witnessing the impact of the Tinubu administration through federal government projects and programmes in the state.

“We are moving forward with the mandate of the Renewed Hope Agenda of Mr President,” the governor said.

He assured the gathering that his administration would continue to execute and commission development projects across the state.

The national coordinator of the movement, Adekanbi Asuku, said the organisation was in Taraba to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu and Mr Kefas.

Mr Asuku urged members to take the campaign to homes, religious centres, wards and local government areas as the 2027 elections approach.

He also attributed improved security in Taraba to the efforts of APC-led administrations and called for continued support for the party.

World.title: Six die in Benue boat mishap despite safety rules
World.content:
Six people have died after a boat carrying mourners capsized on the Buruku River in Buruku Local Government Area of Benue State, months after the state government introduced stricter safety measures for water transport.

The incident occurred around 11 a.m. on Saturday, and iinvolved more than 70 people returning from a burial ceremony.

Raymond Zege, chairman of Buruku Local Government, confirmed the incident to journalists on Saturday, saying the mourners were from neighbouring Gboko Local Government Area.

Mr Zege said the boat’s engine failed, causing passengers to struggle to keep the vessel afloat.

He said another boat attempted to rescue them, but the vessel carrying the mourners encountered strong waves and overturned.

“They were people from Gboko LG. They went for a burial to cross to the other side, but on their way back they overloaded the boat and the engine failed,” he said.

Mr Zege said the passengers panicked while attempting to reach the rescue boat.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“But before they could get to the other boat coming to rescue them, they ran into water waves, and the weight of the boat made it sink,” he said.

He said six people died in the incident.

Safety measures

The accident occurred despite measures introduced by the Benue government in January to strengthen safety on the state’s waterways.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the government announced stricter regulations following the drowning of six students in Buruku after a boat conveying them across the river capsized.

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Security and Internal Affairs, Joseph Har, announced the measures during a meeting with stakeholders, marine workers and security personnel at the Buruku riverbank.

Under the measures, life jackets were made compulsory for passengers, while boat operators were prohibited from overloading their vessels.

The government also restricted river transport to daytime hours, directing that all water transport operations must stop by 8 p.m. daily.

“These measures establish a rigorous safety standard for all river commuters and operators,” Mr Har said.

“Life jackets are now mandatory for every passenger, and operators must not overload their boats under any circumstances.”

Mr Har also directed operators to observe weather conditions and adopt recognised safety practices for inland water transport.

The government said enforcement of the compulsory life-jacket rule would begin fully from 1 February.

Enforcement concerns

Mr Zege said authorities had provided life jackets for people using the river crossing but acknowledged difficulties in enforcing their use.

He said some passengers complained that the jackets were uncomfortable and therefore resisted wearing them.

The latest incident has therefore raised questions about compliance with the safety measures announced by the government earlier in the year.

Mr Har had also disclosed in January that some previously donated life jackets had been vandalised and appealed to local councils and private individuals to support the provision of replacement safety equipment.

The government proposed a joint enforcement team involving the Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, National Inland Waterways Authority and the state Civil Protection Guards.

READ ALSO: Another boat mishap claims 29 lives in Niger

Search and rescue

Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Denis Iyaghigba, said he had received preliminary information about Saturday’s incident.

He said initial reports indicated that a strong water current swept the boat into an abandoned barge at a corner of the river, causing it to overturn.

Mr Iyaghigba urged families of those who may have been aboard the boat to remain calm and await verified information from the relevant authorities.

He said he had directed boat operators and their union to mobilise and assist with the ongoing search and rescue operation.

The incident adds to concerns over safety on Benue’s waterways, particularly in communities that depend on river transport for movement, trade and access to essential services.

World.title: How Tinubu ran Nigeria during four-week trip abroad – Shettima
World.content:
Nigeria’s Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu remained in regular contact with his administration and received updates on developments in the country during his four-week stay abroad.

Mr Shettima disclosed this on Saturday after meeting Mr Tinubu at the president’s residence in Lagos, four days after the President returned to Nigeria from his extended working vacation.

The vice president said, while speaking to journalists after his meeting with Mr Tinubu, that he and Mr Tinubu spoke “almost every other day” throughout the president’s stay abroad, with regular updates on developments in the country.

“We have been in regular contact throughout his sojourn abroad,” Mr Shettima said. “We speak almost every other day, and we are updating him. We are updating him on developments in the nation, and we are happy he’s back on the beat.”

The comments provide an insight into how the administration operated while Mr Tinubu was outside the country for about four weeks, during which the president’s absence generated public discussion amid his failure to hand over to the Vice-President.

The presidency had earlier said Mr Tinubu continued to keep in touch with officials at home and directed the affairs of the country while abroad.

It cited, among other decisions, the president’s directive for an independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 illegal miners in Minna.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Shettima’s account adds that the president was receiving frequent briefings from his administration throughout his absence.

We appreciate pains Nigerians are going through — Shettima

The vice president also used his meeting with Mr Tinubu to defend the administration’s economic policies, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy and the unification of the country’s multiple exchange rates.

He said the decisions were taken when the economy was “teetering on the verge of collapse”, arguing that Mr Tinubu had the courage to implement what he described as far-reaching reforms.

“When we assume the mantle of leadership, our foreign reserves was a staggeringly low $3.9 billion that was not enough to import oil for one month,” Mr Shettima said.

“He saved the economy. I want Nigerians to understand this fundamental truism. We are on the road to Caracas. He saved our economy. He saved the nation from falling to pieces.”

Mr Shettima, however, acknowledged the economic difficulties facing Nigerians and said the government is working on measures to reduce the impact of the hardship.

“We appreciate the pains Nigerians are going through, but tough times do not last forever. Tough people do,” he said.

He announced that the federal government would, in the coming weeks, introduce new transport and logistics initiatives in the North-east, including 10,600 electric tricycles and 300 buses and electric taxis.

He said the initiatives were designed to reduce the burden on Nigerians and “ameliorate the sufferings” of people in the region.

Mr Shettima also described the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as a major intervention for students from poor backgrounds, saying the scheme would help students with limited financial means gain access to higher education.

He said the government would continue to introduce programmes aimed at easing the hardship experienced by Nigerians.

“Politics is in the air, but we will combine politics and governance,” Mr Shettima said.

Mr Tinubu left Nigeria on 30 August for London for a working vacation where he spent a week before travelling to Paris, France where he met French President Emmanuel Macron, businessman Vincent Bolloré and other business leaders during his stay.

He also witnessed the signing of an agreement between the Ogun State Government and DP World for a proposed deep seaport and economic zone in Ogun Waterside.

The president returned to Nigeria on 29 September, arriving at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos ahead of Nigeria’s 66th independence celebration.

The president dismissed the concerns about his health as political rumour, and said he is healthy and ready to resume duties.

“Rumor will always be emanating from politics, but the facts remain, I’m here. Healthy, sound, and ready to go,” he said. “I am ready to kick, ready to work. There’s nothing wrong.”

World.title: 2027: Tompolo rallies Taraba for Tinubu, donates 25 campaign vehicles
World.content:
As campaigns for the January 2027 presidential election gather momentum, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement has launched its grassroots mobilisation campaign in Taraba State, calling on residents to support the re-election of President Bola Tinubu.

The movement, led by its Grand Patron, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, said the President’s reforms require more time to consolidate and deliver greater benefits to Nigerians.

Represented at the launch in Jalingo by Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said Taraba was benefiting from the policies of the Tinubu administration, stressing that continuity was necessary to sustain the gains recorded so far.

He said, “Taraba is thriving because President Tinubu has good reformation policies that are moving the state forward. If we want those policies to continue and be more solid, to consolidate on them, we need to give the dent another four years.”

According to him, another tenure will ensure that civil servants continue to receive their salaries as at when due, while Governor Agbu Kefas would have more time to develop the state.

Tompolo said some challenges previously experienced, by Nigerians, including fuel queues and disruptions in university education have reduced, attributing the changes to policies of the Tinubu administration.

He acknowledged that reforms come with challenges but said they require time to produce their full benefits.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Every policy needs time to consolidate; every policy needs time to show dividends. Every policy reformation will always come with its own challenges, but once we bear a little and they pass, we will go to the smooth road we are to ride on,” he said.

He urged supporters of the movement to take the campaign to every level of the society, including homes, religious centres, wards, local government areas and polling units.

Speaking at the event, Governor Agbu Kefas said the people of Taraba were already witnessing the impact of the Tinubu administration through projects being implemented in the state.

“Taraba is ready. You don’t need to tell the people of Taraba State what the President is doing; they are seeing what the President is doing through me,” Governor Kefas said.

He said his administration remains committed to the Renewed Hope Agenda of the President, adding that the state would continue to work with the Federal Government on development projects.

“We are moving forward with the mandate of the Renewed Hope Agenda of Mr. President and by the grace of God we are going to go to all the units, the wards and be flagging off projects and commissioning projects, not telling empty stories,” he said.

Mr Kefas also pledged massive support for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

“I want to assure you that we are going out en masse to give the President 100 percent votes. We are ready for Mr. President,” he said.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, said the group was in Taraba to extend its message of support for the President and the state governor.

Mr Asuku said Nigerians like the administration’s reforms direction, arguing that abandoning the reforms of the Tinubu administration would be counterproductiIve.

“The surest way for us today is the APC. We are on the right trajectory and that is why we should remain where we are,” he said.

He commended Governor Kefas for what he described as achievements recorded in Taraba over the past three years.

The highpoint of the event was the donation of 25 campaign vehicles, generators and electronic speakers for grassroots mobilisation.

World.title: Abacha freed Ijaw from oppression by creating Bayelsa, Diri says
World.content:
Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has described the late military Head of State, Sani Abacha, as the man who “freed” the Ijaw people from oppression by creating Bayelsa State in 1996.

Mr Diri made the statement Thursday night at the dinner and awards ceremony marking the state’s 30th anniversary of the creation of the state in Yenagoa.

The governor said although Mr Abacha’s legacy might be viewed differently by Nigerians, his decision to create Bayelsa from parts of the former Rivers State remained important to the Ijaw people.

“If at every point in my remarks I keep calling him, it is because of what God used him to do for the Ijaw ethnic nationality,” Mr Diri said at the ceremony held at the Chief Diepreye Alamieyeseigha Memorial Banquet Hall, Government House.

“General Abacha might mean different things to different people, but to Bayelsans, he is the one who freed us from oppression.

“He freed us from injustice and gave a homogenous state for a people that had been balkanised into various states, and making us minority in some.”

Mr Diri said Bayelsans owed Mr Abacha continued gratitude for creating the state on 1 October 1996, adding that the late military ruler was represented at the ceremony by his son, Abba Abacha, and daughter, Fatima Abacha.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Please take our appreciation and gratitude back home to your mother,” he told the Abacha family.

The governor spoke as Bayelsa marked three decades of statehood with a four-day celebration tagged “Celebrating Legacies,” which culminated in the dinner and presentation of state honours to 63 individuals and groups.

Jonathan dedicates award to Alamieyeseigha

Former President Goodluck Jonathan, who was among those honoured, dedicated his award to his late political mentor, Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, who appointed him deputy governor of Bayelsa State.

Mr Jonathan said the creation of Bayelsa had brought many benefits to its people, despite concerns among some young people about the state’s achievements after 30 years.

“Although we have not reached where we are supposed to be, I am happy where we are. I am happy that Bayelsa State was created, and we have gained tremendously,” he said.

The former president also thanked Mr Abacha for creating Bayelsa.

“Bayelsans will always remain grateful to late Gen. Sani Abacha who made it possible for Bayelsa to be among the last six states he created,” he said.

Mr Jonathan commended Mr Diri for organising the anniversary and recognising those who contributed to the state’s creation and development.

From one road to expanding network

Defending the importance of the anniversary, Mr Diri said Bayelsa had made substantial progress from its condition at creation, when infrastructure was severely limited.

He said the state moved from having no tertiary institution to having more than five universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.

He also recalled that Bayelsa had only the single-lane Mbiama-Yenagoa road at its creation, saying the state now had an expanding road network, dualised highways and three senatorial roads connecting different parts of the state.

He described the award recipients as part of the legacy of the state and congratulated them for their contributions.

Who received the honours?

Mr Abacha, Mr Jonathan, Isaac Adaka Boro, Mr Alamieyeseigha, Harold Dappa-Biriye and several former military administrators of Bayelsa were among those honoured.

The former military administrators recognised included Caleb Olubolade, Phillip Ayeni, Habu Daura and Edor Obi. The immediate past governor, Seriake Dickson, was also honoured.

Others recognised included people credited with facilitating the creation of Bayelsa under the “Contribution to Sustenance of Ijaw Existence” category.

The late British-born linguist, Kay Williamson, was honoured for promoting the Ijaw language.

In sports, the state recognised Olympic wrestlers Daniel Igali and Blessing Oborududu, as well as former Super Eagles players and coaches Samson Siasia and Finidi George.

Other awardees included former Ijaw National Congress president Joshua Fumudoh; musicians Robert Ebizimor, Timaya and Timi Dakolo; and former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Didi Walson-Jack.

Ayebaemi Spiff, Lawrence Ekpebu, Ebiegberi Alagoa, Dimie Ogoina and Youpele Beredugo were among those recognised in education.

Business figures honoured included Dan Etete, Gesi Asamaowei, Preye Berezi, Ken Etete, Ebitimi Banigo, Ephraim Faloughi, Daru Owei and Robert Enogha.

The Bayelsa State Cultural Troupe also received an award, while the late former National Security Adviser, Owoeye Azazi, was honoured in the military category.

Others included Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri; teenage chess player Deborah Quickpen; and the late Ernest Ikoli, a nationalist and pioneer editor of the Daily Times newspaper.

The ceremony was attended by members of the Abacha family, National Assembly members, government officials, traditional rulers, business leaders and diplomats.

Diplomats from Germany, Portugal, Italy, Vietnam, Angola, the Czech Republic, and São Tomé and Príncipe were also present.

World.title: South Korea captain ‘deeply sorry’ for gloating about military exemption
World.content:
South Korea’s Asian Games football captain apologised on Sunday for boasting that his gold medal meant he did not have to do military service.

South Korea defeated hosts Japan 1-0 on Saturday in the men’s final in Toyota, near Nagoya, for their fourth Games title in a row.

Afterwards, Lee Gi-hyuk smiled as he held up his gold medal to reporters and said: “I’m not going to the military.”

Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to perform between 18 months and two years of military service before the age of 28.

But the government rewards Asian Games gold medals and Olympic medals of any colour with an exemption, meaning they will carry out just weeks of light basic training instead.

Exemptions are a sensitive topic in South Korea, and athletes usually shy away from talking about it.

The 26-year-old Lee, a defender who plays in the domestic K League, apologised for “the thoughtless remarks I made and the way I behaved after the match, things I should not have said or done, both as captain and as a player”.

In a statement on Instagram he said he was “caught up in the happiness, adrenaline and excitement of the moment”.

“I am deeply sorry to the fans who are currently fulfilling their military duty, as well as to all those who sincerely supported us,” he said.

“As an adult I should have thought carefully before speaking. I deeply regret having spoken so carelessly, and I will continue to reflect on my actions.

“I sincerely apologise to all the fans who have supported us wholeheartedly and who are doing their utmost to fulfil their military duty.”

Asian Games football is contested between under-23 squads, but three overage players are allowed.

Lee played in South Korea’s disastrous World Cup campaign in North America, when they went out in the group phase.

The golfer Tom Kim also earned a military exemption after winning gold at the Asian Games on Saturday.
