Under Mrs. Adetuyi’s initial leadership, STN operated as a modest call service, but the underlying mission was always broader: expanding access and bringing people together. By 1999, the business introduced voicemail services to the University of Lagos community—a novel offering on a Nigerian campus at the time.

A breakthrough arrived in 2003, when STN became the first provider of digital landline services in Yaba through a franchise agreement with Independent Telephone Network (ITN). At a time when neither NITEL nor the emerging GSM operators had deployed digital telephony in the area, STN connected local homes, schools, and enterprises.

That same year, STN helped develop and power the infrastructure behind WAEC Direct. This landmark platform enabled millions of Nigerian students to check their examination results via scratch card instead of waiting in line at regional offices. Soon after, STN was providing mission-critical connectivity to high-stakes institutions, including the Nigerian Military, the World Health Organisation, and key public agencies across Yaba.

Navigating Independence and Adversity

Growth inevitably forces tough choices. When ITN entered acquisition talks with Visafone, STN’s initial franchise agreement drew to a close. Rather than being absorbed into a larger corporate structure, STN chose independence, trading initially as YOBOC & Co. Ltd while applying directly to the NCC for its own operating licences.

By 2005, the company secured its independent regulatory approvals and formally transitioned to Swift Telephone Network Limited in 2008. To protect its customer base during the shift, the NCC allocated the numbering prefix 01343XXXX, allowing subscribers to retain their lines uninterrupted.

Yet, as with many Nigerian enterprise stories, severe headwinds soon tested its success. In 2009, shortly after securing growth funding, STN faced boardroom disputes, ownership shifts, and devastating infrastructure damage. Operations ground to a halt by November 2010.

Rebirth and Transformation

What seemed like the end proved to be a pause. In February 2017, the company reopened its doors under the leadership of Oluwole Adetuyi, the founder’s son. Rebuilding meant addressing significant legacy hurdles: the original operating licence had expired in 2015, and years of regulatory obligations remained outstanding.

Joined by Yetunde Okafor, the duo set out to restore the company. In 2018, they confronted the backlog directly, clearing tax liabilities and operational levies accrued between 2010 and 2016. Convinced by their compliance and commitment, the NCC officially reinstated STN’s operating licence in 2019, paving the way for a full operational launch by September of that year.

When the COVID-19 pandemic hit in 2020, corporate reliance on traditional office landlines and Private Branch Exchange (PBX) systems plummeted. Recognising that the future of telecom lay in integrated mobile, broadband, and data services, STN adapted once again. On February 22, 2022, the company formally applied for the NCC’s Unified Access Service Licence (UASL).

The Next Chapter

Now officially granted, the national UASL empowers STN to operate fixed, mobile, voice, and data services across Nigeria.

As STN prepares for its national rollout, leadership has outlined several core commitments to create local value: Talent Development: Training Nigerian engineers and digital specialists to build technical capacity locally.

Domestic Partnerships: Prioritising local vendors, contractors, and SMEs across network deployment and maintenance.

Knowledge Transfer: Partnering with international technology providers while keeping intellectual property and skills rooted in Nigeria.

Digital Inclusion: Expanding infrastructure into underserved regions to bridge the digital divide. Enterprise & Job Creation: Driving employment through distribution networks, customer support, and value-added service roles.

The Rollout Plans

Chief Executive Officer of STN, Oluwole Adetuyi, said: “This UASL is not just a licence. It is a new chapter. It represents where we started, what we have endured, how we have evolved, and where we are going. We are building in Nigeria, for Nigeria.”

Reflecting on STN’s resilience, Adetuyi said the milestone would reinforce a larger truth: Nigerian businesses can stand the test of time.

“Telcos can evolve, compete globally, and build institutions of lasting value from Nigeria. At a time when the digital economy is central to national growth, STN is proof that local ambition, backed by resilience, can deliver world-class infrastructure”, said Adetuyi.

According to him, as STN enters the new phase, the company is committing to building a truly Nigerian telecommunications ecosystem.

“Our ambition is simple: to help build Nigeria’s digital economy from the ground up. This licence gives us the platform. Nigerian talent, Nigerian partners, and Nigerian innovation will give us the momentum,” Adetuyi further said, adding that STN will, in the coming weeks, announce strategic partnerships, infrastructure rollout plans, and programmes to engage investors and stakeholders as it begins commercial operations under the UASL.

From a single campus telephone stand in 1998 to a nationally licensed operator today, STN’s trajectory reflects the persistent spirit of Nigerian enterprise. Led by Oluwole Adetuyi, Yetunde Okafor, and the management team, the company enters its next phase honouring the legacy of its late founder, carrying forward the principle that no hurdle is insurmountable.

World.title: Nobody won Friday’s R93 million PowerBall, here’s what’s rolling into Tuesday
World.content:
PowerBall's jackpot has rolled over again, now heading toward R97 million. Image: ChatGPT

Friday’s PowerBall draw has come and gone without a jackpot winner, in either game, sending both prizes rolling over once again.

No player matched all five numbers plus the PowerBall in Friday’s draw, sending the R90 million main jackpot rolling over to an estimated R97 million for Tuesday, 6 October.

THE WINNING NUMBERS

The winning PowerBall numbers drawn on Friday, 2 October, were 15, 26, 27, 28, 39, with a PowerBall number of 10.



For PowerBall Xtra, the numbers were 33, 36, 40, 41, 42, with a PowerBall Xtra number of 04.

HOW CLOSE SOUTH AFRICANS ACTUALLY GOT

While nobody claimed either jackpot, one player came genuinely close.

A single ticket matched all five main numbers in the PowerBall draw, just missing the PowerBall itself, and walked away with R593,155.50 in Division 2.

A further 23 players matched four numbers plus the PowerBall, each collecting R12,894.60.

PowerBall Xtra’s own R3 million jackpot also went unclaimed on the same night.

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING

Rollovers happen whenever no single ticket matches all five main numbers plus the PowerBall, and the unclaimed portion simply carries forward, growing the pot for the next draw.



It’s exactly this pattern that regularly pushes PowerBall jackpots into the tens, and sometimes hundreds, of millions.

For context, the biggest PowerBall jackpot ever won in South Africa remains R178,955,240.90, claimed back on 20 January 2026.

WHAT TO EXPECT NEXT TUESDAY

With no winner again, the main PowerBall jackpot now rolls into Tuesday, 6 October, with an estimated R97 million on the table.

PowerBall Xtra is separately expected to climb to around R6 million for the same draw, though this figure will only be confirmed closer to draw night.

Worth remembering: a bigger jackpot doesn’t change your actual odds of winning, which stay fixed regardless of how large the prize grows.

I always find these extended rollover streaks genuinely gripping to follow.

Somewhere out there, someone’s numbers are about to finally line up, it’s just a matter of which draw finally does it.

Are you playing on Tuesday, and do you already have your numbers picked?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: INTERPOL arrests Turkish fugitive wanted for rape in Durban
World.content:
INTERPOL South Africa arrested a Turkish fugitive in Isipingo, Durban, over rape, sexual assault and kidnapping allegations dating back to 2010. Image: Pexels

INTERPOL South Africa has arrested a 40-year-old Turkish fugitive wanted on rape, sexual assault and kidnapping charges after investigators tracked him to Isipingo, KwaZulu-Natal.

Turkish authorities want the man to stand trial over allegations that he kidnapped his then-fiancée and raped her over several days in 2010.

The INTERPOL South Africa Fugitive Investigation Team arrested him during a coordinated operation on Thursday, 1 October. Crime Intelligence, Isipingo police and private security supported the operation.



Turkish fugitive wanted on rape charges

Turkish authorities want the suspect to face charges of rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, malicious damage to property and assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.

The allegations were reported to the Eskişehir Police Department in Türkiye.

SAPS spokesperson Colonel Amanda van Wyk said information supplied by Turkish authorities showed that the alleged crimes date back to 2010.

The man allegedly kidnapped his then-fiancée, who was 22 at the time, before raping her over several days.

Police said he also allegedly assaulted the woman by repeatedly striking her head against a wall.

The attack allegedly left her with permanent physical and psychological injuries.



INTERPOL tracks suspect to Isipingo

The suspect allegedly fled Türkiye after authorities completed their investigation.

Investigators eventually tracked him to Isipingo. “He was subsequently traced to Isipingo in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa,” Van Wyk said.

Turkish authorities then submitted an extradition request to South Africa.

Van Wyk said INTERPOL’s National Central Bureau in Pretoria obtained and executed a warrant under Section 5(1)(b), leading to his arrest.

Fugitive faces extradition to Türkiye

The man appeared in the Umlazi Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 2 October. “The fugitive appeared before the Umlazi Magistrates’ Court on 2 October 2026, facing an extradition application by the government of the Republic of Türkiye to the Republic of South Africa,” Van Wyk said.

The court must now deal with the application to extradite him to Türkiye, where authorities want him to stand trial.

Second Turkish fugitive arrested in South Africa

The Isipingo arrest came days after INTERPOL South Africa arrested another Turkish fugitive in Cape Town.

Police arrested the former primary school principal on 21 September.

Turkish authorities want him on charges of sexual assault, kidnapping and intimidation involving a nine-year-old child.

He has since appeared in the Cape Town Magistrate’s Court.

Van Wyk said SAPS continues to strengthen cooperation with international law-enforcement agencies through INTERPOL to trace wanted people who cross borders to evade justice.

World.title: Weight-loss drugs: Crackdown could hit 300 000 South Africans
World.content:
A crackdown on illegally compounded weight-loss drugs could affect up to 300 000 South Africans who rely on GLP-1 treatments. Image: Pexels

A crackdown on illegally compounded weight-loss drugs could affect up to 300 000 South Africans, leaving patients with fewer and potentially far more expensive treatment options.

Regulatory and legal action has targeted pharmacies illegally compounding GLP-1 medicines used for weight management.

Health management company Obiflex says patients who relied on compounded versions could now face monthly costs of between R4 000 and R6 000 for registered, doctor-prescribed alternatives.



Weight-loss drug crackdown hits South Africans

Obiflex CEO Shaun Barns said affordability remained one of the biggest obstacles for people seeking treatment.

“There are hundreds of thousands of South Africans, wanting to go on this weight-loss journey but they just simply can’t afford the R4000 to R6000,” Barns said.

The crackdown creates another concern.

Patients who cannot afford registered alternatives could turn to unregulated products sold through unofficial channels.

Barns warned that doing so could carry serious health risks.

Warning over illegal weight-loss drugs

The South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) has previously warned consumers against buying weight-loss medicines from unverified suppliers.



Consumers should only obtain scheduled medicines through legitimate healthcare channels and accredited pharmacies.

Barns warned that illicit products may contain incorrect doses.

He said tests had found discrepancies of up to 40% between the dose stated on some product labels and what the products actually contained.

That means patients could unknowingly inject or take significantly more or less of a medicine than intended.

Registered treatment can cost thousands

The rapid growth in demand for GLP-1 medicines has created a lucrative market for weight-loss products in South Africa.

But price remains a major barrier.

Obiflex estimates that registered alternatives could cost patients between R4 000 and R6 000, depending on the treatment.

That leaves patients who previously relied on cheaper compounded products facing a difficult decision.

They can move to a registered alternative, stop treatment or risk buying products from an unregulated source.

Health authorities have warned that the last option could expose users to medicines that have not undergone the necessary checks for quality, safety and dosage.

SAHPRA urges caution

SAHPRA has urged consumers to check where their medicine comes from before buying weight-loss products, especially those advertised online or through social media.

The regulator has previously taken action against operations linked to unauthorised weight-loss medicines and warned about products containing active pharmaceutical ingredients without the required regulatory controls.

World.title: Update: Former employer allegedly stole R20 milliom from Orlando Pirates
World.content:
Orlando Pirates‘ legal action follows an extensive internal forensic investigation into financial transactions at the club. According to court papers, the investigation identified approximately R43.1 million in unauthorised funds that allegedly flowed from Orlando Pirates accounts into accounts controlled by Joselowsky between 2016 and 2026.

ORLANDO PIRATES SEEK TO PROTECT CLUB FUNDS

The court papers describe Joselowsky’s former position at Orlando Pirates as one involving an exceptionally high level of responsibility and trust.

Club commercial manager Mpumelelo Khoza stated in an affidavit that Joselowsky occupied a position of “extreme personal and fiduciary trust”, with “complete responsibility for managing the bank accounts, payroll, supplier disbursements and financial ledgers.”



According to the forensic investigation, concerns began emerging in July 2026 when routine management account reviews reportedly identified significant discrepancies.

Orlando Pirates subsequently approached the High Court without giving Joselowsky prior notice. It argues that an advance warning could allow funds to be moved before the court could intervene.

The affidavit claims that “if an interim freezing order is refused, [Joselowsky] will dissipate the stolen proceeds across multiple local and offshore banking accounts”, potentially causing “an irreparable monetary loss to the club.”



The court papers also raise concerns about Joselowsky’s Austrian citizenship. The club considers relevant to its concerns about the potential movement of funds and his ability to leave South Africa.

LEGAL PROCESS CONTINUES AS BUCCANEERS PURSUE RECOVERY

The matter involves both civil recovery proceedings. There is an ongoing criminal process as Orlando Pirates attempts to establish what happened to the money identified during the investigation.

Orlando Pirates spokesperson Thandi Merafe has stressed that the club’s court application should not be interpreted as a final determination against the former employee.



The club described the legal action as a “precautionary step to preserve funds while the matter is investigated.”

Orlando Pirates further emphasised that “the application is a precautionary step to protect the Club’s funds” and “does not constitute a final judicial finding of wrongdoing.”

Attempts by members of the media to locate Joselowsky at his listed residence in Glenhazel have reportedly been unsuccessful, with estate security indicating that there was no record of him at the address.



The legal proceedings will now determine the next steps as Orlando Pirates seeks to preserve the identified funds and trace the transactions highlighted by its forensic investigation.

For the club, the immediate priority is protecting its financial interests while allowing the High Court and relevant authorities to deal with the allegations through the proper legal process.

World.title: Bafana Bafana v Egypt: Three players who could earn rare starts
World.content:
Bafana Bafana face their toughest test of the current international break when they take on Egypt in an international friendly in Cairo on Sunday evening.

Pitso Mosimane‘s side have made a strong start under their new coach, beating Guinea 2-1 before producing a convincing 5-0 victory over Eritrea.

Egypt, however, will provide a significantly different challenge and should give Mosimane a clearer indication of where his team stands against one of Africa’s traditional heavyweights.



With Mosimane expected to make several changes to his starting XI, there could be opportunities for some of the players who have featured less prominently in the opening two matches.

Bafana to take on Egypt

Here are three players who could come into the starting lineup against Egypt:

Sipho Chaine

Orlando Pirates goalkeeper Sipho Chaine could be handed a rare start for Bafana Bafana.

The 28-year-old is one of the more experienced members of the squad but has had limited opportunities at international level, making Sunday’s match a potential chance for him to stake his claim.

With Ricardo Goss also competing for the position, Chaine could get the nod as Mosimane looks to assess his goalkeeping options.

Puso Dithejane

Young winger Puso Dithejane could be in line for his first start for Bafana Bafana.



Dithejane’s performances in Major League Soccer with Chicago Fire have earned him a call-up to the national team, and his pace and attacking ability could provide another dimension against Egypt.

After making his way into the squad, a start in Cairo would give the youngster an opportunity to show Mosimane what he can offer at international level.

Themba Zwane

Themba Zwane could also return to the starting XI as Mosimane looks to add experience to his midfield.

The veteran midfielder has not started for Bafana Bafana in some time, but Sunday’s match could provide him with an opportunity to remind the new coach of his qualities.

With Teboho Mokoena unavailable, Zwane’s experience could be particularly valuable in the middle of the park against a strong Egyptian side.

Mosimane is expected to use the friendly to assess different combinations, and the match could provide several players with an important opportunity to impress as Bafana Bafana continue to build under their new coach.

Which player should start?

World.title: Mamelodi twins murder: Police follow new lead in stabbing case
World.content:
Police are following a new lead after 14-year-old twins Bothlale and Bonolo Makena were stabbed to death inside their Mamelodi West home. Image: Pexels

Police are following a lead in the murder of 14-year-old twins Bothlale and Bonolo Makena, who were stabbed to death inside their Mamelodi West home.

Their mother found the boys with multiple stab wounds inside a bedroom when she returned from work on Friday, 2 October.

Police have not arrested anyone.

However, investigators have received information that could help them establish what happened inside the house.



Police follow lead in Mamelodi twins murder

Gauteng police spokesperson Colonel Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi confirmed that detectives were following up on information.

“Unfortunately, I cannot dwell much into the investigation, lest I jeopardise it,” Nevhuhulwi said.

She said police hoped the information would help them unravel the circumstances surrounding the killings.



Police have not disclosed what the lead involves or whether they have identified any suspects.

No signs of forced entry

Investigators have also found no indication of forced entry into the house.

That has become a key part of the investigation as detectives work to determine how the killer or killers gained access to the property.



Police have yet to establish a motive.

The circumstances surrounding the attack also remain unclear.

Government has urged residents not to circulate unverified information about the murders on social media.



Deputy government spokesperson William Baloyi called on anyone who saw or heard anything unusual before or after the killings to approach police.

Who were Bothlale and Bonolo Makena?

Bothlale and Bonolo have been remembered as quiet boys who loved attending church.

Ethiopian Catholic Church Bishop Mashilo Mangena said he had baptised the twins and was preparing to confirm them as full members of the church.



Mangena said the teenagers regularly attended church classes and stayed away from criminal activity.

Their deaths have shocked residents in Mamelodi West, with community members questioning how two children could be murdered inside their home without neighbours hearing anything.

The investigation continues.

Anyone with information can contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or report information at their nearest police station.

World.title: Will naturalised citizens and permanent residents get Smart IDs before the new deadline?
World.content:
It's some good news for permanent residents and naturalised citizens as South Africa phases out green IDs. Image: file

Naturalised South African citizens and lawful permanent residents who have been caught up in the country’s green ID book phase-out have been given an important assurance by Home Affairs.

The department has confirmed that the remaining eligible members of these groups will be enabled to obtain Smart ID cards before the green ID book is no longer valid.

Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber made the commitment as he announced the final timeline for phasing out South Africa’s historic green ID books.



Smart ID access has already changed

Naturalised citizens and permanent residents were previously among the groups that struggled to access Smart ID cards because of problems with Home Affairs’ systems.

That changed in May 2025, when Home Affairs opened Smart ID applications to naturalised South African citizens and lawful permanent residents for the first time on a broader basis.

The department said the change opened access to more than 1.4 million eligible people and also allowed them to use the eHomeAffairs platform.

However, the rollout has not necessarily meant that every eligible person has already moved from a green ID book to a Smart ID.

Home Affairs promises access before the deadline

Schreiber has now specifically addressed those who remain dependent on the old document.

He said Home Affairs will enable the remaining cohort of naturalised citizens and permanent residents, as well as South African citizens living abroad, to obtain Smart IDs before 31 March 2027.



“Importantly, prior to 31 March 2027, the department will enable the remaining cohort of naturalised citizens and permanent residents, as well as South African citizens abroad, to also obtain Smart IDs.” Minister Schreiber said. “By including these groups that have historically been excluded, we will ensure that – for the first time ever, every single eligible person is finally able to obtain a secure Smart ID card.” Schreiber added.

That date is important because it is when Home Affairs plans to stop producing green ID books and permanently decommission the machines used to make them.

When does the green ID book become invalid?

Stopping production and making the green book invalid are two different deadlines.

Home Affairs will stop producing green ID books on 31 March 2027.

Existing green books will then have another 12 months before they cease to be recognised as valid identity documents.

The final deadline is 31 March 2028. After this date, the green ID book will no longer be accepted as a valid form of identification.

This means naturalised citizens and permanent residents who still have green books have a clear window in which to move to the Smart ID system.

So, who qualifies?

The Smart ID rollout covers naturalised South African citizens and lawful permanent residents.

A naturalised citizen is someone who became a South African citizen through naturalisation rather than being a citizen by birth. A permanent resident, meanwhile, has permanent residence in South Africa but is not automatically a South African citizen.

Both groups were historically affected by Home Affairs system limitations, but the department says they are now eligible for Smart IDs.

There was initially a phased rollout for permanent residents and naturalised citizens, including a first phase focused on people from visa-exempt countries. Home Affairs said applicants from non-exempt countries would be assisted as the rollout expanded.

World.title: Chivayo helicopter crash: Pilot’s final radio words before fatal accident
World.content:
Wreckage of the Bell 430 helicopter that was carrying Wicknell Chivayo after it crashed near Marondera (Picture: ZBC News)

The pilot of the helicopter carrying Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo reportedly battled poor weather and struggled to emerge from dense cloud shortly before the aircraft crashed near Marondera, killing all five people on board.

Details of the final radio communications were provided by Chivayo’s senior security aide, Froster Chisi, who was travelling in another helicopter flying nearby.

According to The NewsHawks, Captain Kelvin Tafirei Soda and fellow pilot Captain Courage Mutavirwa encountered rainy and misty conditions while flying back to Harare from Chivayo’s rural homestead in Gandami, Chikomba, on Wednesday.



The Bell 430 was carrying Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke and her personal aide Senelisiwe Magagula.

Chivayo helicopter pilot: ‘I haven’t exited the cloud’

Chisi said the weather deteriorated as the two helicopters approached Marondera, where they were expected to stop before continuing to Harare.

The pilot of the second helicopter reportedly suggested changing course through Bromley because of the conditions.

Soda continued communicating with the other aircraft as he struggled with poor visibility.

“I’m in bad weather; I haven’t exited the cloud,” Soda reportedly said over the radio.

His last reported position was over the Surrey area.



When the pilot of the second helicopter said they were about 10 minutes from their destination, Soda reportedly asked: “Which destination?”

“Marondera,” the other pilot responded.

There was no further communication from Chivayo’s helicopter.

Second helicopter waited for the aircraft

Chisi’s helicopter landed in Marondera, with those on board initially expecting the Bell 430 to arrive later.

They reportedly waited for the aircraft before flying to Harare to collect vehicles.

After spending more than an hour trying to contact Chivayo, Muteke and the pilots, they eventually learnt that the helicopter had crashed.

The aircraft went down at about 5pm at Kudenga Farm near Waddilove Mission in Marondera Rural.

All five people on board died.

What investigators will examine after Chivayo crash

Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe director-general George Mashababe said preliminary observations indicated that fuel spilled after the helicopter struck the ground, resulting in a fire that also burnt surrounding grass.

A flight recorder recovered from the wreckage is expected to assist investigators in reconstructing the aircraft’s final moments.

Investigators are expected to examine the recorder, radio communications, weather conditions and wreckage as they establish what happened.

However, authorities have not concluded that bad weather or spatial disorientation caused the crash.

The radio exchanges provide an account of the conditions faced by the pilots, but they do not establish why the helicopter ultimately went down.

The investigation remains ongoing.

World.title: Reiger Park’s R108m white elephant
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A multi-million-rand enterprise and skills hub in Reiger Park stands empty, despite more than R108 million being spent building it.

Located in a community heavily plagued by drugs and gangsterism, the facility was designed to provide local traders with retail spaces and skills training,

but its doors remain shut.

It is one of five completed facilities, costing a combined R209-million, that Ekurhuleni has listed as unused.

Even residents want the hub to open.

“It could have made a big difference because there are many of us who looked forward to this facility for jobs. Especially me, I just finished school last year. I’m still sitting at home. This is a really big waste of time,” a resident said.

The City of Ekurhuleni said the Reiger Park Enterprise Hub and Ramaphosa Skills Centre was built for trading, light industry, manufacturing workshops, offices and training. But for years, it’s been standing idle.

Despite repeated attempts by eNCA to get answers from the city, neither the mayor nor any municipal officials were available.

Community leader, Lucinda Schubert, said the hub could be a huge benefit for young people in the area.

“There are a lot of youth that don’t know what to do with themselves. That don’t know where to go. With the training centre and everything built here and can help teach the youth and make them employable. Giving them skills, but none of that is being utilised. Not like there’s an alternative place in Reiger Park for those kinds of things to happen.”

This building in Reiger Park is one part of a wider problem.

Ekurhuleni has listed five completed but unused facilities in its metro, including sports facilities in Bakerton and Vosloorus and early childhood development centres in Vosloorus and Eden Park.

Reiger Part CPF member Leon Bussack said opening the hub could help keep young people away from criminal activities.

“It’s a shame that we have a building like this just standing around when it could be used. We always say a lack of opportunity will result in the criminal element sneaking in. This is a typical example. It’s only one of a few examples in Reiger Park. It’s sad to see that such a building is not being used. These boys could find themselves out of the drug trade. Doing something more constructive.”

World.title: Life will never be the same – expert on survivors of mass shootings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Life may never return to what it was for survivors and families of victims of mass shootings.

That's according to psychologist Tholinhlanhla Dlamini-Ngcoya.

She warned that some may turn to substance abuse as a form of self-medication.

The most recent attack saw 18 people killed at a tavern in Wedela, Carletonville.

That same weekend, 10 people were killed at a shisanyama in Lwandle, Cape Town.

Another 11 people were killed in a shooting in KwaMakhutha, near Durban.

“Their normal is going to be different from what they knew life to be before. Now there is an experience that has changed and tainted the way they look at people and people's behavior at a place of joy and fun where they go to a tavern.

She said some substance abuse because they're trying to numb their feelings.

“And when we're talking about substance abuse, I need the families to also be aware that people can be addicted to prescribed drugs. They might be sleeping tablets.

"So a normal life as we know it is going to be different for the survivors, a normal life as we know it is going to be different for people around those survivors. They have to now move differently. They have to talk differently.”

World.title: Interpol nabs Turkish fugitives in Cape Town and KZN
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Interpol arrested a Turkish fugitive, a former primary school principal, in Cape Town.

He was wanted in connection with charges of sexual assault, kidnapping and intimidation involving a nine-year-old victim.

The former principal was arrested on Monday, 21 September 2026, and has since appeared before the Cape Town Magistrates’ Court.

Meanwhile, 40-year-old Turkish fugitive has been arrested in Isipingo, KwaZulu-Natal, on Thursday. The arrest was affected by Interpol South Africa’s Fugitive Investigation Team, supported by Crime Intelligence, members from the Isipingo Police Station and private security.

Turkish authorities to stand trial on charges of rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, malicious damage to property and assault with intent to cause grievous bodily harm (GBH), which were reported to the Eskişehir Police Department in Türkiye.

According to the information received from Turkish authorities, SAPS spokesperson Colonel Amanda van Wyk said, the suspect allegedly kidnapped his then-fiancée in 2010 and raped her over several days.

He also allegedly assaulted the victim by repeatedly striking her head against a wall, resulting in permanent physical and psychological impairment. The victim was 22 years old at the time of the alleged offences.

He then fled to Isipingo.

" Upon receipt of the extradition request from Turkish authorities, Interpol National Central Bureau (NCB) Pretoria obtained and executed a warrant in terms of Section 5(1)(b) of the relevant legislation, resulting in the fugitive’s arrest.

“The fugitive appeared before the Umlazi Magistrates’ Court on Friday, 2 October 2026 facing an extradition application by the government of the Republic of Türkiye to the Republic of South Africa.”

World.title: ‘Control yourself’ - Pastor Mboro calls on men in fight against GBV
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pastor Paseka Motsoeneng warns that gender-based violence and femicide have reached a crisis.

Speaking during a GBVF march in Kempton Park, he urged the government to act and called for stronger community safety measures.

“They (Men) should stop being easily provoked. And you need God and the fruits of the spirit.

“No matter how they dress. I saw another woman was wearing shorts. Even if the thighs can shine like that, even if they go naked, control yourself. We don’t even have to put rules about what they must wear and what they must do. If they take their breasts out, no problem. Let’s protect women and fight this thing,” he said.

Motsoeneng said the number of women killed in Ekurhuleni is less than the reality of women dying every day in South Africa.

“These are just the numbers that are discovered in the media. Every week women are dying and some they wake up; their parts are gone. There is also a spiritual thing in this thing.

There are human sacrifices, the blood of the women, their cry and the children. Every time they do this, it extends their power.

Religious leaders in Ekurhuleni joined the growing call to end South Africa’s gender-based violence crisis.

Demonstrators, including civil society and faith groups, gathered at the Kempton Park Civic Centre to demand greater police accountability and action.

The demonstration follows the discovery of at least 11 women’s bodies in Ekurhuleni since July, three of whom remain unidentified.

World.title: Zille launches controversial M1 bridge campaign
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - DA Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille has sparked controversy with a campaign spotlighting the city’s crumbling bridges.

She staged her warning on a dilapidated stretch of the M1, calling it a potential safety hazard for motorists.

“You can see behind me a bridge that is crumbling and in fact the bridge on the off-ramp is even in worse condition. Now the city has done an audit of bridges about eight years ago in which the audit warned them that the bridges would have to be seen to very quickly because they were rapidly becoming unsafe because of lack of maintenance.

“This is one of them, but there are many others around Joburg. Some are in an even worse condition. In fact, the city's own statistics say that 78 percent of bridges are in need of urgent maintenance and repair. They're either bad or very bad in their condition and this is serious for motorists because they and pedestrians often don't realise the state of the bridges that they drive over and under and that creates a potential hazard.

Johannesburg Metro Police spokesperson Xolani Fihla said the DA would be fined for placing posters on bridges, which is not permitted.

He added JMPD would consult the IEC to explore further action.

“Political parties need to adhere to municipal bylaws.

“We will remove those posters on the bridge. This will definitely be taken forward,” Fihla said.

Zille conceded that the DA did not seek official approval for the event but insisted it’s vital to alert drivers to the risk posed by Johannesburg’s neglected bridges.

“Pointing out to the public that bridges are dangerous is certainly not a gimmick, it's a public service. This is an event organized by the national DA in concert with the provincial DA. We didn't specifically seek permission, but we are warning motorists that this is a very dangerous bridge and that they need to know it.

World.title: ‘Andile Lungisa not entitled to public office’ - ANC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC said Andile Lungisa, who hopes to become Mayor of Gqeberha, isn’t entitled to public office.

This follows Lungisa’s urgent court bid after the party dropped him from its list of potential councillors.

The High Court in Johannesburg heard the case this week. In a statement, the ANC called the legal fight "sorrowful”.

The party pointed to Lungisa’s criminal record as the key issue.

In 2018, he was sentenced to two years in prison for assaulting DA councillor Rayno Kayser with a jug.

The ANC said this record rules him out of public office.

Judgment has been reserved in the matter.

World.title: Young Men Movement calls for everyday action against GBV
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Young Men Movement founder Kabelo Chabalala has said that inconsistent leadership can undermine the fight against gender-based violence.

He stressed the need for sustained plans and commitments that outlast political changes, urging a year-round focus on GBV.

“I think the biggest challenge in this country is also how we are structuring approaches. A lot of these issues continue to manifest in the different parts of our country also because of the problematic discontinuation of who is in leadership from a political perspective.

“We are heading towards 16 days of activism. We're going to see some talks and a little bit of promises around action, and then we're going to move on into December. We forget that women are being killed every day in this country.

“It's not a Kempton Park problem. It's not a September, October problem. It's an everyday problem that requires us to work around it and around the clock every day without having to pause even for a moment.”

World.title: Gauteng e-panic safety under scrutiny
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Gauteng e-panic button data breach matter will soon be escalated to the Premier's office.

A security flaw that exposes sensitive personal information has caused panic among users.

It seems the app has exposed victims' reports, names, and locations.

The Gauteng Legislature e‑Government Committee said the app is not safe to use.

Committee chairperson Mbali Hlophe said the breach was serious.

“It's very alarming and I must indicate that for us, we are more sensitive because of all the stuff that's taking place on the string of women that have been lost and killed and so forth. So, I mean, you can imagine what this then means, because it means the victims and the perpetrators of them would have access to this.

“We want to have a report on the access logs, so they must be able to indicate from 2024 when this was first launched to date. Two years later, how many people have had access to this? Are there any foreign people that have had access to it? If this student was able to log in, who else could have?

“There could be criminal syndicates who have been viewing all this information throughout. We just need that surety. And it's certainly what society would also want. But in addition to that, because this information has now been exposed, they do need to report it to the information regulator and also to inform the individuals that have utilized this app, especially those whose information has been compromised in line with the POPIA Act, they do need to inform them.

World.title: Unite or watch State House ambition go up in flames, Uhuru tells Opposition
World.content:
Former President Uhuru Kenyatta and Wiper Leader Kalonzo Musyoka during the funeral service of Martha Karua's father at Mugumo Primary School grounds in Kirinyaga county on October 3, 2026. [Jane Mugambi, Standard]

The clash between President William Ruto and his former boss, Uhuru Kenyatta, escalated on Saturday when the former Head of State urged the opposition to unite and sent his former deputy home.

The advice, which also served as a warning to the opposition, is that without unity, the State House dream is simply a fairy tale.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Egyptian player Malak Zaki wins U13 singles title at Egypt International Table Tennis Championship
World.content:
Egyptian player Malak Zaki secured first place at the Egypt International Junior and Cadet Table Tennis Championship in the under-13 girls’ singles, while compatriot Zeina Farouk came in second, and Youssef Taher achieved second place in the under-13 boys’ singles.

The championship resumed on Saturday at the Dr. Hassan Moustafa Hall complex in 6th of October City, running from October 2 to 5 with 250 players from 20 countries. The Egyptian Table Tennis Federation organizes international tournaments to support young talent.

World.title: Egypt responds to Ethiopia’s accusations of meddling in its political affairs
World.content:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty announced on Saturday that Egypt has not interfered in Ethiopia’s internal affairs, and stressed that respect for state sovereignty and non-interference in internal matters are fundamental principles of Egypt’s foreign policy.

Speaking to “Al-Qahera News” channel, Abdelatty explained that “Egypt has no involvement in what is happening inside Ethiopia,” and stressed that blaming external parties for internal crises is unacceptable and does not contribute to achieving desired stability.

The Foreign Minister added that Ethiopian statements linking domestic developments to external parties represent an attempt to divert attention from the situation within Ethiopia and to evade the internal crises the country is facing.

Escalating diplomatic tensions

Abdelatty’s remarks follow escalating diplomatic tensions between Cairo and Addis Ababa, after Ethiopia on Thursday declared a member of the Egyptian embassy in Addis Ababa persona non grata and gave him 48 hours to leave the country – without disclosing why.

Egypt responded with a similar measure, declaring a counselor at the Ethiopian embassy in Cairo persona non grata and giving him 48 hours to leave the country.

A well-informed Egyptian source on Saturday confirmed that Cairo refuses to be dragged into Ethiopia’s internal crisis, noting that Egyptian foreign policy is grounded in respect for state sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, and a commitment to good-neighborly relations.

The source also criticized what it described as attempts to divert attention from the “true internal motives” behind the events in Ethiopia, asserting that this will not help calm the situation in an African nation that requires the support of African Union institutions to break free from cycles of conflict.

The African Union meanwhile issued a statement calling on Egypt, Ethiopia, and Eritrea to exercise restraint, de-escalate tensions, and resolve disputes through diplomatic channels and peaceful dialogue—a move that surprised an Egyptian source, who viewed the statement as dragging Cairo into an issue described as an internal Ethiopian affair.

World.title: Egypt’s fuel prices may increase by 10-15%: Official
World.content:
The Head of the General Division for Petroleum Products at the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce (FEDCOC), Hassan Nasr, predicted a 10–15 percent increase in gasoline and diesel prices in the coming period.

During a phone-in with “Hadith al-Qahira” (Cairo Talk) on the “al-Qahira wal Nas” (Cairo and the People) channel, Nasr said that a price hike is inevitable, noting that the fuel pricing committee is scheduled to meet this October to review fuel rates.

When asked about the possibility of prices remaining unchanged, he replied, “No, the increase is definitely coming,” pointing out that rising fuel prices are to be expected given the fluctuations in global energy markets.

Discussions regarding a hike in gasoline and diesel prices have been ongoing for about two months, he explained, coinciding with a roughly 50 percent rise in global oil prices compared to the previous period, a shift that will rapidly impact Egypt.

The division head noted that the state bears a heavy financial burden due to fuel subsidies, emphasizing the substantial cost involved, while also taking citizens’ socioeconomic circumstances into account when making decisions to adjust fuel prices.

He also noted that maintaining current price levels would place a heavier burden on the state due to continued subsidies on petroleum products.

World.title: Low-pressure system and rain on Egypt until the weekend
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) forecasts that the country will be affected by a low-pressure system, leading to a drop in temperatures and an increased likelihood of rainfall in several areas.

Unsettled weather conditions are expected to persist through the end of the week.

Light rain is anticipated, accompanied by low-level cloud cover and a noticeable drop in temperatures; daytime highs are expected to range between 29-30C, while nighttime lows will fall to around 19C.

The EMA also warned of morning mist—expected between four am and eight am—on roads leading to and from the north of the country, including routes passing through Greater Cairo, the Canal cities, central Sinai, and northern Upper Egypt.

Motorists are advised to exercise caution and adhere to traffic regulations during periods of reduced visibility.

Weather Forecast for Sunday

Sunday’s weather maps indicate a likelihood of light to moderate rainfall—potentially accompanied by thunderstorms—across parts of the northern coast.

Inland areas may experience light rain, with a low probability of precipitation in Greater Cairo; caution is advised.

Sunday’s weather will be autumnal and slightly hot during the day along the northern coast, hot in Greater Cairo and northern Upper Egypt, and very hot in southern Upper Egypt.

Conditions will be mild during the early part of the night, turning cooler towards the end of the night and in the early morning.

The forecast maximum temperatures are 26C for the northern coast, 30C for Greater Cairo, 31C for northern Upper Egypt, and 37C for southern Upper Egypt.

Minimum temperatures will range between 19C-24C, depending on the region.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: US Marine in Japan arrested on suspicion of murder, local police say
World.content:
Tokyo, Japan —

A US Marine was arrested Sunday on suspicion of murder and robbery after a woman’s body was discovered in a hotel room in Japan, local police told CNN.

A 39-year-old woman was found unresponsive in her hotel room in Naha city on Okinawa island and pronounced dead at the scene early Saturday, Okinawa police said.

Police also told CNN that based on the condition of the woman’s body, she appeared to have been murdered, but did not provide any more details.

The 20-year-old Marine was stationed at Futenma Air Station, also on the island, police added.

CCTV footage reportedly showed a man, believed to be a foreign national, with a shaved head, entering the hotel room with the woman and later leaving the building with her belongings in hand, police said.

The US embassy in Tokyo said on X it was “aware that a US service member is in custody following the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa.”

“As an investigation is underway to determine the facts of the case, the United States is communicating and cooperating with the Government of Japan and local authorities,” the embassy added.

CNN has contacted the Pentagon and the US Marine Corps for comment.

The woman’s body was discovered at around 4.30 am local time on Saturday and the US Marine was arrested less than 24 hours later, at 1am local time, while walking around the city, the force added.

Police said an investigation is ongoing.

World.title: Trump, crime and corruption loom over Brazil’s presidential vote
World.content:
Millions of Brazilians will vote in a general election on Sunday that will choose the country’s president against a backdrop of corruption scandals, deep political polarization and growing voter fatigue, with two familiar political camps once again dominating the race.

Among the frontrunners are the country’s leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro, who are championing different paths for Brazil.

“It’s two competing visions of what the country should look like and what Latin America should look like,” Brian Winter, editor-in-chief of Americas Quarterly and vice president of policy at Americas Society/Council of the Americas, told CNN.

Voting is compulsory for most adults in the world’s fifth largest country, and turnout is typically among the highest in the Americas.

The choice facing Brazilians extends well beyond domestic politics and could reshape how Brazil positions itself on the global stage. The vote would determine whether the region’s largest country tilts toward a growing conservative bloc aligned with US President Donald Trump or continues Lula’s pursuit of a multipolar foreign policy.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva waves to supporters during a presidential election campaign rally in São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo, Brazil, on Aug. 16. Andre Penner/AP

Lula, 80, is seeking a fourth and likely last term. He governed Brazil from 2003 to 2010 and returned to the presidency in 2023 after a remarkable political comeback: Lula spent 580 days in prison on corruption convictions that Brazil’s Supreme Court later annulled in 2021, restoring his political rights, before he defeated then-president Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election.

Lula is neck and neck with Flávio, who is trying to carry forward the political movement built around his father. Jair Bolsonaro, now under humanitarian house arrest for health reasons, is barred from running and is serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted of attempting a coup to overturn his 2022 election loss.

Four other presidential hopefuls trail behind Lula and the younger Bolsanaro in the polls. They include centrist psychiatrist and best-selling author Augusto Cury; right-wing former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado; Renan Santos, a right-wing founder of the Movimento Brasil Livre now running under the Missão party; and Romeu Zema, the economically liberal, right-leaning former governor of the state of Minas Gerais.

If no candidate wins more than half of valid votes on Sunday, the two with the most votes advance to an October 25 runoff.

Two visions of Brazil’s place in the world

Lula has continued to champion multilateralism while distancing the country from the United States.

That shift is visible in Brazil’s official trade data. China has been Brazil’s biggest export market since 2009, but its lead has widened sharply since Trump came to power.

Lula’s relationship with Trump soured as Brazil became caught up in the US president’s tariff agenda and US policy toward organized crime in Latin America — friction that has given Lula another platform to run on: Brazil’s sovereignty.

The first flashpoint came in summer of 2025, when Trump announced tariffs on many Brazilian goods, while explicitly citing what his administration called the politically motivated prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro. The tariffs were later rolled back in November.

The former Brazilian president’s other son, Eduardo Bolsonaro, who moved to the US and lobbied the Trump administration on his father’s behalf, initially claimed credit for the pressure — a boast that later backfired on Flávio’s campaign as the tariffs hurt Brazilian businesses.

Trade tensions returned this summer when Trump imposed fresh tariffs on certain Brazilian goods, still in effect today.

Lula rejected the measures and threatened to retaliate against the US — a move he said later in September, in an interview with CNN’s Christiane Amanpour, he would hold off on while negotiations with Washington continued.

The ongoing spat with the US has resonated with swing voters who lean right and embrace nationalist ideals. “Some have joked that the most effective campaigner for Lula has been Donald Trump,” Winter said. “The tariffs and the other efforts to interfere in Brazil’s politics have, for the most part, backfired and helped Lula.”

Brazilian Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, right, handles an oversized pair of scissors, accompanied by Argentina’s President Javier Milei during the Liberal Party convention where Bolsonaro was confirmed as the party’s presidential candidate, in São Paulo, Saturday, July 25. Ettore Chiereguini/AP

Lula brought that argument onto the world stage at the United Nations General Assembly in September. “Brazil is nobody’s backyard,” he said, while accusing “some Brazilian politicians” of aligning themselves with foreign interests at odds with the country’s own — remarks widely seen as aimed at Flávio Bolsonaro.

That divide extends to other foreign relations: Two days after Lula’s UN speech, Brazilian diplomats joined representatives of several countries in walking out as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his address, amid Lula’s sharpening criticism of Israel’s conduct in Gaza.

Flávio Bolsonaro has taken a markedly different approach, cultivating ties with Netanyahu, Trump and other leaders Lula has clashed with. When Flávio launched his campaign in July, Netanyahu appeared by video to endorse him, as reported by CNN Brasil. In May, Flávio met Trump in the Oval Office to discuss organized crime, tariffs and critical minerals, then Vance and Rubio the next day.

Argentine President Javier Milei, a libertarian and longtime Bolsonaro-family ally, traveled to Brazil in July to back Flávio’s campaign. He called Lula a “convict” and the government “thieving socialists,” prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador to Buenos Aires.

This comes as Latin America’s broader political map has moved right following closely fought elections: Right-wing firebrand Abelardo de la Espriella narrowly won Colombia’s presidential election in June, and Keiko Fujimori won Peru’s runoff weeks later by roughly a tenth of a percentage point.

“A Flávio Bolsonaro victory would cement this move to the right that we’ve seen in so much of Latin America over the last two years,” Winter said, noting that many of the region’s right-leaning governments are aligned with Trump on security and drug policy.

Military police officers march during a graduation ceremony at the Center of Improvement and Training of Soldiers (CFAP) at Sulacap neighbourhood in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 25. Mauro Pimentel/AFP/Getty Images

Crime at the forefront

That alignment intersects with voters’ most immediate concern: crime.

“Security and crime have been the main issues that have led the Latin American right to win 13 of the last 16 presidential elections in Latin America,” Winter said, noting that robberies, extortion and cellphone theft still shape how Brazilians experience insecurity even as homicide rates have fallen over the past decade.

Much like his father, Flávio has made a tougher approach to crime central to his campaign, advocating for the designation of major criminal factions as terrorist organizations, new federal prisons and lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 16.

“The family’s brand has been successful above all because they’re seen as intolerant of crime,” Winter said, pointing to Jair Bolsonaro’s signature finger-gun pose.

During his May trip to Washington, Flávio urged the Trump administration to classify Brazil’s two most powerful criminal organizations as terrorist groups; the US announced days later that the designation would take effect that June.

Lula’s government opposed the move, warning that applying a terrorism framework to Brazilian criminal groups could become a pretext for foreign intervention.

Affordability and an uneasy electorate

Brazilians are also grappling with a slowing economy and persistent affordability issues. Headline indicators show low unemployment and moderating inflation, yet perceptions of household finances remain far less upbeat. “The economy is OK, but people feel like their salary doesn’t go as far,” Winter said. “They feel like their standard of living has declined, even when sometimes the official statistics tell a different story.”

These cost-of-living concerns loom over Lula’s record. The leader is associated with social mobility and poverty reduction in Brazil, which was fueled by a booming economy during his first two terms, from 2003 to 2010.

But this time, many voters are struggling to feel a similar jump. “The progress has not been nearly as widely felt as it was during his first two terms,” Winter said.

Flávio faces a different challenge: inheriting a movement still centered on his father while presenting himself as his own candidate. “Flavio Bolsonaro is not the Bolsonaro that most right-wing voters originally wanted to cast a ballot for,” Winter said. “He is clearly the most moderate member of the family, and that may give him appeal to swing voters, but it also means that he doesn’t stir enthusiasm in the same way that his father did.”
