World.title: Zadar Connected Year-Round: Winter Flights to Munich Confirmed, Expansion to Paris, London or Venice
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – Zadar is set to become connected year-round, with winter flights to Munich now confirmed, and expansion to Paris, London or Venice being actively eyed.

The new year-round air route between Zadar and Munich should be only the beginning of the further expansion of Zadar’s air connectivity with Europe, County Prefect Josip Bilaver said in response to journalists’ questions after a working meeting at the Zadar County House with Croatian Roads Management Board President Ivica Budimir and associates. O23 reports how Bilaver recalled that the possibility of introducing a year-round connection was announced about a year ago, and that operations during the winter months have now also been confirmed. He emphasised that the first reactions from citizens have been extremely positive.

“Munich is a major international air hub from which you can continue travelling practically to the entire world. Our wish is to have more such routes and we believe this should only be the beginning,” Bilaver said. He added that talks have already been held with other airlines, as well as with Croatia Airlines, and that further expansion of the year-round route offer is expected next year.

“As a county, together with the tourist boards, cities and municipalities and the tourism sector, we are ready to support such projects. Representatives of the tourism sector already several months ago expressed their readiness to participate in co-financing the routes. When we have concrete routes and proposals, we will also discuss concrete amounts,” the Prefect announced. He stressed that year-round air connectivity is important not only for tourism, but also for better connecting the residents of Zadar County with the rest of Europe and indeed the world.

“A good indicator will be precisely the Munich route, for which we expect good occupancy. After that we will see whether there is a possibility of connecting Zadar with some other major European centre. Split, for example, has a connection with Rome, but I believe there is no need for us to compete with them on the same route in the winter period. I would like Zadar to get a connection with some other major European centre such as Venice, Paris or London and thus further expand its year-round connectivity,” County Prefect Bilaver concluded.

World.title: Railway Mega-Project Would Position Croatia as Important Transit Hub
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – The recently announced and sighed railway mega-project has a high chance of positioning Croatia as an important transit hub.

The future Adriatic-Ionian railway corridor would bring many benefits, and its importance is also recognised by the European Commission. Europe must be better connected, that’s the premise that guided the signatories of the initiative “Adriatic-Ionian Railway Corridor. Transport Connectivity is deemed to be the Foundation of Development and Resilience”, and finalising the documents, the first step has been taken towards a future railway corridor that will connect Italy, Slovenia and Croatia with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania and Greece. Katarina Kusec reports for Poslovni that Croatia could benefit greatly in this story, as the new corridor would specifically link Trieste, Koper, Rijeka, Zadar, Šibenik, Split, Ploče, Bar, Durrës and Greek centres along the Adriatic-Ionian route.

better connectivity for all

The initiative was signed on Friday by Member of the European Parliament and member of the Committee on Transport and Tourism Nikolina Brnjac, Zadar County Prefect Josip Bilaver, representatives of the coastal counties, and State Secretary in the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Žarko Tušek. The aim of the initiative, it was said at the conference, is to better connect Croatia by rail with neighbouring countries and the rest of the Adriatic-Ionian region and to encourage joint investments in transport infrastructure, Hina reports.

“I don’t even need to say how important this is for the railway connection of Ploče, the Port of Ploče, with the ports of Split, Zadar, Šibenik and Rijeka. At the same time, for the first time it would enable the railway connection and financing of Istria County, Kvarner and Dalmatia with the rest of Croatia and with the European network,” said Brnjac, emphasising that the next step is a meeting with stakeholders from the governments of the countries through which the route would pass. The initiative will, she said, also influence the reconstruction of existing railway corridors as well as the construction of new lines. Tušek noted that without a modern railway there can be no strengthening of logistics capacities and position in the TEN-T network. He also highlighted the need to integrate the Istrian railways into the complete Croatian network, adding that study documentation for the Učka railway tunnel is currently being prepared. In this regard, he also announced that next year a tender will be issued for the Učka project, that is, the lowland railway project and the connection of Rijeka to that lowland railway.

financing the future adriatic-ionion corridor

Returning to the Adriatic-Ionian corridor, the question of its financing also needs to be raised. Brnjac said that 81 billion euros of EU money is currently available until the next financial framework, of which 35 billion for transport, 30 for energy and 17.5 for military mobility, and that is why this initiative was launched, working on opening the regulation of the Trans-European Transport Network.

“When the regulation tender is opened, then the Adriatic-Ionian corridor would become an integral corridor and then we can have funds for further financing,” she stressed, noting that the only known deadline is that a large conference on this topic will be organised in the European Parliament at the beginning of next year. More specifically speaking, the final conference is planned in Brussels, when the initiative will be handed over to European Commission Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism Apostolos Tzitzikostas, who, she said, has recognised the importance of this initiative.

All the signatories are aware of the importance of the said corridor for Croatia both in terms of connectivity and tourism, so HŽ Infrastruktura Management Board President Damir Lončarić emphasised that the Adriatic-Ionian railway corridor is a strategic issue for the state. “HŽ Infrastruktura is ready to make a full contribution in terms of expert and operational support for this project,” Lončarić added. The sheer importance of this massive project is further heightened by the security and geopolitical circumstances in Europe, as the war in Ukraine has shown how important alternative and reliable transport routes are for the economy, energy and military mobility. In addition, a more modern railway would enable faster freight transport, relieve road traffic and stronger inclusion of Croatian ports in the international chain.

World.title: Croatian Subjects Found to Have Forever Chemicals in Them Speak Out
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – Croatian subjects found to have so-called forever chemicals in them have spoken out, with one man from Lika having been found with the highest levels of all.

Gospić lawyer Vjekoslav Bušić, better known to the public as one of the founders and prominent representatives of the Citizens’ Initiative “Gospić is Our Home”, revealed in a report by Slobodan Mufic for Index that he has the worst findings among the ten Croatian participants in the study on the presence of PFAS compounds in the blood, also known as “forever chemicals”.

“I spoke with the other participants in the study and it turned out that the highest values of the four long-chain PFAS were found in me, even though I’ve only been living in Gospić for the last three and a half years. Interestingly, my wife is clean as a whistle. Her findings are phenomenally low, and we have practically the same lifestyle habits and eat the same food,” said Bušić.

7 from gospić, one from pula and two from knin

The study was commissioned by the Greens/EFA group in the European Parliament. The biological analyses were carried out by the Institute for Occupational Medicine of the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, and the toxicological interpretation of the results was done by Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. In addition to the seven people from Gospić, two more from Knin and one person from Pula were tested.

A total of 110 people from Croatia, Italy, Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, Spain, Denmark and Finland took part. Among the participants were also women of reproductive age, residents of areas near the chemical industry and trade union representatives, which shows that this is not a randomly selected representative sample of the European population.

All four analysed long-chain PFAS compounds (PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS and PFOS) were found in all 110 participants. However, in 27 of them, or 25 percent, the sum was above the health-based reference value set by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). Of the ten Croatian participants included in the study, six had a sum above the reference value – that is, 60 percent. The sum of the four long-chain PFAS compounds in the study was compared with the reference concentration of 6.9 nanograms per millilitre of blood. Exceeding that value does not mean that a person will develop a disease, nor does it constitute a diagnosis. It is a health-based reference value linked to EFSA’s assessment of long-term exposure to PFAS compounds and possible effects on the immune system.

Bušić emphasises that he has no reliable explanation for his findings: “It’s difficult for me to assess what the cause could be; I can only speculate. I thought it might be because in the last year and a half I have really often walked around the silos in the former PPK Velebit. Maybe the problem is inhaling those particles – I don’t know myself.”

how dangerous are these forever chemicals?

“On the other hand, toxicologists warn that heavy metals, which were also found in the illegally disposed hazardous waste in Gospić, are in the long term much more toxic and dangerous to human health than those ‘forever chemicals’. In any case, the findings are what they are, but one should not draw some final and alarming conclusions about carcinogenicity from them. It seems to me that all of this is still quite unresearched,” says Bušić, and adds:

“I still believe that I live in one of the cleanest and best-preserved areas in all of Europe. It’s important that it remains so and that the remediation of the waste in Gospić is carried out in the best possible way. And who knows, maybe I ‘picked up’ the PFAS while I was living in Zagreb.” The testing was carried out in the first days of July this year in Brussels. Bušić says that the people from Gospić received a link where they could apply online: “We didn’t even know how many people were participating in the study; in the end we realised that there were ten of us from Croatia. Apart from the seven of us from Gospić, the application of one person from Pula and two people from Knin, also members of an association, was accepted.”

The office of Croatian MEP from the Greens/EFA, Gordan Bosanac, organised the participation of ten Croatian volunteers and their trip to Belgium for blood sampling. In June, Bosanac described the project as a study of people deliberately selected from areas with possible increased exposure to PFAS, for example near landfills or industrial plants.

“Given our situation, this was a good signal that we should perhaps carry out some biomonitoring on a wider circle of people. Especially on those who live relatively close to the silos in Gospić or those who worked at the Rakitovac municipal landfill, where that hazardous waste was also brought. And it would be interesting to see the findings of the people who worked for Josip Šincek, who transported and unloaded that waste,” said Bušić.

Josip Šincek is a Varaždin entrepreneur and the main suspect in the USKOK investigation into illegal waste management; investigators suspect that through related companies he organised the import and transport of plastic, mixed and medical waste from Croatia and abroad. In Gospić, his company operated from 2021 in the former PPK Velebit complex in Bilajska Street, where tens of thousands of tonnes of illegally disposed and partly hazardous waste were later discovered.

World.title: Plenković: Without Government Measures, Inflation Would be 7%
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – PM Andrej Plenković has stated that without government measures, inflation would currently be 7% in Croatia.

The Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS) recently published that the year-on-year inflation rate measured by the consumer price index in September amounted to 4.7 percent, and 0.9 percent compared to August. Poslovni reports that it accelerated by 0.5 percentage points compared to August on an annual basis, and by 0.8 percent compared to July.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenković warned on Friday after a meeting with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder that without government measures inflation would have been 35 percent higher and would have stood at around seven percent, instead of the 4.7 percent that is the first estimate by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS) for September, Hina reports.

The DZS earlier today published that the year-on-year inflation rate measured by the consumer price index in September amounted to 4.7 percent, and 0.9 percent compared to August. It accelerated by 0.5 percentage points compared to August on an annual basis, and by 0.8 percent compared to July. Energy prices had the greatest impact on the rise in inflation, rising by 20.5 percent year-on-year in September, while food, beverages and tobacco rose by only 0.2 percent, and non-food industrial products fell by 1.4 percent.

“What is good is that other segments are going downwards; there we have succeeded with measures in mitigating the growth. Without government measures, the overall inflation rate would have been 35 percent higher – it would have been around seven percent,” Plenković said in response to journalists’ questions.

He also recalled that prices of motor fuels are lower due to the government’s weekly interventions and stated that at the moment blue diesel is 10 cents cheaper, eurosuper 20 cents cheaper, and eurodiesel as much as 32 cents cheaper than the prices that would have been formed without government measures.

He added that there is still room to mitigate the rise in fuel prices through interventions, because Croatia is in good time asking the European Commission for permission to exceptionally lower excise duties even below the minimum threshold set by European regulations. A new government intervention is expected next Monday.

World.title: Iraq’s Real Estate Bank challenges legality of Zayouna Gate project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The state-owned Real Estate Bank of Iraq issued an official statement on Saturday, October 3, 2026, challenging claims regarding the newly launched Zayouna Gate residential development in eastern Baghdad.

Addressing promotional campaigns and unit pre-sales announced by private developer Amwaj International, the bank warned that the underlying land remains protected sovereign property, stating that unauthorized residential conversions on the site constitute an infringement on public assets and a squandering of public funds.

According to a formal statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the Real Estate Bank detailed five structural and legal clarifications:

Sovereign Land Ownership: As a public state-owned banking enterprise, all real estate holdings and property assets form an indivisible part of the bank’s sovereign capital reserves. The institution stressed that no civil servant or public official, regardless of executive rank, holds legal authority to waive, transfer, or reassign ownership of the land to private parties.

Permit Scope & Build-Operate-Transfer Terms: The investment permit associated with the property was issued in 2022 to a private firm, Wahat Al-Rawan, solely for the construction of a modest three-story commercial complex—not a high-density, multi-tower residential project for freehold unit sales. Under the statutory terms of the concession, all structures were mandated to revert fully to the Real Estate Bank upon expiration of the investment lease.

Physical Status of the Site: The bank affirmed that the land plot remains vacant and free of authorized construction as of October 3, 2026. Authorities cautioned that any unauthorized excavation, perimeter fencing, or groundwork on the parcel will be treated as an illegal encroachment on state property.

No Contract Executed or Land Transferred: The Real Estate Bank stated that it has neither signed an execution contract nor handed over the physical plot. The parcel remains subject to ongoing judicial proceedings and active inquiries by the Federal Commission of Integrity regarding alleged administrative infractions and improper attempts to modify the project’s zoned use from commercial leasing to residential sale.

Active Legal Injunctions: The bank confirmed it has filed a formal appeal in the interest of the law, lodged lawsuits before competent judicial courts, and submitted dossiers to the Federal Commission of Integrity to block any illicit transfer of public assets while investigative reviews remain underway.

The bank’s public disclosure introduces significant regulatory friction into the project just 24 hours after Amwaj International hosted its launch event for the proposed twin 36-story development, highlighting heightened government scrutiny over urban land allocations and sovereign property rights in central Baghdad.

World.title: Iraq transits 2M barrels past Hormuz on VLCC in decades-first shipping shift
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC), an affiliate of the Ministry of Oil, announced on Saturday, October 3, 2026, the successful transit of two million barrels of domestic crude oil aboard a chartered Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) past the Strait of Hormuz.

The operation marks the first time in decades that the state-owned maritime shipping enterprise has conducted independent crude transportation beyond the strategic maritime chokepoint, shifting a portion of Iraq’s petroleum commercialization away from traditional delivery at Basra offshore terminals to delivery points beyond the Gulf.

Speaking to the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) in remarks reported by the 964 Network, IOTC Director General Ali Qais explained that the landmark transit was executed under the direct directives of the Prime Minister and the supervision of the Minister of Oil.

Following extensive technical negotiations with international maritime carriers, IOTC chartered a VLCC supertanker, loaded two million barrels of crude, and navigated the vessel into open international waters outside the Strait of Hormuz.

The strategic maneuver is designed to grant the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) elevated commercial flexibility, capturing premium pricing benchmarks, mitigating regional maritime transit risk premiums for buyers, and optimizing sovereign export revenues.

Qais emphasized that executive directives are actively steering the company toward the expedited procurement and outright ownership of its own fleet of dedicated crude oil supertankers.

Moving beyond spot charters, the acquisition drive seeks to restore Iraq’s sovereign blue-water tanker capabilities, modernizing IOTC’s logistics infrastructure to compete directly with national maritime shipping lines across the Gulf and broader Middle East.

World.title: Iraq studies raising oil export capacity through Turkey’s Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar met in Turkey to finalize a deal for oil flows between Iraq and Turkey through the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

Khudair stated on Saturday that the meeting was highly constructive, with discussions centered on increasing export capacity through Ceyhan and Turkish firms’ participation in Iraqi oil and gas projects.

The involvement of Turkish companies in Iraq’s energy sector is critical to the governments of both countries, particularly the Iraqi government, according to Khudair. He noted that the step helps attract competent global corporations to develop Iraq’s oil and gas resources.

The Iraqi oil minister indicated that two joint technical committees have been formed to develop oilfields and construct oil facility infrastructure.

Khudair arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Friday to discuss cooperation in the fields of oil, gas, and energy.

Khudair signed an agreement with Turkey in early August to transport Iraqi crude oil through the Iraq-Turkey pipeline to the port of Ceyhan. The deal stipulates a minimum volume of 750,000 barrels per day for a one-year period, pending the completion of a broader framework agreement.

At the time, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi declared that Iraqi and Turkish enterprises will begin executing the deal to transport crude oil to Ceyhan via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline.

Al-Zaidi said that Baghdad and Ankara were working to finalize a framework deal for the oil, electricity, and water resources sectors.

World.title: Amwaj International launches 36-story Zayouna Gate towers in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amwaj International officially launched its latest premium residential development, Zayouna Gate, during a launch ceremony hosted on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at the Mövenpick Hotel Baghdad.

The event convened business leaders, prominent real estate figures, and investment stakeholders to review the master plan of the large-scale urban project, which aims to expand modern vertical living within eastern Baghdad.

Located in the central Zayouna district, the development features two 36-story residential towers accommodating 524 apartments. Units range from two-bedroom and three-bedroom layouts starting at 163 square meters to high-end penthouses on the upper levels.

Positioned as a self-sustaining gated community, Zayouna Gate combines luxury housing with civic infrastructure, dedicated green space, and family-oriented amenities.

Key components of the development include:

An integrated private school serving community residents.

Central landscaped gardens and landscaped green spaces.

Dedicated children’s play zones and pedestrian walking and jogging circuits.

A sports club, fitness gym, and exclusive residents’ social club.

Retail promenades, commercial outlets, and day-to-day community services.

Structured underground and surface parking for residents and visitors.

Smart-home building automation, 24/7 concierge, and integrated surveillance security systems.

Amwaj International confirmed that its primary sales center began receiving prospective buyers and prospective residents on Friday, October 2, 2026, to review architectural models, unit configurations, and available inventory.

The project marks another expansion in Amwaj’s metropolitan pipeline, advancing master-planned residential communities across Baghdad’s high-density urban corridors.

World.title: Graham Arnold sets sights on Asian Cup following Iraq’s Khaleeji 27 exit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi national football team head coach Graham Arnold addressed media representatives on Saturday, October 3, 2026, affirming that the squad’s primary strategic objective is to deliver a commanding performance at the upcoming AFC Asian Cup.

Reflecting on the Lions of Mesopotamia’s campaign at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup (“Khaleeji 27”) in Jeddah, Arnold stated that despite falling short of the knockout stages, the tournament yielded crucial tactical gains, most notably expanding squad depth and integrating a new generation of domestic talent.

Speaking to journalists, Arnold voiced strong optimism regarding Iraqi football’s long-term trajectory. He highlighted that working alongside a refreshed technical staff while blooding younger prospects produced impressive individual showings.

Arnold revealed that the technical team has identified four to five newly tested players who demonstrated starting-caliber potential, adding essential tactical variety—particularly across the frontline—ahead of the continental championship.

Addressing the public scrutiny surrounding Iraq’s early elimination, Arnold defended his squad’s on-pitch record, which concluded with one victory, one draw, and a narrow defeat to tournament hosts Saudi Arabia.

The Australian tactician voiced deep frustration with the tournament’s regulations, arguing that relying on a drawing of lots rather than official FIFA world rankings to break group-stage ties was deeply disappointing.

Nevertheless, Arnold affirmed he returned to Baghdad with his head held high, satisfied that the pre-tournament objective of evaluating emerging talent succeeded.

Looking ahead, Arnold outlined the national team’s roadmap toward the AFC Asian Cup, confirming that Iraq will contest two international friendlies during the November 2026 FIFA international window.

The upcoming training camp will serve as an operational proving ground to merge the newly discovered prospects with established key starters returning from injury, cementing an expanded, competitive roster for continental competition.

World.title: Construction begins on first phase of Iraq’s Madinat Al Ward
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ORA Iraq awarded CRC Dorra the building contract for the first phase of Madinat Al Ward, paving the way for large-scale development in Iraq.

The deal was signed in the presence of Naguib Sawiris, Chairman of ORA, and Mohamed Dorra, Vice Chairman of Dorra Group, as the project progressed from ground preparation to primary construction.

CRC Dorra will begin construction after POWERCHINA has completed the earthworks and ground preparation for Phase One, according to ORA Iraq.

The deal adds another important regional contractor to the development.

CRC Dorra is the contracting arm of Dorra Group, an engineering and construction business founded in 1943 that operates in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Iraq.

Its work includes residential, commercial, office, and hotel developments, as well as design-build projects.

ORA said that the selection was based on CRC Dorra’s construction expertise and capacity to perform large-scale projects.

The commencement of construction marks a key milestone for Madinat Al Ward as ORA expands its investment and development efforts in the Iraqi market.

The company said that it continues to be dedicated to building the project as an integrated community, with the new contract advancing Phase One from site preparation to physical construction.

World.title: US Treasury approves waiver for Iranian flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Foreign Affairs Fuad Hussein announced on Friday, October 2, 2026, that U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent has agreed to exempt religious pilgrimage flights to holy sites in Iraq from secondary sanctions imposed on Iranian aviation, following intensive bilateral talks held in Washington.

The decision resolves mounting diplomatic friction surrounding the status of Najaf International Airport, granting legal clarity for passenger arrivals while shielding Iraqi aviation infrastructure from punitive measures.

In a statement shared on X (formerly Twitter) and reported by the 964 Network, Hussein outlined that discussions with Bessent encompassed the overarching trajectory of U.S.-Iraqi economic and security ties, regional fiscal stability, and the spillover impacts of American sanctions enforcement on the domestic Iraqi economy.

Hussein specifically raised the operational paralysis facing Najaf International Airport—a vital national transport hub serving millions of international religious pilgrims annually—emphasizing that economic restrictions should not impede lawful civilian travel or religious observances. Secretary Bessent acknowledged Iraq’s sovereign concerns, formally approving a targeted waiver for flights directed toward the holy shrines.

During the diplomatic session, Hussein reaffirmed Baghdad’s appreciation for past U.S. and International Coalition support in the campaign to defeat Daesh (ISIS), while reiterating the federal government’s constitutional roadmap under Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to monopolize arms under the state and maintain sole authority over war and peace.

Commending Washington’s accommodation, Hussein noted that recognizing the importance of religious freedom and facilitating pilgrim transit reflects shared values of mutual respect and tolerance, reinforcing a stable, long-term bilateral partnership between Iraq and the United States.

World.title: ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition in Baghdad.

The participating companies expressed strong ambition to expand operations and capture growing commercial opportunities in Iraq’s rapidly developing technological sector.

Hassan Abdul-Baqi Khalaf, founder of domestic startup Al-Burhan for AI Image and Video Recognition, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the venture originated from registered patents specializing in automated media verification and tamper protection against digital forgery and deepfakes.

Khalaf—a computer science student at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB) collaborating with a doctoral partner in mathematics and physics—highlighted that their platform processes requests for more than 3,000 daily active users across private corporate clients and the public.

Delivering up to 95 percent accuracy in identifying manipulated content, the company is leveraging its inaugural exhibition presence to pursue operational partnerships with federal entities, specifically the Ministry of Interior, to detect fabricated media and enhance sovereign cyber verification tools.

International infrastructure providers also underscored their entry into the domestic market. Engineer Ahmed Mustafa of Canada’s Al-Mamas, an IT and network engineering specialist, revealed that the firm is seeking to establish an operational foothold in Iraq following successful deployments in the UAE, Qatar, and Egypt.

Al-Mamas holds exclusive distribution rights across the Middle East and North Africa for precision German-manufactured timing and synchronization hardware, which is critical for maintaining ultra-low-latency architectures across telecommunications networks, industrial automation, data center facilities, and distributed artificial intelligence systems.

Highlighting regional corporate expansion, Samer Al-Yasin, sales director for Qatar-headquartered conglomerate Mannai Corporation, affirmed that Iraq represents a fertile and attractive destination for long-term tech investment.

Marking its second exhibition appearance in Baghdad, Mannai—which employs over 15,000 personnel across the Gulf—formally established its Baghdad branch three months ago and is actively preparing to launch regional offices in Erbil and Basra.

Al-Yasin emphasized that the group is deploying enterprise digital transformation, cloud integration, and systems architecture tailored for federal ministries, banking institutions, and healthcare providers, aiming to transfer its regional technical expertise to drive national modernization and support sovereign institutional revenues.

World.title: Nestle dairy whitener found unsafe, substandard by FSSAI; Nestle says product safe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A sample of NestlÃ© Indiaâs Low Fat Dairy Whitener, collected from the premises of The LaLiT in Connaught Place, has been declared âunsafe and substandardâ by a Food Analystâs laboratory, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Saturday.

The sample was collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd (The LaLiT), Connaught Place, FSSAI said. The regulator said the Food Analystâs report found the product non-compliant under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

FSSAI said a copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator and a notice was issued regarding the non-compliant product. The operator was given an opportunity to appeal against the Food Analystâs report within the prescribed period.

FSSAI also directed that the identified product be immediately prohibited from sale.

However, NestlÃ© India said the product is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements.

A NestlÃ© India spokesperson said phosphorus occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in milk-based products. The company said the FSSAI laboratory report reflects total phosphorus against the additive limit without accounting for the substantial natural phosphorus contribution from milk-based ingredients.





NestlÃ© said the product is in full compliance with prescribed limits for added phosphorus under the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, including on an âas consumedâ basis. The company said it has been engaging with the authorities through the due process established under law and has shared data on other same or similar milk-based products to demonstrate the presence of naturally occurring phosphorus.

World.title: Army soldier found hanging in a shed in Jammu; probe on
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 45-year-old

soldier was found hanging in a shed at the Sunjwan camp in

on Sunday, news agency PTI reported citing officials.

The deceased was identified as Naik Wagh Ambades, a resident of Maharashtra.

Officials said he allegedly died by suicide.

The reason behind the alleged suicide was not immediately known. Police have initiated inquest proceedings to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the death.

His body was taken to Government Medical College Hospital in Jammu for postmortem and other legal procedures.

World.title: Punjab arms network busted: AK-47, grenades seized, accused linked to foreign smugglers
World.content:
Image source: DGP Punjab Polic X account

NEW DELHI: Amritsar Rural Police have busted an illegal arms and explosives supply network, arresting one accused.In a post shared by the DGP Punjab Police on X, the police said the operation also resulted in the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, a magazine, live cartridges and two hand grenades.Preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused is allegedly linked to foreign-based smugglers and was involved in procuring illegal weapons, police said.An FIR has been registered at Gharinda police station in Amritsar under relevant sections of the Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation is underway to uncover the wider network and establish its backward and forward linkages, police said.The Punjab Police said it remained committed to maintaining strict vigil against illegal arms trafficking and organised criminal networks and taking firm action against those involved in the illegal supply chain.

World.title: ‘She will continue’: Thiruvananthapuram mayor denies BJP councillor Sreelekha resigned from post
World.content:
Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V V Rajesh on Sunday said former Kerala DGP and BJP councillor R Sreelekha would continue in office, denying that she had resigned from the Corporation.

The controversy began after a message purportedly posted by Sreelekha in a WhatsApp group of residents in her ward said she had submitted her resignation to the Mayor and would give a copy to the District Collector on October 5.

Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30 but had not sent it to the Corporation Secretary, who is authorised to accept such resignations. He had also said the letter cited personal difficulties.

On Sunday, however, Rajesh said there was no resignation letter.

"Who told you that she has given the resignation letter? She will continue and I have said it yesterday itself," he said.

When asked about the WhatsApp message attributed to Sreelekha, Rajesh did not directly address it. He instead said there was no threat to the functioning of the Corporation.

"You want the governance to take place smoothly. As all desire, the governance will go forward strongly," he said.





Mayor says Sreelekha will remain councillor

Rajesh said councillors often submit letters seeking funds for their wards or raising issues related to their functioning.

"Such a letter was given to me for the smooth operations in the ward. As she is a ruling councillor, I find that some of the matters cited in it require the party's intervention. Some have to be done by the Mayor. We will address the matters as in letters given by other councillors," he said.

He said Sreelekha would remain a councillor and complete her five-year term.

Sreelekha has not yet publicly responded to the conflicting statements over her alleged resignation.

CPM attacks BJP councillor

CPM leader and former minister V Sivankutty criticised Sreelekha and questioned her credibility.

"Nothing that Sreelekha says can be believed. Not only that, she will resort to any threat to secure position and power. This should only be viewed as a threat directed at the BJP to gain new positions," he said.

Asked whether Sreelekha was putting pressure on the BJP with a possible move towards the Congress, Sivankutty said some politicians would move wherever they saw greater benefits.

"Naturally, some go where there is greater benefit. They will move to wherever they get the maximum advantage," he said.

Sreelekha's role in BJP

The BJP took control of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation for the first time last year after securing the support of 51 councillors, including an Independent, in the 101-member civic body.

World.title: No room to roam: The cost of a crowded planet for wild animals
World.content:
Over the past fifty years, the average size of monitored wildlife populations around the world has fallen by 73 per cent, according to WWF's Living Planet Report 2024. The report names loss and degradation of habitat as the most commonly reported threat, driven mainly by how the world grows its food.

This finding raises a plain question. When animals lose the land, water and forest they depend on, what happens to them?

A shrinking home, not a vanishing one

Habitat rarely disappears all at once. It is cut into pieces by farms, roads, canals, railway lines, power lines and growing towns. Each piece may still have trees and water, but it supports fewer animals than the original whole did.

The 73 per cent figure also needs careful reading. It describes the average change across thousands of monitored populations.

It does not mean that three-quarters of the world's animals are gone, or that three-quarters of species have disappeared. What it does show is a steady thinning, and the report describes such declines as an early warning of greater risk to species and ecosystems. The pressure it describes is gradual and widespread rather than the result of a single event, which is partly why it is easy to overlook.

The report also notes that some populations have held steady or recovered where conservation has worked.





Not just about wildlife, itâs about the essential ecosystems that sustain human life

âThis is not just about wildlife, itâs about the essential ecosystems that sustain human life,â said Daudi Sumba, chief conservation officer at WWF.

What changes for an animal that loses space

The effects usually arrive in a recognisable order. Food and water become harder to find, so animals travel farther to reach them. Their routes cross fields, highways and railway tracks. Animals with large ranges, such as elephants and big cats, are affected first, because they need the most room.

Smaller populations face a slower problem. When forest patches are cut off from one another, animals cannot move between them to find mates. Over time a small, isolated group becomes more vulnerable to disease and to sudden shocks such as drought or fire. Wherever forest meets farmland or settlement, animals and people also meet more often, and not always safely.

Elephants outside the fence

India's elephants show how this plays out. The country holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants, according to the last census in 2017.

Most of them do not live inside protected areas. Government and press figures put the share outside reserves at about 80 per cent. That share matters for everything that follows. A herd that lives mostly outside reserves has no boundary between it and the land that people farm, travel across and build on.

For these herds, a journey between feeding grounds can pass through paddy fields, village lanes, rail lines and overhead power cables.

Official data tabled in Parliament in 2024 shows what that means. Over five years, the leading cause of unnatural elephant deaths was electrocution, ahead of train accidents, poaching and poisoning. Odisha, Assam, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu reported the largest numbers of electrocution deaths.

The country holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants

The government has taken some steps in response. It has identified and ground-validated about 150 elephant corridors, the routes herds use to move between forests.

The Railways and Environment ministries have also formed a standing committee to reduce deaths on tracks.

Tigers on islands of forest

Tigers tell a more hopeful story, with a warning attached. The 2022 estimate counted at least 3,682 tigers in India, a record, spread across 53 tiger reserves. These reserves are among the best protected forests in the country.

But the same assessment shows the limits of protection. Roughly a third of the reserves need stronger protection, habitat restoration or more prey for the tigers to feed on.

A few reserves in Mizoram, Nagaland and Jharkhand reported almost no tigers at all. Summaries of the report also describe many reserves as small islands of forest, joined to one another by a limited number of corridors. A reserve with a healthy tiger population can send young animals out in search of territory of their own, and many of them end up in unprotected land among farms and villages.

The record count and the weak reserves belong in the same account.

Protection works where it is applied well, and the gaps appear where it is not.

Where Kaziranga ends

Kaziranga's protection does not stop at the park boundary, and a new proposal from the Assam government has put that line under debate. The state wants to replace the default 10-km eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve with a site-specific zone of one to three kilometres. An ESZ is a regulatory buffer, declared by the environment ministry on a state's proposal.

It is not an outright ban: depending on the notification, activities in it may be prohibited, regulated or permitted, and mining is among those most strictly restricted.

The state wants to replace the default 10-km eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma says the 10-km limit applies only because Kaziranga has not yet been finally notified. He argues it brings populated areas such as Kaliabor, Doboka and Jakhalabandha under restrictions, and holds up civic projects like a proposed stadium in Bokakhat.

The state says the park's boundary and its UNESCO World Heritage status will not change, and that the 10-km zone stays in force until a new one is notified.

Some residents agree. Hundreds rallied in support of the proposal on August 18, saying the current limits get in the way of building homes and basic infrastructure.

The opposition and conservationists are not convinced. Congress state president Gaurav Gogoi led a protest at the Kohora range and alleged that the change could give legal cover to mining.

The state government rejects the charge. Conservationists such as Jadav Payeng and Kavita Ashok point to the annual floods, when rhinos, deer and elephants move to higher ground outside the park. A smaller zone, they warn, could cut off those routes.

A 2025 conservation assessment notes that a smaller zone is not necessarily a weaker one if it is designed to protect the most sensitive areas. Whether it does will depend on the final notification, which will decide whether wildlife corridors, flood escape routes and wetlands fall inside the line.

Wetlands and the quieter losses

Space does not only mean forest. Globally, freshwater species have seen the steepest declines in the WWF report, and wetlands are often among the first places to be drained or built over.

The report points to Chennai, where rapid urban growth has led to a large loss of wetland area. Wetlands shelter birds, fish and amphibians, and they also soak up floodwater for the city around them. When they go, wildlife loses a home and people lose a buffer.

The cost to people

When space runs out, people pay too. Government data tabled in Parliament showed that elephants killed 2,853 people in India over five years, with the highest toll in 2023. Many of these deaths happened in places where farms, villages and elephant routes overlap. The elephant deaths and the human deaths come from the same stretches of land, where both now depend on the same ground.

The Environment Ministry has issued guidelines on managing human-elephant conflict, and it says compensation is provided for losses.

These measures respond to the damage after it happens. They do not by themselves restore the space that animals have lost.

Where space is being rebuilt

Some efforts aim at the cause. West Bengal has begun a community programme called Gajamitra, or Friends of Elephants, in which local people take part in reducing conflict. Conservation scientists have also suggested low-cost methods for farmers, such as planting chillies, ginger or citrus around fields, which elephants tend to avoid, or placing beehives along field edges.

The WWF report also records progress in India, where it says some wildlife populations have stabilised or recovered. It credits government initiatives, careful habitat management, scientific monitoring and community involvement. At the global level, the report calls for more effective conservation along with changes in food, energy and finance systems.

What the evidence points to

The picture from India and from the world is consistent. Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks.

Their numbers thin out, they wander into danger, they come into conflict with people, or they disappear from places they once held. Where land is protected, connected and shared with the people who live beside it, some populations hold their ground or recover.

Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks. Their numbers thin out

India's own examples point in both directions: electrocutions and train deaths on one side, a record tiger count and recovering populations on the other. The difference lies largely in whether land is protected and linked together, and whether the people who live beside wildlife are part of the plan.

The question on World Wildlife Day is how much room is left for wildlife, and who decides what happens to it.

World.title: 'Who is safe?' Delhi minister Sirsa attacks Punjab govt after Mad Sandhu killing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social media influencer Mad Sandhu, alleging that the stateâs law and order was in the hands of the âmafiaâ.

Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Police said the attackers opened fire before fleeing the spot.

Sandhu suffered two gunshot wounds and was rushed to a private hospital in critical condition, where he later died during treatment. An eyewitness said around two to three rounds were fired and that Sandhu was shot at close range.

Reacting to the killing, Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in Punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.

âThere is no law and order in Punjab. The law and order situation in Punjab is in the hands of the mafia. In Punjab, you receive only one piece of information every day,â Sirsa told ANI.

âOtherwise, the police do not even register an FIR. If they are drug dealers, they are going around killing people. If they are mafia members, they are killing people. If there are gangsters, they are killing people. Social media influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead and if even the Sarpanch of a village is not safe, and a former Sarpanch is not safe, then who is safe?â

Sirsa further alleged that extortion gangs, mafia groups and the drug mafia were operating in Punjab.





âDuring the tenure of the Aam Aadmi Party, gangs involved in extortion, the mafia, and the drug mafia are operating in Punjab. There is also a school mafia operating, where even if you raise your voice against problems in schools, you will be thrown out of the party,â he added.

Who was Mad Sandhu?

Madhusudan Sandhu was a makeup artist and social media influencer who regularly appeared on podcasts and digital platforms, where he spoke about make-up artistry, the film industry and gender issues.

His content and fashion choices had also attracted criticism and abuse on social media.

Sandhu had around 2.26 lakh followers on Instagram and had acted in the Punjabi film *Oye Bhole Oye*. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had objected to his social media content and clothing, saying his videos could have a negative impact on young people.

Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka also criticised the AAP government over the killing and demanded Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mannâs resignation, alleging that the government had failed to protect people.

Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them publicly on social media. He questioned why the threats had not been taken seriously and demanded an early arrest and a thorough investigation into who was behind the killing and why Sandhu had been threatened.

World.title: ‘If you manufacture a dictator, we will bury it’: Uddhav, Raj launch joint protest against CEC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a joint protest march in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with participants demanding the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra.

Addressing the gathering after the march, Uddhav Thackeray accused the government of attempting to create a dictatorship under the slogan of âMake in Indiaâ.

âI think you will also remember that when Modi ji first became Prime Minister, he gave the slogan, âMake in India.â Remember? We accept that. But if, under âMake in India,â you are also going to manufacture a dictator in our country, then we have gathered here today to bury that dictatorship and put an end to it.

Everything else under Make in India is fine. But if, in the name of Make in India, you are going to create a dictatorship, then consider that we have buried your dictatorship.

..â

Speaking ahead of the protest, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said the demonstration was a collective response to what he alleged were attempts to undermine democratic institutions, electoral processes and the constitutional rights of citizens.





âThis protest is against the Hitler-rule prevailing in the country, hijacking elections, keeping the Election Commission and the Supreme Court in one's pocket, running a dictatorship, stealing votes, stealing elections, and poaching MPs and MLAs. This is a revolt against all that, much like the one in 1857,â he told reporters.

Thackeray questioned the appointment process of Election Commissioners.

âI have a question mark over the appointment of the Election Commissioners.

The Election Commission should be appointed through an election. Earlier, there was a committee comprising the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. They (the central government) removed the Chief Justice from this committee. In place of the Chief Justice, they appointed a minister chosen by the Prime Minister.

That minister is Amit Shah. There are hearings after hearings in the courts, but there is no accountability.â

Thackeray also questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was appointed and alleged that powers related to citizenship rights were being exercised through the Election Commission.

âThe first question is: How was Gyanesh Kumar appointed? Does the Home Ministry have the power to cancel a person's citizenship rights? They are using that power through Gyanesh Kumar, and that is why we do not want Gyanesh Kumar.

Earlier, it was 'India Against Corruption', and now it is 'India Against Vote Chors'... The BJP does not know how to run a government... The way you are running the government is not governance; it is revenge.

..â

The march, dubbed the Virat Garjana Morcha (Grand Roar March), began at Metro Cinema and proceeded towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters in south Mumbai. State leaders of the Congress and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) also participated in the protest.

The protesters demanded the removal or resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.

Party flags were not allowed during the march, with participants and supporters asked to carry only the national tricolour.

World.title: Keralam government to begin talks on starting an academy for calligraphy
World.content:
The Keralam Government will take active measures to help popularise the art of calligraphy in the State. Speaking at the inauguration of the fourth edition of the International Calligraphy Festival of Keralam 2026 in Kochi, Chief Minister V D Satheesan said that talks would begin to set up an academy dedicated exclusively to calligraphy. Collaborating with renowned calligraphy artist and founder of the festival, Narayana Bhattathiri, the proposed academy would be a centre for learning and preservation of the art form.

The three-day festival, which began on October 2 at Durbar Hall Art Gallery and Rajendra Maidan, includes the works of over 24 Indian artists and three international artists – from Sri Lanka, Bhutan and France. The gallery space at Durbar Hall is alive with letters in all forms and shapes – the familiar rounded scripts of southern Indian languages, the angular style of Devnagiri, the curvilinear script of Bangla, a few ancient Indian scripts and English, rendered in different styles.

“One does not need to understand or know the language to enjoy the beauty of calligraphy,” says Bhattathiri, who is also the honorary director of the World Calligraphy Association. “The idea is to open the world of calligraphy to people and bring them closer to the art of writing,” he adds.

One of the only international calligraphy festivals in India, the event aims to take calligraphy out of galleries and into the mainstream. “I did calligraphy on an umbrella. That way, it reaches places,” he says. A calli-fashion event, part of the festival, showcased calligraphy on clothes. “It is a way of keeping calligraphy alive,” he adds.

After over four decades of calligraphy practice, the veteran says how it always brings a certain peace to him. “It has a deeply meditative quality. It helps cut out noise – both internal and external. It brings a sense of calm. It influences the mind,” the artist says. He opened a gallery, Ka Cha Ta Tha Pa in Thiruvananthapuram, one of only such galleries in the State, to showcase Malayalam calligraphy.

The festival, which concludes on October 5, includes workshops, art performances and live demos as well.

World.title: Why scientists are rethinking the chemical ‘arms race’ against fungi
World.content:
For a long time, fungal infections have meant itchy skin, discoloured nails and sometimes hair loss.

These symptoms are collectively called dermatophytosis and are caused by a group of fungi called dermatophytes.

‘’Unfortunately, immunocompromised patients can get lesions all over their body. The itchiness and the lesions can get so severe that people even get suicidal thoughts,” said Shivaprakash Rudramurthy, professor of medical mycology at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.

Global warming

Dermatophytes are molds: fungi that grow in long strands. The other common category of fungi is yeast, which are single, oval-shaped cells. Among the yeasts, Candida auris is rapidly emerging as a multidrug resistant pathogen in ICU facilities. It enters the blood stream and causes severe infections, most of which are untreatable by the available antifungals. According to Prof. Rudramurthy, those infected suffer a 30-40% mortality rate.

C. auris has become a menace only in the last two decades. The first report was in 2009 in Japan. Several other fungal species have become more pathogenic only in recent times. The cause of this rise remains unresolved but scientists and medical doctors have some ideas.

Fungi grow best in damp places below 30° C, so they can grow on our skin, especially in moist areas of the body, like armpits and the genital area. However, bloodstream infections in humans were rare because they could not survive in the body’s 37° C temperature.

“Fungal infections are common in cold-blooded animals with lower body temperatures,” Sriram Varahan, a mycologist at CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad, said.

“But global warming puts a selective pressure on fungi such that only the more heat-tolerant ones survive. These ones can survive inside our bodies too, if they gain access to it. This is called the fungal infection — mammalian selection hypothesis.”

Clinical samples

Today, roughly 20% of infections reported in hospitals are fungal in nature — yet most hospitals in India lack the capabilities and infrastructure to identify fungal pathogens, Prof Rudramurthy said.

This prompted PGIMER to begin storing fungal pathogens some 25 years ago. Today, the institute holds a stock of 15,000 clinical fungal isolates across India and helps other medical centres and clinicians identify and culture them for study, free of cost.

The C. auris isolates from PGIMER’s repository have come handy for Kaustuv Sanyal and his research associate Aswathy Narayanan, both at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, Bengaluru. They study how fungal pathogens divide and their genomes evolve.

In a recent study published in Nature Communications, they characterised the clinical isolates of C. auris found across India. Their focus was the pathogen’s ability to resist antifungals. They were able to establish their findings in patient samples and go beyond earlier studies in model systems.

“More than 90% clinical isolates of C. auris are resistant to common azole-based antifungals, such as fluconazole,” Prof. Sanyal said. Some “30% of them are resistant to another class of antifungals called the polyenes. They mostly respond to a different class of antifungals called the echinocandins.”

A drug may not work on a pathogen for many reasons, including the drug’s target becoming mutated or the drug’s effect being negated by the pathogen’s own biomolecules. Dr. Narayanan and her collaborators at the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram, found significant changes in drug-resistant C. auris genomes that could explain why Indian clinical isolates were able to resist azoles and echinocandins.

Susceptibility tests

A fungal cell has two protective layers surrounding it. The outermost is the cell wall and the inner one is the cell membrane. Azole and polyene antifungals target a fat called ergosterol that is enriched in the cell membrane. Echinocandins target the cell wall.

“When we grow C. auris isolates in the presence of fluconazole, the pathogen fights back by making extra copies of the Erg 11 gene. This in turn helps in higher production of ergosterol, thereby eliminating the effect of the azole drug,” Dr Narayanan said.

The study found parts in the C. auris genome where additional copies of the Erg11 gene were present.

With echinocandin drugs such as caspofungin, the team found mutations in the Fks1 gene that allowed the pathogen to resist the drug’s action. The team also found genetic changes promoting higher tolerance of echinocandins.

“Fks1 mutations can enable C. auris to survive even caspofungin doses up to 16 ug/ml. That means a patient with such a pathogen will need the drug at a concentration higher than 16 ug/ml,” Prof. Sanyal said. “Today, clinicians would not know that because they test the pathogen’s ability to survive only until 2 µg/mL of caspofungin — as defined by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and followed globally.”

The logical thing for clinicians would be to look for mutations like in the Fks1 gene and decide the limits for tests to decide the antifungal dose for patients. But due to associated costs, a more practical way is to increase the limits of susceptibility tests for caspofungin to higher than 16 ug/ml, Prof. Sanyal added.

C. auris, without any specific gene mutation or gene duplication, still responds to high concentrations of caspofungin in unexpected ways. While the pathogen dies at lower concentrations of the drug, at exceptionally high ones, it survives. This is paradoxical.

“This is because caspofungin at high doses activates compensatory pathways in the fungus,” Prof. Sanyal explained. “The fungus starts producing chitin, the raw material of the fungal cell wall, in large quantities. Any damage that caspofungin brings about on the cell wall is compensated by the extra chitin production. And thus the cell wall remains intact despite the antifungal.”

Such examples of paradoxical growth are called the Eagle effect, named for the U.S. pathologist Harry Eagle.

Beyond the arms race

The studies underline the importance of clinicians conducting more nuanced susceptibility tests to decide the antifungal doses. They show that fungi are protected from antifungals by genetic mutations as well as by making more copies of protective genes.

Prof. Sanyal also stressed on the need for a combination of therapies to target cellular compensatory pathways, keeping the major antifungals effective against drug-tolerant species.

However, Dr. Varahan said he believed scientists and doctors need to think of gentler alternatives: “When we target [a molecule] without which an organism cannot live at all, evolution ensures that its population survives with a changed molecule. So instead of participating in an arms race, it is perhaps better to target the less critical molecular pathways, inhibition of which will allow the pathogen to still survive but not cause a disease.”

It seems the idea of dousing fungal pathogens with antifungals is nearing its end. The next-generation of antifungals will need more planning.

Somdatta Karak heads science communication at CSIR-CCMB.

World.title: AAP MLA cries foul over teacher shortage in Punjab; is suspended by party
World.content:
While Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann boasted that his government, in just four-and-a-half years, had delivered more development work than two decades of Congress and Akali rule, citing the transformation of government schools and Punjab’s rise to the top position in education, the same day, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana raised questions over these claims, though he is not the first party legislator to do so.

On Saturday (October 3, 2026), Maiserkhana, the AAP MLA from Maur constituency in Bathinda, Punjab, alleged that, despite his repeated requests, the State government had failed to address the shortage of teachers in certain government schools in his constituency.

The AAP suspended the primary membership of Mr. Maiserkhana with immediate effect over what it termed “anti-party activities and indiscipline”. The party said Mr. Maiserkhana had attempted to defame the party by making false statements regarding the functioning of a government school.

Disputing his party’s claims about achievements in school education under the AAP government in Punjab, the MLA alleged that the reality on the ground was quite different by expressing his concerns through a social media platform.

Mr. Maiserkhana, whose son is enrolled in a School of Eminence in Bathinda district and daughter at a government primary school, said that he had taken to social media after growing frustrated at being unable to get his grievance over the shortage of teachers resolved.

A visibly emotional Maiserkhana in his video said, “I am going live out of sadness. I kept demanding that teacher posts be filled, but it hasn’t happened yet... I have always worked for the betterment of the party... yet now they are sidelining and ignoring me, pushing me out of everything. Why? Simply because I am fighting for the schools, for my own children, and for the children of everyone who sends their kids to government schools.”

The MLA claimed that among the ruling party MLAs, he is the only MLA whose children study in a government school, and alleged that he knows he will be denied a ticket to contest the upcoming polls, but he will still continue to fight for people. He added that despite taking the grievance to the party high command, there was no resolution.

Notably, this is not the first instance of an AAP MLA raising questions about the AAP’s much-touted Schools of Eminence. In 2023, ahead of AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal’s visit to inaugurate Punjab’s first School of Eminence in Amritsar, the former IPS officer and Amritsar MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh had pointed out that the school in question was only ‘renovated’ and that it was made a smart school earlier by the previous governments. Later, in June 2025, Mr. Pratap Singh was suspended from the party for five years and accused of allegedly indulging in anti-party activities. Mr. Pratap Singh had remained critical of the government on various issues.

The AAP, meanwhile, dismissed the MLA’s charges regarding the School of Eminence at Ram Nagar in Bathinda. The party’s statement said, “The claim was completely contrary to the official record issued by the school principal on September 29, 2026. According to the record, the school has 30 sanctioned teaching posts, of which 25 are currently filled. The staff posted at the school includes one principal, seven lecturers, 15 teachers from the Master Cadre and two Computer Science teachers. The school currently has 580 students studying from Classes 6 to 12 across 19 sections.”

The opposition took the opportunity to hit out strongly at the AAP government. A senior Shiromani Akali Dal leader, Daljit Singh Cheema, said the hollowness of the government’s much-publicised ‘Sikhya Kranti’ has been exposed. “Mr. Maiserkhana’s questioning teacher shortages and the neglect of government schools and his suspension after raising these concerns speaks volumes,” he said.

World.title: How accessible is your apartment community?
World.content:
How accessible is your apartment community? That’s the central idea of this short film Block A For Accessibility, released with a private screening at PVR Satyam Cinemas on September 25. The 20-minute CBFC-certified film by YWTC (Yes, We Too Can!!!) Charitable Trust, in collaboration with Fiserv as CSR partner and United Way Mumbai as the CSR NGO partner, is a story of care, community, and design.

The film revolves around Natarajan, an ageing father, who after starting to use a wheelchair keeps himself isolated from the vibrant life of his apartment complex because he does not want to trouble his son.

A sudden accident at the building’s stairs becomes a turning point for the entire community.

The film follows the internal realisation of the association secretary and the decisive action of the builder.

Natarajan’s character is played by a deaf person, Ravi Kumar. Voice was given by Umapathy, a wheelchair user. Most of the cast and crew are persons with disabilities, including the director. The film has sign language interpretations along with subtitles, and audio description for those with vision-related challenges.

The film addresses a universal civic necessity: accessible housing that accommodates an ageing population and ensures people of all abilities live with independence and dignity.

For a screening of “Block A For Accessibility” at your apartment complex/workplace, write to yeswetoocan@gmail.com

Handrails: a silver jubilee gift

Not many residents at Raheja Regency, a 25-year-old apartment community in MRC Nagar, likely know the two people who were instrumental in getting handrails installed at strategic points in the society recently. Nonagenarian Arjun Krishna and Vasantha Arjun were too modest to talk about this accessibility feature and agreed to give their names after much prodding by this journalist.

One of the earliest residents of this gated community, when the couple were part of the resident association, they got handrails fixed at most of the blocks some 20 years ago. These have been patronised by all, especially the senior citizens. But the community could do with some more, and the couple themselves have experienced the practical difficulty in not having them.

“One of the ladies has even fallen not having a railing to hold on to it,” says Vasantha. The couple sponsored the entire cost of installing the handrailings at some new locations as a gift to the community that has been their home for the last 25 years (the couple marked 25 years of staying in the community this June).

Pool lift: for easy swimming

Madhavi Latha Prathigudupu’s day is not complete without accessing the swimming pool at her gated community in Arumbakkam. Since 2022, what makes this common amenity accessible for this para-athlete is the pool lift that was incorporated.

The swimming champion cannot do without being in the pool and her late father had to help her get into the waters. She convinced Triumph Apartments, a community with 108 flats where she owns one, to make the pool accessible. “Before installing the pool lift, we had a demonstration done by the manufacturer with the committee members to get their approval,” says Madhavi, president of YWTC Charitable Trust.

Today, she goes independently into the pool (she controls the lift pool through a remote) and most importantly has raised the importance of having inclusive amenities at gated communities not just for those with disabilities but even for use by the elderly. There was no ramp when she moved in to the community; the association did not just construct one for access to her block but made the improvisation at other towers as well.

Accessibility standards of the National Building Code insist on a barrier-free built environment and all common facilities accessible to all people. “It’s your right, so ask the builder for such accessible features before investing in a flat,” she adds.

Sensory park: designed by special parents

In August, the Community Living Association for Parents of Special Citizens (CLAPS) celebrated four years of moving into an inclusively designed campus at Tiruvallur, near Poondi reservoir.

A group of 50 parents of young adults with special needs got together to conceptualise such a model in a 8.5 acre residential campus that comes with a host of universally designed and accessible amenities.

Latha Krishnan and Vaijayanthi Srinivasan, both special parents, say the activity centre, swimming pool, and sensory park are the most popular among the young adults aged 20 and above.

Unlike the apartment communities where they faced many challenges, here everything is customised in keeping with the different needs of the children, a majority are on the spectrum, some with Down’s Syndrome and intellectually disability.

The sensory park, for instance, is a hit for those with autism and has equipment with different textures. The activity centre allows them choose programmes as per one’s moods and likes. To oversee the children, there are many external professionals, including the warden, supervisor and activity head.

World.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met, says reports
World.content:
The Strait of ​Hormuz will not reopen until ‌seven Iranian conditions set ​out in ⁠a June interim agreement with the U.S. are met, ‌Nournews reported Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad ‌Baqer Qalibaf as ‌saying ⁠on Sunday (October 4, 2026), a few ⁠days after Tehran received Washington's reply to its diplomatic ​proposal.

“The Americans, ‌who say something different in the media, have recently put forward ‌proposals through a ​mediator. But they must understand that the ⁠period of dragging out the process ‌and dictating one-sided demands is over," Mr. Qalibaf was quoted as saying.

"The position of the Islamic Republic of ‌Iran is completely clear and ​firm, and the Strait of Hormuz ⁠will not be opened until ⁠our seven conditions, based on the ‌Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met," he said.

World.title: Keralam’s former Minister Muneer seeks comprehensive probe into Malaysian engineer’s death in 2006
World.content:
Former Minister for Public Works in Keralam and senior Indian Union Muslim League leader M.K. Muneer has sought a comprehensive probe into the circumstances leading to the reported death by suicide of Lee See Been, the project engineer of a Indo-Malaysian joint venture involved in the World Bank-aided development of MC Road from Angamaly to Thiruvananthapuram, in November 2006.

Gyanesh Kumar, the current Chief Election Commissioner, was the Secretary, Public Works, when the incident happened. Mr. Muneer, who held the Public Works portfolio between 2001 and 2006, told the media here on Sunday (October 4, 2026) that no proper inquiry had been conducted into the death of engineer Been so far. Though there were reports about a note, it lacked clarity. Mr. Muneer’s term as Minister ended in early 2006.

Mr. Muneer said that though the Left Democratic Front government, which came to power thereafter, had conducted an inquiry by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau into the alleged irregularities related to the road works under the Kerala State Transport Project, Mr. Kumar was exonerated by the court. Mr. Kumar was later transferred to New Delhi.

Mr. Muneer’s remarks come close on the heels of the United Democratic Front government seeking a preliminary inquiry into the accusation that the alleged efforts to extort bribes from PATI-BEL consortium, the Indo-Malayasian construction firm involved in the project, had caused inordinate delays and cost escalations. This allegedly resulted in significant losses to the exchequer and also the death by suicide of Been.

(Those who are in distress may seek help by dialling the Tele-MANAS helpline 14416.)

World.title: Iran's Foreign Minister tells U.S. there is no military solution to their conflict
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday (October 4, 2026) that there was no military solution to his country's conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the U.S. and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Mr. Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.

"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding that "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at providing a framework for a permanent resolution, but the deal collapsed, largely due to disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has sought to impose control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, and has attacked vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.

Iranian and U.S. officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.

Mr. Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.

The United States has not struck Iran since September 1.

U.S. media outlet Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday (October 2) to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Ruling TVK is obsessed with purchasing MLAs: M.K. Stalin tells voters
World.content:
DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Sunday (September 4, 2026) appealed to voters in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies to vote for the DMK candidates, alleging the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was more interested in "purchasing" MLAs to protect its government.

In a speech posted on his social media page, Mr. Stalin alleged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was not concerned about pressing issues but was interested in constructing a new Secretariat on the advice of an astrologer.

"He is least bothered about the protests by fishermen and farmers. Instead, he will visit London to watch a car race. When murders have become the order of the day, he will be busy releasing reels about the 'Singapen' force," Mr. Stalin said.

He appealed to voters who had "chased away" the ruling party's candidates when they came seeking votes to defeat them in the byelections.

"You should disappoint the TVK, which seeks to cheat people by releasing reels and projecting false claims as achievements. There will be no betrayal of voters in the future only if you teach a lesson to the ruling party and its candidate who defected to it," he said.

Mr. Stalin asked voters to consider why a byelection had become necessary in their constituencies barely four months after the Assembly election.

"While MLAs in other constituencies are studying the requirements of their constituencies, the MLAs whom you thought would be loyal to you have come back to seek your votes. Is there any justification for their act? Do they have even an iota of concern for your welfare?" he asked.

He alleged the MLAs from the two constituencies had "sold the self-respect" of the voters by "selling themselves" in the "horse race" of the ruling party.

"Are you ready to believe their lies and false stories?" he asked.
